# AI agents and skills

Use this page to install and launch coding agents, keep their API keys safe and share skills between them.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig ai list
bxrig ai default claude-code --yes
bxrig ai launch                   # the default agent, with its keys loaded
```

![The Agents page of the Control Center](/assets/screenshots/ai-agents.webp)

## Install and launch agents

BxRig installs and launches coding agents (Pi, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kilo Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor Agent, Amp, Crush, Goose, Kiro, Qwen Code, Grok Build) and orchestrators.

```bash
bxrig ai list
bxrig ai default claude-code --yes
bxrig ai launch                   # the default agent, with its keys loaded
bxrig ai shell                    # a pull-down terminal (Super+`)
bxrig ai session start            # a persistent tmux session
```

Give any of them BxRig's own tools, and see what leaves your machine: [MCP and privacy](/ai/mcp-and-privacy/index.html).

## Keep API keys safe

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["bxrig secrets set"] --> B["Desktop keyring"]
  B --> C["bxrig secrets run"]
  B --> D["bxrig ai launch"]
  C --> E["Your command"]
  D --> F["Your agent"]
```

The diagram shows how a key goes from you into the keyring and only then into the program that needs it.

Keys are stored in your desktop keyring (BxRig installs one if you have none), never in files or shell history.

```bash
bxrig secrets set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY     # typed hidden
bxrig secrets list
bxrig secrets run ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -- some-command
```

Each key is marked as an AI key or another kind, and agents declare which providers they accept (OpenCode can use several). Exporting keys globally is opt-in. Move keys between machines with `bxrig secrets export` (encrypted with age).

## Use skills with every agent

**Skills** are small `SKILL.md` files that teach an agent how to do one thing well. BxRig stores them once in `~/.agents/skills` and links each one into the skills folder of every agent you have (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode). A folder of your own with the same name is never replaced.

```bash
bxrig skills install bxrig boxlang matchbox --yes
bxrig skills status
bxrig skills search matchbox            # the skills.boxlang.io hub
bxrig skills update --yes
```

The hub ([skills.boxlang.io](https://skills.boxlang.io)) audits every skill. A skill that failed its audit is refused. Skills are optional in the wizard (AI page).

## Go local

BxRig runs models on your machine with llama.cpp, picked for your hardware, with OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs on `127.0.0.1:8089`. Start with `bxrig ai setup`. See [Local AI](/ai/local-ai/index.html).

Your own agents, built with bx-agents (Boxy and the rest), run in the background with `bxrig ai agents`. See [BoxLang agents](/ai/boxlang-agents/index.html).

## Advanced

### Skills BxRig knows

|    Name    |                         What it is                         |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `bxrig`    | Five skills about BxRig itself, shipped inside the program |
| `boxlang`  | BoxLang language fundamentals, from the hub                |
| `matchbox` | The MatchBox runtime, from the hub                         |

Install one from the hub by its path:

```bash
bxrig skills install ortus-boxlang/skills/boxlang-developer~language-fundamentals --yes
```

Next: [Local AI](/ai/local-ai/index.html) · [BoxLang agents](/ai/boxlang-agents/index.html) · [MCP and privacy](/ai/mcp-and-privacy/index.html)

# Apps and web apps

Use this page to find, install, remove and update software without knowing what a package is.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig tui apps                  # the Apps manager
bxrig install vlc heidisql --yes
bxrig web install google --yes  # Docs, Drive, Gmail, Calendar... as app windows
```

![The Apps page of the Control Center](/assets/screenshots/control-center-apps.webp)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Search or pick"] --> B["Plan in plain words"]
  B --> C{"You press y"}
  C -->|"yes"| D["Install from repo, AUR or vendor"]
  C -->|"no"| E["Nothing changes"]
```

The diagram shows that every change in the Apps manager shows its plan first and waits for you.

## Use the Apps manager

`bxrig tui apps` (or the **Apps** page, second in the Control Center, or `bxrig launchers on` for a menu entry) is where you find, install, remove and update software.

     Installed (24)   Discover   Updates (3)
     › Search your apps
     ╭──────────────────────────────╮ ╭────────────────────────────╮
     │▸ Firefox     extra   272 MB  │ │ [icon]  Firefox            │
     │  Obsidian    AUR     200 MB  │ │         extra   133.0-1    │
     │  ...                         │ │ Fast, private web browser  │
     ╰──────────────────────────────╯ │  o open   x remove   n info│
                                      ╰────────────────────────────╯

**Three tabs.** Left and Right (or `1`, `2`, `3` from the list) switch between them.

* **Installed** lists the apps that have a launcher, one row per package, with where each came from in plain words (a repository like `extra`, `AUR` for community build scripts, `Flatpak`, or `built here` for anything installed from outside the repositories), its size, and the date. `s` sorts by name, size or source, `f` filters by source.
* **Discover** shows the catalog by category when the search box is empty (`Enter` opens a category, `Escape` goes back). Type to search: catalog apps show at once (so `email` finds Thunderbird, Gmail, HEY and friends, also by what an app does), then the repositories and the AUR follow in the background after you pause typing. A check mark shows what you already have.
* **Updates** counts what is waiting (from `checkupdates`, plus `yay` or `paru` for the AUR) and has one button, **Update all** , which runs `bxrig system update`. Arch is updated all together on purpose; updating one package alone can break the others.

**The search box is always there.** Typing searches, so there is nothing to learn. `Down` or `Enter` moves into the list, where the keys are actions: `i` install, `x` remove, `o` open, `n` info, `u` update all, `/` or `Escape` back to the search box, `q` quit. A click works everywhere.

**Every change shows a plan first** , in plain words, and waits for `y`. Removing an app says what else goes with it (unused dependencies) or that something else needs it, and that your files and settings in your home folder stay. Installing from the AUR says so before anything runs.

## Install from the catalog

BxRig knows about 290 apps and web apps in groups (development, terminal, AI, infrastructure, network, system, desktop, everyday, web apps, media, gaming). Each is **default** (installed by the wizard's Basic mode) or **optional** . Sources: official packages first (`pacman`), then the AUR (`yay`), PKGBUILDs pinned to a commit, vendor installers and web apps.

```bash
bxrig catalog list --group media
bxrig catalog show strata
bxrig install vlc heidisql --yes
bxrig profile-install jvm --yes        # a ready-made set
```

In the wizard, **Basic** installs the recommended set; **Customize** lets you tick apps per category. Some entries only apply to one desktop (they say so).

## Add web apps

A web app is a frameless window with its own launcher entry.

```bash
bxrig web add Notion https://notion.so --yes
bxrig web list
bxrig web install google --yes         # Docs, Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube...
bxrig web install microsoft --yes      # Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, OneDrive
bxrig web install apple --yes          # iCloud, Pages, Numbers, Keynote, Apple Music, Apple TV
```

The same three are in the wizard (Apps page) and the control center (Web apps).

## Set your defaults

```bash
bxrig default show
bxrig default browser brave --yes
bxrig default terminal ghostty --yes
bxrig default filemanager strata --yes
```

## View images and PDFs

A plain install gives you one app for each job, the way Preview does on a Mac.

|               You want to                |                                                            Use                                                             |            Mac             |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| View, crop, rotate and annotate an image | **Gwenview** (the default for image files; HEIC and AVIF open through the image format plugins that are installed with it) | Preview                    |
| Read a PDF                               | **Okular** (the default for PDF files)                                                                                     | Preview                    |
| Sign a PDF or fill it in                 | **Signed** (from the AUR)                                                                                                  | Preview (sign PDF)         |
| Annotate a screenshot                    | **Satty**                                                                                                                  | Preview markup, Screenshot |

The wizard sets Gwenview and Okular as the default apps for those file types after it installs them (Basic mode, or when you tick them in Customize). To change it later, use your desktop's file type settings or `xdg-mime default`. imv stays in the catalog as an optional lightweight viewer. Quick Look (the space bar preview) is still Kiview.

## Files and sharing

The default file manager is **Strata** ; Dolphin is the alternative (`bxrig dolphin doctor` checks it works outside Plasma). `bxrig strata integrations` adds LocalSend and KDE Connect to Strata's *Send to* menu. `bxrig quicklook PATH` previews a file with Kiview.

## More tools

|           Area           |                                                                                Command                                                                                 |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Dictation                | `bxrig dictation setup superwhisper\|voxtype --yes`                                                                                                                    |
| Databases                | `bxrig db list\|start ENGINE\|stop\|status\|logs` (see [Databases and virtual machines](/build/databases-and-vms/index.html); HeidiSQL and DBeaver are in the catalog) |
| Cloud storage as folders | `bxrig cloud remotes\|configure\|mount NAME\|status` (rclone 1.74 and later has its own web GUI: `rclone gui`)                                                         |
| VPN                      | `bxrig vpn list\|connect NAME\|disconnect\|locations NAME` (one list: saved network profiles, NordVPN, NordLayer, Tailscale, Mullvad), `bxrig vpn nordvpn setup`       |
| Containers               | `bxrig containers doctor\|socket enable\|docker-compat\|list\|start\|stop\|restart\|logs`                                                                              |
| Editor                   | `bxrig editor lazyvim`                                                                                                                                                 |
| GPU drivers              | `bxrig gpu doctor`                                                                                                                                                     |

## Advanced

### Password managers

The Security category of the catalog has these, and the wizard's "Password manager" question offers the same list (Bitwarden stays the default):

|                       App                        |         Source          |                              Notes                              |
|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Bitwarden, KeePassXC                             | official repo (`extra`) | desktop apps                                                    |
| 1Password, Proton Pass, Enpass, NordPass, Keeper | AUR                     | desktop apps; NordPass is a repack of the vendor's Snap release |
| Bitwarden CLI, pass, gopass                      | official repo (`extra`) | terminal tools, no window                                       |

Web only: use the browser extension. Dashlane has no Linux desktop app (only a browser extension) and LastPass has only its browser extension and an unofficial command line tool, so neither is in the catalog. Install their extension from your browser's add-on store.

Checked on 2026-11-15 against the Arch package search and the AUR (package exists and is not flagged out of date), not by installing each one. Proton Pass and Enpass also exist on Flathub, but the catalog has no Flatpak source, so they use the AUR packages.

### Manager details

The text you typed stays when you move between Installed and Discover; Updates has its own filter.

**Pictures.** The preview shows the app's icon and, for installed apps that have them, screenshots, through the same cache as the other pages ([Pictures in the terminal](/maintain/images/index.html)). With no picture you get a coloured tile with the app's first letter. Nothing waits for a picture.

**On a small terminal** (80 columns by 24 rows) the preview moves under the list. Below about 90 columns the Control Center also collapses its sidebar by itself.

```bash
bxrig tui apps --demo           # made-up data, nothing is read or run
bxrig tui apps --json           # the installed list and the update count, no terminal needed
```

Settings for tests and unusual machines: `BXRIG_DESKTOP_DIRS` (folders with `.desktop` files, colon separated, instead of `/usr/share/applications` and your own) and `BXRIG_CACHE_HOME`. Every outside command is optional: no `pacman`, `checkupdates` or `flatpak` gives an empty list and a sentence on screen, never an error.

Next: [Updates and channels](/maintain/updates/index.html) · [Backups](/data/backups/index.html) · [Export and import](/data/export-import/index.html)

title: BoxLang and MatchBox
body: BoxLang and MatchBox Use this page to keep BoxLang and MatchBox current, manage modules and run your web apps. The installer puts in Java 21, bvm (BoxLang Version Manager), mvm (MatchBox Version Manager), BoxLang and MatchBox. bxrig boxlang sits on top of them. Try it bxrig boxlang status bxrig boxlang check # your BoxLang and modules against the latest bxrig boxlang update --yes Pick a version bxrig boxlang use latest # bvm: install if missing, then use bxrig boxlang use snapshot bxrig boxlang matchbox use latest # mvm bxrig boxlang run hello.bxs # the real boxlang, in this terminal bxrig boxlang repl Keep it up to date flowchart LR A["bxrig boxlang check"] --> B{"Anything behind?"} B -->|"no"| C["Exit 0"] B -->|"yes"| D["Exit 10"] D --> E["boxlang update --yes"] D --> F["modules update"] The diagram shows how a check leads to an update. bxrig boxlang check # BoxLang against the latest release, and every module against ForgeBox bxrig boxlang update --yes # bvm install latest + bvm use latest (or the quick installer when there is no bvm) bxrig boxlang modules outdated # the bx-module table bxrig boxlang modules update # every outdated module (bx-module update --force) bxrig boxlang modules remove bx-ftp --yes bxrig boxlang home --open # ~/.boxlang (or BOXLANG_HOME): modules, config, logs check reads the version from the jar next to boxlang , so the runtime is never started for it, and the latest from version-latest.properties on downloads.ortussolutions.com. It exits 10 when anything is behind, like bxrig update check . A build number does not count: 1.19.0 and 1.19.0+67 are the same release. Install modules Modules come from ForgeBox and install with bx-module . bxrig boxlang modules list # the live ForgeBox list bxrig boxlang modules search ai bxrig boxlang modules install bx-ai bx-sites bxrig boxlang vscode # the BoxLang extension and developer pack VS Code is a default app; the wizard offers to add the BoxLang extension ( ortus-solutions.vscode-boxlang ) and the developer pack. The Control Center has a Modules page ( bxrig tui modules ): u updates a module (or all outdated, on the first row), x removes one, i installs one. The System panel has a BoxLang tab: the version you run and the latest, an Update button, the modules with the ForgeBox version of each outdated one, Update modules, Open home folder and the Modules page. It asks ForgeBox at most every 10 minutes. Run your web apps Register your BoxLang and CFML web apps once, then start, stop and open them from anywhere: the command line, the Control Center's Servers page ( bxrig tui servers ) or the BoxLang tab of the Developer panel. bxrig boxlang servers scan ~/code --yes # every folder with a miniserver.json or server.json (3 levels deep; --depth=N) bxrig boxlang servers add ~/code/shop-api # or one folder bxrig boxlang servers start shop-api bxrig boxlang servers open shop-api # in the browser More verbs: bxrig boxlang servers # what is registered, and what runs bxrig boxlang servers log shop-api --follow bxrig boxlang servers folder shop-api # in the file manager bxrig boxlang servers stop shop-api bxrig boxlang servers remove shop-api # forgets it; the folder stays The Developer panel also has a Ports tab: what listens on this machine (your dev servers, databases and apps, not the system's own), with a button to open a web port. Compile to a native binary matchbox script.bxs MatchBox compiles BoxLang to bytecode on a Rust runtime and can build standalone native binaries. BxRig itself is built this way. Advanced How BxRig drives a web app The folder has It runs on How BxRig drives it miniserver.json BoxLang MiniServer boxlang-miniserver miniserver.json in the folder, detached; its output in ~/.local/state/bxrig/servers/NAME.log server.json CommandBox box server start , stop and log with directory= the folder The port, host and web root are read from that file every time, so editing it is enough. An app runs when its port is listening. A CommandBox app without web.http.port gets a port from CommandBox, so BxRig cannot tell it runs or open it: set the port in server.json . The registry is ~/.config/bxrig/servers.json . The MatchBox home, .env files and logs MatchBox follows the BoxLang CLI. On its first run it creates ~/.matchbox (move it with MATCHBOX_HOME ) holding config/boxlang.json and logs/ . Every run also reads two .env files: ~/.matchbox.env (yours) and .env in the directory you run from, where the project file wins. Scripts read the values with getSystemSetting() . BxRig is a MatchBox program, so it reads them too. bxrig boxlang matchbox status # the MatchBox home, config, .env files and logs bxrig boxlang matchbox log-level info --yes bxrig boxlang matchbox env list # the names in ~/.matchbox.env, never the values bxrig boxlang matchbox env set OPENAI_API_KEY sk-... --yes bxrig boxlang matchbox log-level debug --yes log-level changes logging.rootLevel in the home config and leaves its comments alone. env set writes one line to ~/.matchbox.env (mode 600) and env unset removes it. The first command to change something prints a plan, and --yes applies it. Values are never printed. BxRig writes the result of every command to its own MatchBox log, ~/.matchbox/logs/bxrig.log , as [bxrig] boxlang exit 4 . MatchBox keeps warnings and errors by default, so a normal run writes nothing and a failed precondition (exit 4) or a failure (exit 5 or 6) is recorded. To see every command, set the level of the bxrig logger in ~/.matchbox/config/boxlang.json : { "logging": { "loggers": { "bxrig": { "level": "INFO" } } } } Exit 0 is written at INFO , a usage error or plan (2) and an update notice (10) at DEBUG , and exits 1, 3 and 4 as warnings. Nothing is written with an older MatchBox that has no runtime home. These files and folders belong to MatchBox releases that have a runtime home. With an older MatchBox the commands still work on the files, but nothing reads them. Other commands bxrig boxlang links # docs and sites bxrig boxlang welcome # a getting-started page Try BoxLang · Docs · BoxLang AI · BoxLang Agents · BoxLang Sites · ForgeBox · Skills Next: Developer tools · Databases and virtual machines · Scheduler

```bash
bxrig boxlang status
bxrig boxlang check                   # your BoxLang and modules against the latest
bxrig boxlang update --yes
```

![bxrig boxlang check](/assets/screenshots/boxlang-check.webp)

## Pick a version

```bash
bxrig boxlang use latest              # bvm: install if missing, then use
bxrig boxlang use snapshot
bxrig boxlang matchbox use latest     # mvm
bxrig boxlang run hello.bxs           # the real boxlang, in this terminal
bxrig boxlang repl
```

## Keep it up to date

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["bxrig boxlang check"] --> B{"Anything behind?"}
  B -->|"no"| C["Exit 0"]
  B -->|"yes"| D["Exit 10"]
  D --> E["boxlang update --yes"]
  D --> F["modules update"]
```

The diagram shows how a check leads to an update.

```bash
bxrig boxlang check                   # BoxLang against the latest release, and every module against ForgeBox
bxrig boxlang update --yes            # bvm install latest + bvm use latest (or the quick installer when there is no bvm)
bxrig boxlang modules outdated        # the bx-module table
bxrig boxlang modules update          # every outdated module (bx-module update --force)
bxrig boxlang modules remove bx-ftp --yes
bxrig boxlang home --open             # ~/.boxlang (or BOXLANG_HOME): modules, config, logs
```

`check` reads the version from the jar next to `boxlang`, so the runtime is never started for it, and the latest from `version-latest.properties` on downloads.ortussolutions.com. It exits 10 when anything is behind, like `bxrig update check`. A build number does not count: 1.19.0 and 1.19.0+67 are the same release.

## Install modules

Modules come from [ForgeBox](https://forgebox.io) and install with `bx-module`.

```bash
bxrig boxlang modules list            # the live ForgeBox list
bxrig boxlang modules search ai
bxrig boxlang modules install bx-ai bx-sites
bxrig boxlang vscode                  # the BoxLang extension and developer pack
```

VS Code is a default app; the wizard offers to add the BoxLang extension (`ortus-solutions.vscode-boxlang`) and the developer pack.

The **Control Center** has a Modules page (`bxrig tui modules`): `u` updates a module (or all outdated, on the first row), `x` removes one, `i` installs one. The **System panel** has a BoxLang tab: the version you run and the latest, an Update button, the modules with the ForgeBox version of each outdated one, Update modules, Open home folder and the Modules page. It asks ForgeBox at most every 10 minutes.

## Run your web apps

Register your BoxLang and CFML web apps once, then start, stop and open them from anywhere: the command line, the Control Center's Servers page (`bxrig tui servers`) or the BoxLang tab of the Developer panel.

```bash
bxrig boxlang servers scan ~/code --yes     # every folder with a miniserver.json or server.json (3 levels deep; --depth=N)
bxrig boxlang servers add ~/code/shop-api   # or one folder
bxrig boxlang servers start shop-api
bxrig boxlang servers open shop-api         # in the browser
```

![The Servers page](/assets/screenshots/servers-page.webp)

More verbs:

```bash
bxrig boxlang servers                       # what is registered, and what runs
bxrig boxlang servers log shop-api --follow
bxrig boxlang servers folder shop-api       # in the file manager
bxrig boxlang servers stop shop-api
bxrig boxlang servers remove shop-api       # forgets it; the folder stays
```

The Developer panel also has a **Ports** tab: what listens on this machine (your dev servers, databases and apps, not the system's own), with a button to open a web port.

## Compile to a native binary

```bash
matchbox script.bxs
```

[MatchBox](https://matchbox.boxlang.io) compiles BoxLang to bytecode on a Rust runtime and can build standalone native binaries. BxRig itself is built this way.

## Advanced

### How BxRig drives a web app

|  The folder has   |     It runs on     |                                                 How BxRig drives it                                                 |
|-------------------|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `miniserver.json` | BoxLang MiniServer | `boxlang-miniserver miniserver.json` in the folder, detached; its output in `~/.local/state/bxrig/servers/NAME.log` |
| `server.json`     | CommandBox         | `box server start`, `stop` and `log` with `directory=` the folder                                                   |

The port, host and web root are read from that file every time, so editing it is enough. An app runs when its port is listening. A CommandBox app without `web.http.port` gets a port from CommandBox, so BxRig cannot tell it runs or open it: set the port in `server.json`. The registry is `~/.config/bxrig/servers.json`.

### The MatchBox home, `.env` files and logs

MatchBox follows the BoxLang CLI. On its first run it creates `~/.matchbox` (move it with `MATCHBOX_HOME`) holding `config/boxlang.json` and `logs/`. Every run also reads two `.env` files: `~/.matchbox.env` (yours) and `.env` in the directory you run from, where the project file wins. Scripts read the values with `getSystemSetting()`. BxRig is a MatchBox program, so it reads them too.

```bash
bxrig boxlang matchbox status         # the MatchBox home, config, .env files and logs
bxrig boxlang matchbox log-level info --yes
bxrig boxlang matchbox env list       # the names in ~/.matchbox.env, never the values
bxrig boxlang matchbox env set OPENAI_API_KEY sk-... --yes
bxrig boxlang matchbox log-level debug --yes
```

`log-level` changes `logging.rootLevel` in the home config and leaves its comments alone. `env set` writes one line to `~/.matchbox.env` (mode 600) and `env unset` removes it. The first command to change something prints a plan, and `--yes` applies it. Values are never printed.

BxRig writes the result of every command to its own MatchBox log, `~/.matchbox/logs/bxrig.log`, as `[bxrig] boxlang exit 4`. MatchBox keeps warnings and errors by default, so a normal run writes nothing and a failed precondition (exit 4) or a failure (exit 5 or 6) is recorded. To see every command, set the level of the `bxrig` logger in `~/.matchbox/config/boxlang.json`:

```json
{ "logging": { "loggers": { "bxrig": { "level": "INFO" } } } }
```

Exit 0 is written at `INFO`, a usage error or plan (2) and an update notice (10) at `DEBUG`, and exits 1, 3 and 4 as warnings. Nothing is written with an older MatchBox that has no runtime home.

These files and folders belong to MatchBox releases that have a runtime home. With an older MatchBox the commands still work on the files, but nothing reads them.

### Other commands

```bash
bxrig boxlang links                   # docs and sites
bxrig boxlang welcome                 # a getting-started page
```

[Try BoxLang](https://try.boxlang.io) · [Docs](https://boxlang.ortusbooks.com) · [BoxLang AI](https://ai.boxlang.io) · [BoxLang Agents](https://bxagents.ai) · [BoxLang Sites](https://bxsites.io) · [ForgeBox](https://forgebox.io) · [Skills](https://skills.boxlang.io)

Next: [Developer tools](/build/developer-tools/index.html) · [Databases and virtual machines](/build/databases-and-vms/index.html) · [Scheduler](/data/scheduler/index.html)

title: Command contract
body: BxRig command contract Target (2026-11-09): Hyprland + Noctalia on CachyOS, KDE kept side by side; see plan.md section 19. setup is the headline command. Status (2026-11-15): built. This file started as the proposal and became the design record; sections 1 to 12 are the rules and the first build, section 13 onward holds one decision section per feature, 14 the installer and the wizard. Where a sentence here and the code disagree, the code wins: docs/reference/cli.json is the command registry (96 commands and their flags, usage and examples), docs/reference/commands.md is generated from it, and bxrig help NAME prints the same text. The legacy tree in artifacts/legacy/original/ is the v0.10.0 source, kept as a feature reference and never modified. 1. Grammar bxrig <command> [subcommand] [args...] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] [--quiet] [--force] A command is one word from docs/reference/cli.json ( setup , keys , menu , record , browser , ...); its subcommands and positional arguments are in its usage lines. Groups in the reference (Start here, Install, Desktop, Look, System, Develop, Tools) only organise the page. Mutating verbs ( install , apply , remove , restore , enable , disable , set , ...) need --yes ; read-only ones ( list , show , status , plan , doctor ) never do. Flags are checked against the registry before anything runs: a flag the command does not list is a usage error (exit 2, the usage line is printed); secrets run passes everything after its own flags through. An unknown command is exit 2 too. CLIGetArgs() puts flags in args.options and the words in args.positionals ; a flag with a value is written --name=value (the form --name value is a flag plus a positional on MatchBox). 2. Mutation rules (apply to every mutating verb) No --yes : print the exact plan, change nothing, exit 2. --dry-run with --yes : print the exact plan, change nothing, exit 0. Preflight everything before the first mutation. A preflight failure means zero changes. Never escalate privilege silently. sudo is only called for pacman steps shown in the plan. Never run AUR builds as root (exit 4). Every config file touched goes through the config service (backup, atomic replace, journal). No direct writes. Output lists succeeded and failed items separately. No rollback is promised across pacman and yay. External installer scripts (bvm, mvm, toolchain node 's nvm, catalog source: script ) are downloaded to a temp file, their url and sha256 are printed, and they run as the normal user (never root) with no confirmation gate and no flag: the typed EXECUTE and --allow-external-scripts were removed on 2026-11-10 (owner: running them is the point of the command). Decision 2026-11-09: no checksum pinning for these scripts. Subprocesses are launched with argument arrays, never through a shell string. The one place that starts a process is util/Proc ; the few sh -c wrappers pass every value as a positional argument ( detach , recording, the pull-down shells). The plan, dry-run and run protocol is one class, util/Mutation , reached through Out.plan( ... ) : no --yes prints "Plan: TITLE", the extra lines and "Nothing was changed. Add --yes to apply." (exit 2); --dry-run prints "Dry run: TITLE" and the same lines (exit 0); the first failing step ends the run (exit 6). A ratchet in tests/dry-test.sh forbids hand-written plan footers. Documented exceptions to --yes : a command that changes only your own settings or starts or stops a program acts at once and takes --dry-run (themes, appearance , time format , display , notify , tiling , runner set , layout , record , webcam , window , browser private , files here , dictation toggle ). Anything that installs packages, writes system files or changes login behaviour always needs --yes . 3. Exit codes Code Meaning Example 0 Success or no-op already installed, or --dry-run 1 Check negative package-status says missing 2 Usage error or missing confirmation no --yes , unknown flag 3 Timeout, or item unavailable pacman lookup timed out, package not in any repo 4 Precondition failed root with AUR, not Arch, Java missing, not KDE where required 5 Official (pacman) phase failed 6 AUR (yay) phase failed 7 Partial success some items done, some failed; --json lists both 8 Config conflict drift detected, symlink or special file at target, concurrent run lock 9 Internal error bug, unexpected exception ( Application.bx onError prints it and exits 9) 10 An update is available update check only The codes are frozen. tests/cli-contract-test.sh and the per-command tests check them; a bad name is exit 2 everywhere (it was 4 in some commands before the Names helper); an unknown command or flag is exit 2. Names in code. src/bxrig/util/Exit.bx names every code: ok 0, negative 1, usage and plan 2, timeout 3, precondition 4, official 5, failed 6, partial 7, conflict 8, internal 9, update 10. Cli.say , Cli.fail , Out.say and Out.fail take a name or a number; an unknown name throws. Command classes write the name ( variables.out.say( "precondition", ... ) , CLIExit( xit.usage() ) , return new bxrig.Exit().ok(); ), so a typo cannot turn into a wrong exit code. The numbers on the wire are the table above. tests/dry-test.sh fails on a bare number as the code argument of say / fail and on CLIExit( N ) in Main.bx (130, Ctrl+C, is the exception). 4. --json With --json a command prints one JSON object on stdout and no human text ( Cli.envelope ): { "schema": 1, "command": "profile install", "version": "0.11.0-dev", "ok": false, "exit": 7, "dry_run": false, "data": { "done": [], "failed": [], "skipped": [] }, "warnings": [] } data is different for every command (the package commands put would_install , done , failed and skipped there, section 11); ok is true when exit is 0. A plan is exit 2 with the plan in data ; a dry run is exit 0 with dry_run true. 5. Catalog (single source of truth) The catalog is catalog/apps.json (schema 4, 349 apps today, version in catalog_version : what each app is) plus one install file per distribution, catalog/install/{arch,suse,debian,ubuntu}.json (how to install it there; see "Distributions"), packed into the binary as a resource ( src/resources/catalog ). It started as the legacy apps.json (482 entries) and replaced the hardcoded lists. The findings below are the 2026-11-09 audit of that legacy data and are kept as the record of why the catalog looks as it does. Entry schema (legacy fields kept, new fields marked): Field Notes id , name , kind ( desktop tui web ), category , description as legacy source ( pacman aur pkgbuild script manual web ), target package name, or URL for web and script pkgbuild source: repo , path , ref Build with makepkg as the normal user from a PKGBUILD in a public git repo, pinned to a full 40-character commit ( catalog check rejects anything else), then install the result with pacman. Used for desktop apps packaged in omacom/omarchy-pkgs . The PKGBUILD is shown before it is built. check (for script ) argv array that exits 0 when installed, for example ["command","-v","pi"] default base tier flag source_status , source_confirmed legacy provenance flags, kept profiles (new) list of profile ids deps (new) other catalog ids check (new) optional post-install check, argv array verified_on (new) date the target was confirmed against real repos Findings from the legacy data (historical, decisions recorded 2026-11-09): Unverified sources. 176 entries are source: manual (95 tui, 81 desktop). Their package names are unverified. Proposal: a CI job that checks every pacman / aur target against real repos (Arch container, AUR RPC) and fails on unknown names. manual entries stay installable only by explicit user action. Default list mismatch. 61 flagged default (29 pacman, 18 aur, 14 web). app-profile.json base lists 46. 20 defaults are not in that base list (for example ark dolphin dolphin-plugins kio-extras rclone fuse3 sshfs nfs-utils cifs-utils podman-desktop tabby beekeeper-studio google-docs google-sheets google-slides kompare filelight ffmpegthumbs kdegraphics-thumbnailers kimageformats ). 5 base entries are not flagged default ( dbeaver filezilla krdc podman-tui rustdesk ). The 61 flags win. The 5 dropped base entries are dbeaver (pacman), filezilla (pacman), krdc (pacman), rustdesk (aur) and podman-tui (manual). Pending: keep them as curated (not default), or re-flag any as default. Browsers. brave is aur ( brave-bin ) and default. A fresh default install therefore needs yay on day one. Decision: bootstrap installs yay only if it is not already present. Preserve list. Legacy preserve (CachyOS, KDE Plasma, Hyprland, Noctalia, existing user configs) becomes enforced rules, not just text. Named profiles keep the existing four ( core jvm containers terminal ) and are expressed as catalog profiles tags. Later profiles ( web backend ai ops desktop full ) are added only after package names are verified. Ship vs embed (pending confirmation): the default catalog is embedded in the binary at build time, so there is one file to ship and it always matches the code. An optional ~/.config/bxrig/catalog.json adds entries or sets default / profiles on existing ids. It is validated against the same schema and can never delete or replace an embedded entry's target , so a bad override cannot redirect an install. 6. State and config layout ~/.config/bxrig/ same root as legacy bxrig.json global settings catalog.json optional user additions (merge-only) ai.json menu.json shortcuts.json ... one file per feature, as legacy ~/.local/state/bxrig/ journal/ one record per apply: files, hashes, backup paths backups/ backups, indexed by the journal lock single-writer lock config list|diff|apply|restore work from the journal, so restore needs only an id. Retention default: keep the last 20 per file. Open: this applies to the user's config files that BxRig writes, not to the legacy source tree. 7. Test contract A snapshot test freezes bxrig help , the exit-code table and the --json schema. Every mutating verb needs these cases: success, no-op, invalid input, dependency failure, privilege rejection, partial failure, recovery. Real-system cases run in tests/arch/ (non-root, real pacman). Cases needing KDE, Wayland or hardware are marked manual and tracked in the acceptance log. 8. Catalog check, validation and reporting bxrig catalog check [--json] [--online] plus a CI job that runs it in the Arch container. Offline validation (always, no network): schema version; unique ids; enums for kind / source ; web targets are https with no credentials or control characters; package targets match ^[a-zA-Z0-9@._+-]+$ ; default entries have a non- manual source; profiles and deps reference existing ids; no dependency cycles. Online verification ( --online , CI): every pacman target must resolve with pacman -Si (or -Sg for groups); every aur target must resolve through the AUR RPC ( /rpc/v5/info ); manual targets are probed against both and reported as promotable. Results are stored per entry as verified_on and a status: ok , moved (listed source is wrong but another source has it), missing , unverified . Reporting: a table by status and source for the console, --json for tools, and a markdown report in the CI step summary and artifact. Policy: missing entries with default: true fail CI; missing non-default entries are warnings listed in the report; moved entries are warnings with the suggested fix. First measurement (2026-11-09, stock Arch core/extra only, so CachyOS repos and multilib are not covered): Check Result pacman targets (118) 111 resolve, 7 do not: 5 exist in AUR ( git-cola insomnia localsend ulauncher wlogout ), 2 found nowhere ( intellij-idea-community-edition , swww ) aur targets (64) 40 resolve in AUR, 11 are now official ( doggo impala nwg-dock-hyprland opencode podman-desktop rio spotify-launcher superfile television warehouse zenmap ), 13 found nowhere ( beeper ctop dbgate espanso grokbot herder inshellisense notion-desktop pi-agent tmog todoist upnote zap-whatsapp ) manual targets (176) 93 are official packages today (promotable, for example jq ripgrep-all tmux kitty starship terraform kubectl ), 83 are not The check must also run against the CachyOS repos on a real CachyOS machine before any missing entry is removed. 9. Open questions The 5 dropped base entries: keep as curated, or re-flag any as default? Catalog embed with merge-only user override: confirmed? Hyprland features (layout, runner, shortcuts, menus) are now in scope, not deferred. 10. Implemented so far (2026-11-09) config list|diff|apply|restore|history (section 6 design; lock is a file created with fileWriteExclusive , temp files and journal records are created exclusive with their mode). Global flag check and the --json envelope (sections 1 and 4) for the read-only commands. catalog list|show|groups|check|version : the catalog is schema 4 plus the install files ( catalog/README.md ) and is packed into the binary as a resource ( src/resources/catalog , read by src/bxrig/CatalogData.bx ). Filters use the --name=value form ( --tier=default --group=infra ), because MatchBox CLIGetArgs takes --name value as a flag plus a positional. catalog check is offline: errors exit 1, warnings (unpinned pkgbuild refs, default entries without a package) do not. The user override file is deliberately last (extensibility phase). 11. Package commands on the catalog (B2, decided 2026-11-09) Applies to plan , install-plan , install , optional-* , profile-* , package-status , package-source . All read the embedded catalog (schema 3). Hardcoded lists in Main.bx go away. Selection bxrig install # tier default bxrig install ID [ID...] # exactly these apps bxrig install --profile=NAME # a profile bxrig install --optional # default tier plus optional tier Naming an app is enough. There is no --aur flag : anything in the catalog installs from its source ( pacman , aur , pkgbuild , web ). Unknown id: usage error (exit 2), nothing runs. Skip reasons: optional (not selected), wrong_shell and unresolved (catalog has no installable source yet; a named unresolved app is reported failed , exit 3). Already installed apps are skipped with reason installed . Section 2 still applies: no --yes prints the plan and exits 2; --dry-run --yes prints it and exits 0. AUR and pkgbuild builds never run as root (exit 4). Profiles live in the catalog (0.3.0): a top-level profiles list and, per app, a map profile id to default / optional . --profile=NAME installs the profile's default members; --optional adds its optional ones. See catalog/README.md . Shells: an app may carry shells ( hyprland , plasma ). The running shell comes from XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP , overridable with --shell=hyprland|plasma|all . Non-matching apps are skipped: wrong_shell ; a named app still installs. Per-source steps source step pacman one pacman -S --needed call for all pacman apps (sudo shown in the plan) aur AUR helper (yay) as the normal user, apps one at a time pkgbuild PKGBUILD shown, makepkg as the normal user, result installed with pacman web a .desktop launcher in ~/.local/share/applications/bxrig-<id>.desktop running brave --app=URL (written atomically, no package). The resolver adds brave to the plan when a web app is selected and brave is not installed. Result shape ( --json , inside the section 4 envelope) data for plan , install-plan and install : { "selection": { "mode": "default|ids|profile|optional", "ids": [], "profile": null }, "would_install": [ { "id": "git", "source": "pacman", "targets": ["git"] } ], "done": [ { "id": "git", "source": "pacman" } ], "failed": [ { "id": "docker", "source": "pacman", "error": "target not found" } ], "skipped": [ { "id": "jq", "reason": "optional" } ] } plan and --dry-run fill would_install and leave done / failed empty. A real run fills done / failed and leaves would_install empty. Exit: 0 all done or nothing to do; 5 pacman phase failed, 6 AUR/pkgbuild phase failed (only when nothing succeeded); 7 some done and some failed. package-status ID exits 0 when installed, 1 when missing; data is { "id", "source", "installed": true|false } . package-source ID prints { "id", "source", "targets", "tier", "group" } . Human output is the same lists, one app per line with its source. Open questions Decided: a web app counts as installed when its launcher file exists. 12. Implemented so far, B2 (2026-11-09) Catalog 0.3.0: profiles , per-profile tier, shells (section 11, catalog/README.md ). Resolver class (selection) and Packages class (read-only commands). plan , install-plan , optional-plan , profile-plan , profile-install-plan , package-status , package-source , profile-list , desktop-list , tui-list , web-list , optional-list run on the catalog. Installed state comes from one pacman -Qq call (web apps: launcher file). install , optional-install , profile-install run on the catalog through Installer (one pacman -S call, yay per AUR app, pinned PKGBUILDs via git clone + makepkg -si ). Rules as in sections 2 and 11: no --yes prints the plan (exit 2), --dry-run exits 0, root with AUR or PKGBUILD builds exits 4 before any change, a named app without a source exits 3, partial results exit 7 (5 or 6 when nothing succeeded). Web apps install as launchers (see section 11 table). The 28 pkgbuild apps are pinned to one commit of omacom/omarchy-pkgs and install with git clone , git checkout COMMIT , makepkg -si as the normal user (root exits 4). All of them are optional, so a plain bxrig install skips them. Not on the catalog: apps-doctor , dev-plan . 13. Desktop setup (decided with the owner 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-10; all built) Builds on sections 2 to 4 (mutation rules, exit codes, --json ), the config service (section 6) and the Installer (argument arrays, done / failed / skipped ). Hyprland with Noctalia is installed beside KDE Plasma; KDE is never removed or reconfigured except what --keys hands over, which is backed up first. 13.1 Commands bxrig setup hyprland [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] packages, images, starter configs, shortcut files bxrig setup plasma [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] HyprKwin tiling on KDE Plasma bxrig setup plasma --keys | --undo-keys hand Plasma's clashing keys over / back bxrig setup hyprland --terminal=ghostty|kitty|alacritty|foot|konsole Super+Enter terminal (ghostty default) bxrig setup hyprland --layout=dwindle|master|scrolling|floating default window layout in the starter hyprland.lua (dwindle default) bxrig setup hyprland --workspaces=N --natural-scroll --layouts=us-intl,es --theme=dark|light|auto --wallpaper=box|grid|aurora|minimal starter choices (defaults: 2, off, us, dark, box); two or more keyboard layouts switch with Alt+Shift bxrig setup terminal [--default=ghostty] [--also=kitty,foot,...] install terminals, starter configs with the Nerd Font bxrig setup shell [--shell=zsh|fish|bash] Starship + shell init, login shell (zsh default) bxrig setup xremap [--build=hypr|kde] [--yes] Cmd-style keys: AUR package, input access, user service bxrig setup undo hyprland|plasma|xremap [--yes] remove only what setup added bxrig setup status [--json] bxrig tiling on|off|status HyprKwin inside Plasma, no logout bxrig keys show | search TEXT | run ID | style [traditional|mac] | set ID KEYS | reset ID | conflicts | sheet | render xremap|hyprland|plasma | check | apply [--yes] [--dry-run] [--force] (the full usage is in cli.json) bxrig assets list | install [--yes] [--dry-run] bxrig session show | set hyprland|plasma [--yes] [--dry-run] bxrig runner list | show | doctor | launch | select JSON | set P | menu-set P | launcher-command P JSON | menu-command P JSON the launcher abstraction (13.9) Every target runs, re-runs and undoes on its own; a re-run changes nothing when everything is in place. No --yes prints the plan (exit 2); --dry-run exits 0. Results as install : done / failed / skipped , exits 0, 2, 4 (precondition: root, wrong OS or CPU, no sudo, no Plasma, unsupported Plasma, X11, nothing to undo, session not installed), 5 (the pacman step failed), 6 (another step failed with nothing done), 7 (a step failed after earlier ones were done; later steps are skipped), 8 (config drift or lock). Never run as root: sudo is used only for the steps shown in the plan. --json is always one envelope on stdout (the config service has a quiet mode for that). A failed step says why (2026-11-17): its failed entry carries command (the argv that failed) and output (the last five lines of what it printed, at most 800 characters), and the text report prints them under the Failed: line ( command: ... , | line ); bxrig init does the same for its steps. systemd steps are skipped where systemd is not running (no /run/systemd/system : a container or a chroot; BXRIG_SYSTEMD_RUN_DIR replaces the path in tests): the step is listed in skipped with the reason and the command to run on a real system, the plan carries a warning, and the run is not a failure. Exception to --yes : tiling on|off acts at once (a reversible user setting meant to sit behind a shortcut). status exits 0 on, 1 off, 4 not installed. 13.2 setup plasma (HyprKwin) HyprKwin ( DGBooth/HyprKwin ) is a KWin script with Hyprland-style layouts and keys. It needs Plasma 6.6 or 6.8 on Wayland (6.7 warns, older or X11 exit 4). It is fetched pinned to a full commit (v1.2.0, 31abb63 , same rule as PKGBUILDs) into a temp directory and installed with its own tools/install.sh as the normal user, which backs up every global shortcut first. Plasma's keys stay Plasma's unless --keys (runs tools/hyprkwin-shortcuts.py apply ; --undo-keys restores). The animations effect needs one logout. setup undo plasma runs HyprKwin's uninstall. tiling on|off sets hyprkwinEnabled in kwinrc [Plugins] and asks KWin to reconfigure over D-Bus ( off also unloads the script). 13.3 setup hyprland Preconditions (exit 4): not root, pacman, CachyOS or Arch, x86_64, sudo. Steps, in order: packages : the missing ones of 17 official packages in one sudo pacman -S --needed call: hyprland , native noctalia , uwsm , hyprlock , xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland , hyprpolkitagent , qt6ct , nwg-look , hyprpicker , grim , slurp , wl-clipboard , brightnessctl , kitty , adw-gtk-theme , noto-fonts , noto-fonts-emoji . Individual packages, never the CachyOS meta-package cachyos-hypr-noctalia (it conflicts with cachyos-desktop-settings , which the KDE session may rely on). Noctalia is the native noctalia package; noctalia-shell + noctalia-qs are a different Quickshell-based variant that conflicts with quickshell (a warning, not an error, if installed). Bar plugin data. db list --json rows are {container, status (the engine's text), state (running, paused, created, exited), image, engine, name, port} ; db info ENGINE --name N --show-password --json returns data.url , the connection string the Developer bar plugin copies ( vm list --json has state , ports , url per VM and vm start|stop NAME run them). Rules. Services listen on 127.0.0.1 only. A container that exists is never replaced (a stopped one is started; a running one is left alone). Containers are named bxrig-db-<engine>-<name> (name defaults to default ; letters, digits and hyphens) and labelled io.bxrig.database=true . Data lives in a named volume with the container's name, not a host folder ( db remove deletes it together with the container and the password files, so the next start is a clean database; --keep-data keeps them, and starting the same name again then reuses the volume and its password): rootless containers cannot write to a bind-mounted folder as the image's own user (OpenSearch, Elasticsearch and Meilisearch run as non-root). Choosing the password: by default one is generated. --password-file FILE uses the first line of a file you made; --ask-password asks twice at the terminal without echo ( /dev/tty , so it needs a terminal; the plan never prompts). A password is never a command-line value, so it cannot land in shell history or the process list. It must be 8 to 128 characters with no whitespace (OpenSearch also needs upper and lower case, a digit and a special character). It applies only when the container is created (the image sets it on first start of the data volume): a second start never changes it, an existing container refuses one, and a kept data volume (from remove --keep-data ) keeps the password it was made with (a different choice is refused). Engines without a password (Redis, Chroma, Qdrant, Weaviate) and Couchbase (set in its web console) refuse the options. The user name is fixed per engine ( postgres , root , admin , elastic ). Generated passwords (24 random bytes as hex) go in ~/.local/share/bxrig/databases/<container>/ ( password and database.env , mode 600, plus meta.json with the port) and reach the container through --env-file , never on a command line. Nothing changes system settings: when vm.max_map_count is too low start stops with the sudo sysctl -w line to run. Images are pinned and were checked on Docker Hub on 2026-11-10 (Elasticsearch's from Elastic's docs). The method is detected ( --method overrides): chezmoi ( .chezmoiroot , .chezmoiignore , or dot_ / .chezmoi* names), then yadm ( .config/yadm/ , or ## alternate names), then stow ( .stowrc , .stow-local-ignore , or only top-level package folders that hold dotfiles), else links . Your dotfiles win, but nothing is replaced unasked. The plan splits the repo's files into new, already in place (a link to the repo, or an identical file) and conflicts (files you already have that would be replaced; chezmoi templates always count). apply --yes needs your approval of the conflicts: --overwrite , or a y at the prompt (read from /dev/tty , so a headless run without --overwrite exits 2 and changes nothing). Every replaced file is first moved into ~/.local/state/bxrig/backups/dotfiles/<time>/ ; if a step then fails (exit 6) the originals are put back. status shows what was applied; undo --yes removes the links BxRig made ( stow -D for stow) and restores the originals (for chezmoi and yadm only the originals come back: the files those tools created stay, remove them with the tool). Method Files go to your home by Applied with links one symlink per file (folders are never replaced by a link) ln -s stow each top-level folder is a package stow -d CLONE -t HOME -R PACKAGES chezmoi dot_ , private_ , executable_ , ... prefixes and .tmpl are mapped to the plain path for the conflict list chezmoi apply --source CLONE --force yadm ## alternate suffixes are mapped to the plain name yadm clone -f --no-bootstrap REPO ( yadm pull when it is already set up) Repo-only files ( .git , README* , LICENSE* , .gitignore , .stow-local-ignore ...) are never linked. A missing tool ( chezmoi , yadm , stow ; Arch extra ) is installed with sudo pacman -S --needed as the first step of apply (the plan says so). One repository can be set up at a time: a second one is refused (exit 4) until undo . Exits: 0 done, 2 no --yes or conflicts not approved, 4 precondition (cannot clone, unknown method, nothing to apply, tool not installable), 6 a step failed. The wizard's Import page asks for the repository (empty skips); init runs dotfiles apply REPO last , so your files win over the starter configs, and the conflict question appears at the terminal. Tested against real git repositories and fake tools ( stow , chezmoi , yadm , pacman ); the real tools have not been run. Private repositories and credentials are git's business (SSH keys or a credential helper must already work). 13.12 Apps: Basic or Customize, and your defaults (decided with the owner 2026-11-11) The wizard's Apps page asks how you want your apps : Basic (the default: an opinionated, recommended set) or Customize . Every machine uses the same commands; export / import (later) moves them between machines. Command Does secrets status backend in use, whether a keyring is available, how many secrets are stored secrets set NAME [--from-file=F] stores a value: typed hidden at the terminal, or read from a file. Never a command-line value. Replaces an existing one secrets list names only, with the coding agent that reads each known key secrets get NAME [--show] says whether it is set and its length; --show prints the value secrets unset NAME --yes deletes a value (plan without --yes , exit 2) secrets run [NAMES...] [--strict] -- CMD... runs CMD with those secrets in its own environment only; exit code is CMD's. A name that is not set is skipped, --strict exits 4 secrets env [NAMES...] prints export NAME='value' lines for eval (all stored names when none given) Names are environment variable names: capital letters, digits, underscores ( ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , OPENAI_API_KEY , GEMINI_API_KEY ). Backend: the desktop keyring through secret-tool (libsecret) when secret-tool exists and org.freedesktop.secrets is on the user D-Bus (running or activatable); otherwise private files ( ~/.local/share/bxrig/secrets/NAME , mode 600 in a mode 700 folder). The choice is saved in ~/.config/bxrig/secrets.json and shown by status . Keyring entries carry the attributes service=bxrig name=NAME . Values are passed to secret-tool and to programs through standard input and the process environment, never through a command line, a temp file, a log, or answers.json . set is interactive on purpose and needs no --yes . Exit codes: 0 done, 2 usage or plan without --yes , 4 precondition (bad name, secret not set, no value), 6 the store failed. Loading into shells (default is per command, global is opt-in per key): secrets apply [--yes] writes ~/.config/bxrig/secrets.sh (bash, zsh) and secrets.fish . They hold no values: one wrapper per agent command whose key is stored ( claude() { bxrig secrets run ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -- command claude "$@"; } ). secrets set runs it automatically. The shell init templates source these files. secrets global on NAME --yes | off NAME | show : exports a key to every new shell. on prints a warning first (every program, including AI agents and what they run, can read it). The values go to a session cache, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bxrig-secrets.env and .fish (mode 600, tmpfs, wiped at logout), never to a config file. The loader files call secrets unlock once per login when the cache is missing (the keyring's single unlock prompt); secrets lock removes the cache. A globally exported key gets no wrapper. Moving machines and the keyring: secrets export FILE [--plain] [--force] --yes : all stored secrets as export NAME='value' lines, encrypted with a passphrase by age -p (age asks on the terminal; the file is mode 600). --plain writes a readable .env instead (mode 600; the plan says so). An existing file is kept unless --force . secrets import FILE [--overwrite] --yes : reads an age file or a .env file; the plan lists each name as new, same or differs. A name that already has a different value is kept unless --overwrite . New machine: install.sh , init --answers answers.json , secrets import , dotfiles apply . secrets setup [--keyring=kwallet|gnome-keyring|none] [--yes] [--dry-run] : checks for a Secret Service on the user D-Bus (running or activatable). Installs libsecret ( secret-tool , repo core) and age (repo extra) when missing; when no keyring exists, also kwallet on Plasma or gnome-keyring elsewhere, or the one named. --keyring=none installs no keyring and saves the file backend. The plan names what it installs. Package names and secret-tool in libsecret were checked on archlinux.org on 2026-11-11. Secret types and providers (decided with the owner 2026-11-11): Every secret has a type : ai (a key for an AI provider) or other (a GitHub token and so on). A name in the provider registry is ai automatically; any other name is other unless secrets set NAME --type=ai [--provider=ID] says otherwise. The type and provider are kept in secrets.json ( meta , names only, never values). secrets list [--type=ai|other] filters; secrets run --type=ai -- CMD loads every AI key and no other secret. The provider registry ( AiProviders ) maps providers to environment variables: anthropic ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , openai OPENAI_API_KEY , google GEMINI_API_KEY , openrouter OPENROUTER_API_KEY , novita NOVITA_API_KEY , opencode OPENCODE_API_KEY , groq, mistral, deepseek, xai, together ( GROQ_API_KEY , MISTRAL_API_KEY , DEEPSEEK_API_KEY , XAI_API_KEY , TOGETHER_API_KEY ). Names are from models.dev (the registry OpenCode uses), checked 2026-11-11. Each agent declares the providers it accepts ( AiAgents ): Claude Code anthropic, Codex openai, Gemini CLI google, OpenCode all of the above. An agent is only ever given keys from its own list. Its wrapper carries the stored ones among them ( opencode() { bxrig secrets run ANTHROPIC_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY -- command opencode "$@"; } ); nothing else is loaded. Tests: tests/secrets-test.sh (fake secret-tool and busctl ). The registry of agent key names is from the vendors' documentation and the user can store any other valid name. 13.14 AI agents (decided with the owner 2026-11-11) bxrig ai knows four coding agents ( AiAgents ): claude-code (command claude ), codex-cli ( codex ), gemini-cli ( gemini ), opencode-cli ( opencode ), each with the providers whose keys it accepts (see 13.13). Command names were checked in the Arch packages ( openai-codex ships /usr/bin/codex , gemini-cli ships /usr/bin/gemini ; claude-code comes from the CachyOS repo). The key names are from the vendors' documentation. Command Does ai list each agent: installed, key stored, default ai default [ID] [--yes] shows the default, or sets it (the agent must be installed; plan without --yes , exit 2). Saved in ~/.config/bxrig/ai.json ai launch [ID] [--dry-run] opens the agent (the default when no ID) in your default terminal as TERMINAL [-e] bxrig secrets run KEY -- COMMAND , detached. The terminal is the first line of ~/.config/xdg-terminals.list if it names a terminal BxRig knows and it is installed, else the first installed one. ghostty, alacritty and konsole get -e ; kitty and foot get the command directly (foot and konsole flags are from memory, not verified here) ai shell [toggle\|status] [--backend=hyprland\|yakuake] [--dry-run] the pull-down AI shell: one shortcut shows and hides a terminal running your default agent (your shell when none is set); it keeps its session while hidden Pull-down AI shell. The backend follows the desktop: a Hyprland session ( HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE ) uses a special workspace, KDE Plasma uses Yakuake; --backend overrides. Exit 4 when neither applies, when no terminal can carry a window class, or when Yakuake is missing. Hyprland: the first call starts a terminal with the window class com.bxrig.ai (ghostty --class= , kitty and alacritty --class , foot --app-id ; konsole cannot) running bxrig secrets run KEYS -- AGENT , then sizes it to 100% x 45% and moves it to the top with hyprctl dispatch resizewindowpixel / movewindowpixel (best effort). The Hyprland module ( keys apply ) holds hl.window_rule({ name = "bxrig-ai", match = { class = "^com.bxrig.ai$" }, workspace = "special:ai", float = true }) and the shortcut Super+\`` running bxrig ai shell . Later calls toggle the workspace: hyprctl dispatch togglespecialworkspace ai , and if that fails the Lua form hl.dsp.workspace.toggle_special("ai") . Window class is the ghostty config option class` (GTK builds), and it must look like a GTK application id, hence the dotted name. Plasma (Yakuake): the first call starts Yakuake, waits for its D-Bus name, adds a tab ( org.kde.yakuake.addSession on /yakuake/sessions ), types the agent command ( runCommand ) and shows the window ( toggleWindowState on /yakuake/window ); later calls only toggle. The tab is remembered in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bxrig-ai-shell . init installs yakuake (official extra ) when Plasma and an agent are chosen. The Plasma shortcut is not written by BxRig: bind bxrig ai shell in System Settings, Shortcuts (Yakuake also has its own open/retract key). Not verified on a real desktop: the Hyprland window rule and dispatchers in Lua mode, the percentage resize and move, the special-workspace slide direction, and Yakuake's runCommand (its changelog mentions a security prompt). They are on the acceptance checklist. Tests: tests/ai-shell-test.sh (fake hyprctl , dbus-send , yakuake and terminals). Agent sessions (tmux). ai session start [ID] [--name=N] [--dir=PATH] [--dry-run] starts a detached tmux session bxrig-AGENT[-N] running the agent (the default when no ID) in PATH (the current folder by default) through secrets run , so it keeps working after you close the terminal. A session that already exists is reported, not replaced. ai session list shows only bxrig- sessions. ai session attach NAME joins one (NAME is the full name or what follows bxrig- ; needs a terminal; detach with the tmux prefix then d ). ai session stop NAME --yes ends one (plan without --yes , exit 2). Names are letters, digits, - , _ (up to 40). Exit 4: tmux or the agent missing, bad name, no such session; 6: a tmux command failed. init installs tmux when an agent is chosen. AiLocal.bx with AiHardware.bx (pure readers of /proc/cpuinfo , /proc/meminfo , lspci -mm , nvidia-smi ), AiCatalog.bx ( catalog/ai-models.json , schema 1; BXRIG_AI_CATALOG names another file) and AiProvider.bx (the Control Center page ai ). ai hardware : CPU, cores, instruction sets, RAM, graphics, free disk. Budget: a dedicated card's memory minus 1024 MB, else half the RAM; class tiny (<6000 MB), medium (<=14000), high. Backends: cpu; vulkan with any graphics; cuda with NVIDIA; rocm with a dedicated AMD card (>=4096 MB VRAM in mem_info_vram_total ). ai models recommend [--all] : up to three verified chat models that fit (need = max(mem_mb, size_mb) + 512): balanced (best score with reference reply <= 3 s; the default), fastest (score >= 16, quickest), capable (best score, larger on a tie). --all adds every model that fits, untested ones marked. Plus the default embedding model. ai engine [status|install|update] : ~/.local/bin/llama (official, llama.app installer, run with sh after --yes ), else llama or llama-server on the PATH. --source=aur installs llama.cpp-vulkan-bin (Arch only). update runs llama update (official installs only; a package updates with the system). ai models pull ID... [--yes] [--no-test] : batches of three curl downloads in the background ( -fL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors -C - to FILE.part ), progress every 2 s, SHA-256 against the catalog, then FILE.part becomes FILE . A mismatch keeps the .part and fails (exit 6). Disk check before (download + 1 GB). After: ai.json and the preset are written, a running server restarts, each new model gets the answer check. ai models use ID (chat models only; the old one is unloaded with POST /models/unload ), test [ID] (chat: one question, max_tokens 48, thinking off, records reply_s and tps from timings.predicted_per_second ; embeddings: one vector, records dimensions ), tune [ID] [--yes] ( llama bench -m FILE -t HALF,ALL -ub 256,512 -fa 0,1 -p 256 -n 32 -r 1 -o json ; the best setting maximises gen t/s + prompt t/s / 20; written as threads , ubatch-size , flash-attn in the preset), remove ID [--yes] . ai ask TEXT [--model=ID] : one question to the active (or named) model: { model, answer, reply_s, tps } . ai serve [status|start|stop|restart] , ai serve --listen=127.0.0.1|0.0.0.0 [--port=N] [--yes] : bxrig-ai.service (user) runs llama serve --models-preset ~/.config/bxrig/ai-models.ini --models-max 2|3 --host H --port P --no-webui (+ --api-key-file ~/.config/bxrig/ai-api-key when not 127.0.0.1; the key is made on the first switch, mode 600 before it is written, shown once). Default 127.0.0.1:8089. APIs: OpenAI /v1 , Anthropic /v1/messages , embeddings /v1/embeddings (verified on llama.cpp b12627). Preset (INI, router mode): one [ID] per installed model with model = PATH ; chat models ctx-size = 8192 and the tuned keys; embedding models embeddings = true . ai setup [--models=ID,ID|--picks=all] [--tune] [--yes] : engine, missing models (the balanced pick, or all picks, plus the embedding model), serve start , wait for /health (90 s), the answer check, the tune when asked. ai status : all of it for the bar and the page. Wizard: ai_local_setup ( now , later ), ai_local_picks ( balanced , all ), ai_local_tune (confirm); init runs one optional ai setup --yes [--picks=all] [--tune] step. ai_local still installs the local AI apps ticked (Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, KoboldCpp, GPT4All). Bar: the Agents panel's Local tab ( templates/noctalia-plugins/agents/local.luau ): ai status , ai serve start|stop , ai models use , ai ask , and tui ai in a terminal. ai discover [QUERY] [--fits] [--tools] [--vision] [--embeddings] [--limit=N] ( AiHub.bx ): the staff picks (the catalog's picks for this machine), then Hugging Face: GET /api/models?filter=gguf&sort=downloads&direction=-1&full=true&limit=N[&search=Q] , language models only (pipeline text-generation , image-text-to-text , feature-extraction , sentence-similarity , text2text-generation or none), gated repositories left out; per repository GET /api/models/REPO/tree/main?recursive=true for the .gguf files (no mmproj , no -0000N-of-0000M parts) with size and lfs.oid (the SHA-256). The file: the first of Q4_K_M, Q4_K_S, IQ4_XS, IQ4_NL, Q4_0, Q5_K_M, Q5_K_S, Q6_K, Q8_0. --tools asks GET /api/models/REPO and keeps repositories whose chat template mentions tools. BXRIG_HF_URL replaces https://huggingface.co for the API (tests). ai models pull hf:OWNER/REPO[/PATH.gguf] : resolved as above (no file without a 64-character SHA-256 is downloaded). Id: the catalog's id when the catalog has that repository, else the repository name in lower case without -GGUF (owner first when that clashes with a catalog id). The entry is kept in ai.json as models.ID.meta ( source: "hf" , verified: false ). Queue: every pull writes ~/.local/state/bxrig/ai-downloads/ID.json ( queued , downloading , checking , done , failed , cancelled ); --background runs the same pull detached ( setsid , output in pull.log there). ai downloads reads the records with the live share from the .part size; cancel ID marks it, stops its curl ( pkill -f on the .part path) and deletes the part; clear forgets finished records. ai bench [ID] ( AiBench.bx , catalog/ai-bench.json ): 20 cases (12 basic, 8 harder) with 10 tools, the system prompt, temperature 0, thinking off, max_tokens 400. Pass rules: one (the first call has the name and every argument matches its case-insensitive pattern), both (each expected call appears), none (no call). Kept as models.ID.bench { score, of, basic, hard, median_s, at, engine } . Checked on llama.cpp b12627: Qwen3.5 0.8B scores 17/20, as in the catalog. ai link [opencode|crush [--off] [--default] [--yes] [--dry-run]] ( AiAgentLink.bx ): OpenCode ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json gets providers.bxrig = { name, package: "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible", settings.baseURL: BASE/v1, models: { ID: {} } } (chat models) and, with --default , model: "bxrig/ACTIVE" ; a file that is not plain JSON is refused. The wizard's answers live in ~/.config/bxrig/answers.json (mode 600, no secrets) and fill the wizard on the next run. init --export=FILE [--force] copies them (mode 600); on another machine init --from=FILE fills the wizard with them, and init --answers=FILE --yes runs them without asking. Catalog: btrfs-assistant and timeshift (both extra , verified 2026-11-12) are in the default tier, so a plain install and Basic mode install them. Btrfs Assistant is in the default set only when / is Btrfs : the catalog entry has filesystems: ["btrfs"] , the resolver skips it elsewhere as wrong_filesystem (an unreadable filesystem counts as not Btrfs; BXRIG_ROOT_FS overrides the detection, which is findmnt -n -o FSTYPE / ), and naming it ( install btrfs-assistant ) still installs it. It shows the BxRig wordmark in the cyan to green gradient, the tagline and "Powered by BoxLang", checks the machine (CachyOS or Arch, not root, x86_64, sudo), downloads the channel's bxrig-linux-x86_64 and bootstrap.tar.gz , verifies the Ed25519 signature of the release information ( version-latest.properties.sig , OpenSSL, public key embedded in the published script) and the SHA-256 of both files against it, runs the stages of bootstrap/install.sh ( packages , toolchains , binary --binary , core ) behind spinners, then the setup wizard. There is no custom menu: it installs everything the wizard's defaults call for. Log: ~/.cache/bxrig/install.log . No human input: ... | bash -s -- --yes [--answers FILE] [--channel stable|beta] [--no-wizard] . --yes never asks (it needs passwordless sudo or a primed sudo -v ), the wizard then runs bxrig init --answers FILE --yes or, without a file, bxrig init --defaults --yes (the wizard's default answers). --dry-run shows the banner and checks and does nothing. --base-url or BXRIG_BASE_URL points elsewhere. Exit 1 on any failure (nothing is installed after a failed checksum), 2 when you decline. --source SPEC ( BXRIG_SOURCE , decided 2026-11-18): stable (default), beta (= --channel beta ) or github:OWNER/REPO@REF (REF a branch, tag or commit; github:@REF and github:REF mean ortus-boxlang/BxRig ; OWNER and REPO [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ , REF [A-Za-z0-9._/@+-]+ with no leading dash, no .. , no leading or trailing slash; bad values and a --channel that disagrees exit 1). The github source skips the signed release: it is UNSIGNED (warning; --yes or the typed word unsigned at a terminal, else exit 2 before any download), downloads codeload.github.com/OWNER/REPO/tar.gz/REF ( GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN as a header through a curl config on stdin, never printed or logged; refuses paths outside the top folder), runs the tree's own bootstrap/install.sh stages ( binary --yes --force builds from the tree's src/Main.bx ), then the wizard from that binary. --dry-run with a github source downloads and unpacks it, prints the resolved commit and the tree's install.sh --dry-run plan, installs nothing. The source and the commit (the pax header git archive writes into the tarball) go to ~/.cache/bxrig/install.log and ~/.local/share/bxrig/install-source ; bxrig update does not read that file (the binary differs from the channel's, so update check says an update exists and update apply --yes would replace the build). A github source compiles bxrig, so unless the user chose a MatchBox it passes --matchbox-from-source (the manifest branch, bxrig ) to the toolchains stage; --snapshot is passed as given and the binary stage then stops at the capability check (never a silent switch). MatchBox options (decided 2026-11-18, see 14.1): --snapshot ( BXRIG_MATCHBOX_CHANNEL=snapshot ), --matchbox-branch REF ( BXRIG_MATCHBOX_BRANCH ), --matchbox-repo OWNER/NAME ( BXRIG_MATCHBOX_REPO , ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ , needs a branch) and --matchbox-from-source (= --matchbox-branch bxrig ) are validated (bad values and --snapshot with a branch exit 1) and passed through to the toolchains stage; the stable path with the prebuilt binary needs no capable MatchBox, so its stages are unchanged. Channels and S3 ( downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/bxrig/ ): stable/ (a v* tag), beta/ (every push to development , the bleeding edge), each with bxrig-linux-x86_64 , .sha256 , bootstrap.tar.gz , .sha256 and version-latest.properties ( version , commit , sha256 , channel , builtAt ); snapshots/<version>-<sha>/ keeps every beta build and releases/<version>/ every stable one (uploads never delete). CI job 6 publishes when the AWS secrets exist ( AWS_ACCESS_KEY , AWS_ACCESS_SECRET ). update check [--notify] : compares the running binary's SHA-256 with the channel's version-latest.properties ; exit 10 when an update is available, 0 when current, 5 when the server is unreachable; also counts pending system updates ( checkupdates ). update apply [--yes] downloads the channel's binary, verifies its SHA-256 against its .sha256 and the signed release information, and replaces the installed binary atomically (exit 5 on a mismatch or a bad signature, the old binary stays). update channel [stable|beta] shows or sets the channel ( ~/.config/bxrig/update.json ; the wizard asks update_channel , default stable). update notifications on|off|status manages a daily user timer bxrig-update-check.timer that runs update check --notify and shows a notification ( noctalia msg notification-show , else notify-send ); the wizard asks update_notifications , default on. system update [--yes] takes a snapshot first when snapper or timeshift is present, then sudo pacman -Syu --noconfirm and, with yay, yay -Sua --noconfirm . The menu has Settings entries for check, apply, both channels, notifications on and off, and system update. Signing (owner decision 2026-11-13: sign the installer and update): CI signs every version-latest.properties and install.sh with Ed25519 ( openssl pkeyutl -sign -rawin ) using the secret BXRIG_SIGNING_KEY ; the properties carry sha256 (binary) and bootstrap_sha256 (bundle). The public key is keys/release.pub (made with scripts/gen-signing-key.sh ), embedded into the binary ( bootstrap/gen-releasekey.sh writes src/bxrig/ReleaseKey.bx ) and into the published install.sh (CI replaces @@PUBKEY_B64@@ ). With a key a missing or invalid signature, or a file that does not match the signed hash, stops the install or update before anything changes (exit 1 for the installer, 5 for update ); without a key (a development build) only SHA-256 is checked. Limit: the very first curl | bash still trusts the script it downloads (TLS and the bucket), so the signature protects the files the script fetches and every later update; verify install.sh.sig by hand with keys/release.pub for a stricter first install. system updates [--json] (read only, for the System bar panel): { total, repo_count, aur_count, packages: [ { name, old, new, repo } ], needs_reboot, reboot_pending, reboot_stale, reboot_reasons, last_update, last_update_epoch, last_update_ago, aur_helper, aur_error, snapshot_tool } . Repository rows come from checkupdates (exit 0 rows, 2 none, 1 error), AUR rows from yay -Qua or paru -Qua (no helper: none, not an error); repo of a package is repo or aur . Restart rule: reboot_pending when a waiting update replaces a kernel (linux and its lts, zen, hardened, rt, cachyos flavours, not headers, docs or driver modules), systemd, glibc, linux-firmware, a microcode package or the NVIDIA driver; reboot_stale when /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r) is gone; needs_reboot is either. Exit 0 always except 4 (no pacman, no checkupdates , or checkupdates failed). Class SystemUpdates ; the parsers are Pacman.parseUpgrades , Pacman.pendingUpdates and Aur.pendingUpdates ( Aur.updateHelper is yay, else paru; installs still use yay). system update [--repo|--aur|--all] [--yes] [--dry-run] : a snapshot first (snapper, else timeshift, else a note that there is none), then sudo pacman -Syu --noconfirm ( --repo ), the AUR helper -Sua --noconfirm ( --aur , yay else paru; exit 4 without one) or both ( --all , the default). Without --yes the plan is printed (exit 2), --dry-run shows it and exits 0; two scopes together are a usage error (2). Text mode prints [n/N] command as each step starts; the data of a run carries needs_reboot (the kernel that runs was replaced). Theme format: a folder in the colors.toml theme format, so themes move both ways: colors.toml , optional neovim.lua , optional backgrounds/ (the first file is the wallpaper). Both colors.toml shapes are read: the named one ( accent background foreground selection muted red green yellow blue magenta cyan bright_* , mode = "dark"|"light" ) and the older color0..color15 one. The named shape maps to the 16 ANSI slots: black is background , white is foreground , bright black is muted , bright white is bright_foreground . A missing required key or a value that is not #rrggbb rejects the whole theme. Light or dark is the file's mode , else the background luminance (above 0.4 is light).
