Exit: 0 done, 2 plan or bad usage, 4 precondition (bad name or version, KVM unusable, no engine, no terminal to choose a Windows version on, GPU not possible), 6 a command failed. Two kinds, any number of each. Every VM has a name ( [a-z0-9-] , up to 31) and a record in ~/.config/bxrig/vms/NAME.json (mode 600). Windows is dockurr/windows ; a Linux desktop is LinuxServer's lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:TAG . The container is bxrig-vm-NAME , labelled io.bxrig.vm . The first Windows is named windows . The engine is the one bxrig db engine chose (Podman by default). Where things live (documented for the user in docs/guides/vms.md ): data in ~/.local/share/bxrig/vms/NAME ( storage is the Windows disk, config is the Linux desktop's home folder), the record above, the password in the keyring as BXRIG_VM_<NAME>_PASSWORD ( bxrig secrets ), an app-menu launcher ~/.local/share/applications/bxrig-vm-NAME.desktop (runs vm open NAME ), and a shared folder: ~/Windows (drive Z:) or ~/Shared ( /config/Shared ), or --share=none . remove deletes the container, the data, the password, the record and the launcher; the shared folder is never deleted; --keep-data keeps data, password and record. size is du of the data folder; the images are in the engine ( podman image ls ). Security: ports bind to 127.0.0.1 only (the webtop terminal has passwordless sudo; the Windows web viewer and RDP are for you). The password is generated (16 random bytes), stored in the keyring, and reaches the container through an env file (mode 600) that is deleted right after run . The default admin password of dockur is never used. Ports: Linux 3001 upward (HTTPS, a self-signed certificate: accept it once); Windows web viewer 8006 upward and RDP 3389 upward (TCP and UDP); each VM takes the first port no record uses and nothing listens on. Windows: --version takes any dockur VERSION value (25, vm versions windows ). Without it at a terminal, a picker shows ten choices with sizes and notes (11 Pro, 11 LTSC, 11 Enterprise, 10 Pro, 10 LTSC, Tiny11, Tiny11 Core, Tiny10, Server 2025 and 2022; the Tiny builds are marked UNOFFICIAL); with no terminal it exits 4 (a script passes --version ; with --json the picker text goes to the terminal device, never stdout). Defaults: RAM half the machine (4G to 8G), CPUs half (2 to 8), disk 64G. Run: --device /dev/kvm --device /dev/net/tun --cap-add NET_ADMIN --stop-timeout 120 , env VERSION RAM_SIZE CPU_CORES DISK_SIZE USERNAME PASSWORD . The install downloads the ISO inside the container on the first start (3 to 8 GB) and takes a while; you need your own Windows license (dockur uses generic trial keys that do not activate). open starts the VM if needed, waits for RDP, then runs the first FreeRDP client found ( sdl-freerdp3 , sdl-freerdp , xfreerdp3 , xfreerdp , wlfreerdp3 , wlfreerdp ) with /args-from:file:PATH : a mode 600 file holding /v: /u: /p: /cert:ignore +clipboard /dynamic-resolution /title: (and /f ), so the password is never on a command line; the file is removed after 15 seconds. While Windows is still installing, open says so and points at open --web (the browser viewer). Linux: 21 tags from the webtop page (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch: xfce, kde, mate, i3, and lxqt for Ubuntu; Alpine with the upstream latest tag as alpine-xfce ); default ubuntu-xfce . The dev tag and the deprecated Enterprise Linux tags are not offered; KDE tags are Wayland only. Run: --shm-size 1gb , env PUID PGID TZ CUSTOM_USER=bxrig PASSWORD , -v data:/config . Rootless Podman maps the container's root to you, so PUID and PGID are 0 there (files stay yours); Docker uses your ids. --cpus and --memory map to the engine flags. When the host has no IPv6 ( /proc/sys/net/ipv6 missing) the container also gets DISABLE_IPV6=true , because the image's nginx otherwise fails on listen [::] (found by running the real image; doctor notes it). GPU (Linux desktops, opt-in): intel and amd add --device /dev/dri (needs it to exist); auto does that when /dev/dri exists and nothing otherwise; nvidia follows the webtop docs: Docker gets --runtime nvidia --gpus all --device /dev/nvidia-modeset , Podman gets CDI ( --device nvidia.com/gpu=all --device /dev/nvidia-modeset ). The Alpine tags refuse NVIDIA. doctor reports /dev/dri , the NVIDIA driver version (the docs ask for 580 or newer) and nvidia-ctk . Windows has no GPU option. Wizard and menu: two optional questions after the databases: vm_windows (none or one of the ten, with descriptions) and vm_linux (none or six tags); they become optional steps vm create windows --version=V and vm create linux desktop --tag=T , and add the Podman install when no engine answer was given. The menu has a Virtual machines entry (list, sizes, doctor, the two version tables). Verified and not: tested against fake Podman and Docker (every run argument, files, modes, ports, passwords, launchers, exit codes) in tests/vm-test.sh and tests/init_plan_test.bxs . Also run for real (2026-11-13, a sandbox with Docker 29.9.2, no KVM, no IPv6, running as root): vm create linux with the real lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-xfce image through bxrig : the published 127.0.0.1:3001 answers 401 without credentials, 200 with the generated password and 401 with a wrong one; the shared folder works both ways; start , stop , status , size , info , open (browser launch only) and remove behave. Never run: Windows (no /dev/kvm here), Podman, a non-root user (so PUID and file ownership are untested), GPUs, FreeRDP. Unverified on a real machine: Windows booting under rootless Podman ( /dev/kvm , /dev/net/tun , NET_ADMIN ), RDP through the published 127.0.0.1 port (dockur documents the container's own IP too), dockur on a Btrfs disk (CachyOS default; not checked in its README), webtop under rootless Podman with PUID 0 and as a non-root Docker user, the NVIDIA paths (driver 580 or newer from a .run file per the docs, whether CachyOS's packaged driver counts, CDI on Podman, the Arch package name nvidia-container-toolkit ), and the FreeRDP argument file ( /args-from:file: read from the FreeRDP 3 source, the client binary names are a best guess). 13.34 The menu, package search and remove (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) Menu skeleton. bxrig menu has these sections: Apps, Setup wizard (re-run, prefilled) , Install, Remove, Appearance, Trigger, Setup, Update, Develop (BoxLang, databases, virtual machines, containers, the editor), Agent, Learn, About, System. A number the battery does not report is -1 . The rest of data : on_ac (a Mains or USB-C supply is online), profile , lid ( default|suspend|hibernate|lock|ignore|mixed|custom ), lid_battery , lid_ac , charge_limit_supported , power_profiles_daemon , upower . Values come from sysfs ( energy_now / power_now or charge_now / current_now , *_full , *_full_design , cycle_count ). lid [battery|ac] suspend|hibernate|lock|ignore writes the logind drop-in /etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/50-bxrig-lid.conf with sudo install -Dm644 : HandleLidSwitch is the action on battery, HandleLidSwitchExternalPower the action on AC power, HandleLidSwitchDocked=ignore . Without battery or ac both get the action. The side that is not named keeps its value, or suspend (the systemd default) when there is no drop-in, and both lines are always written so the AC line never follows the battery one by accident. It is a plan (exit 2) without --yes , and logind reads it from the next login or reboot (logind is not restarted: that would end the session). A plan for hibernate warns when hibernation is not ready. hibernate [--yes] runs the readiness checks first and exits 4 with the reasons when one fails: disk swap at least the size of RAM ( /proc/swaps , zram does not count), resume= (and resume_offset= for a swap file) on the kernel command line, and the kernel offering the disk state ( /sys/power/state ) without secure boot lockdown ( /sys/kernel/security/lockdown ). Ready: a plan (exit 2) until --yes , then systemctl hibernate --no-block (without --no-block the call would wait until the machine wakes up). The initramfs resume hook cannot be read reliably and is not checked. doctor shows the same checks as hibernation (swap), resume and hibernate-kernel . charge-limit [PERCENT|off|status] [--yes] uses the kernel attribute charge_control_end_threshold of each BAT* (Linux ABI sysfs-class-power : "a battery percentage level, above which charging will stop"; 0 to 100, drivers round to what the hardware supports). PERCENT is 40 to 100. It writes /etc/systemd/system/bxrig-charge-limit.service (a oneshot that writes the value at boot and after suspend, hibernate and hybrid sleep, because some firmware resets it) with sudo install , then daemon-reload , enable --now and restart . off (or 100) disables and removes the unit and writes 100 to the attribute. status is information (exit 0, supported , limit , persisted ). On a laptop whose battery has no such attribute PERCENT and off exit 4. A plan (exit 2) without --yes . Not verified on real hardware (the fake sysfs of power-test.sh only). setup installs and enables power-profiles-daemon and upower ( sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm , sudo systemctl enable --now ). On a machine without a battery it does nothing (exit 0, skipped: "no battery" ) unless --force . The init plan has an optional power-setup step behind the answer power_setup ; no wizard question exists yet. doctor checks battery, the two daemons, the lid action, zram, and (laptops only) the hibernation checks and whether the battery has a charge limit. Problems are reported, never fixed silently. Not built: configuring hibernation (resume offset, initramfs hook) and TLP; battery display and brightness stay with Noctalia and powerdevil. CachyOS ships no laptop power tooling ( cachyos-settings pulls zram, ananicy, inxi, iw, wireless-regdb), so this is ours. Menu: Setup > Power. Verified: tests/power-test.sh (fake sysfs, /proc/swaps , command line, /sys/power , lockdown, meminfo, powerprofilesctl, systemctl, sudo, pacman). Not verified on a real laptop. 13.65 Input devices: Apple Magic and Logitech (decided with the owner 2026-11-17) bxrig input status|offer|apple|logitech|undo|doctor|gestures . doctor and gestures are the older commands of 13.29 and keep working. The rest is bxrig.Input ; detection is bxrig.InputDevices . Detection needs no root and no external tool. It reads /sys/bus/hid/devices ( uevent : HID_ID = bus, vendor, product; HID_NAME ; the bus is 0005 Bluetooth, 0003 USB), then /sys/class/input for what the HID scan missed, then bluetoothctl devices (paired devices that are not connected now) and upower (a battery the kernel did not give), when those tools exist. A device is Apple when the vendor is 05AC and the name has "Magic" in it (the Mac's own keyboard is not listed), Logitech when the vendor is 046D . No product id is hard-coded. Kinds, from the name (a guess): apple-mouse , apple-trackpad , apple-keyboard , logitech-mouse , logitech-keyboard , logitech-receiver , other . A receiver's several HID interfaces collapse into one row. Battery comes first from the kernel ( power_supply/*/capacity under the HID device), then upower; -1 is unknown. Drivers ( hid_magicmouse , hid_logitech_dj , hid_logitech_hidpp ) are loaded , built-in , available ( modinfo finds it) or absent : /sys/module/NAME/initstate exists only for a loaded module, a module directory without it is built in, and /sys/bus/hid/drivers/DRIVER means the driver is registered. lsmod is not used: it never lists a built-in driver (the old doctor said "not loaded" for one). status [--json] : data.devices[] ( id , name , kind , vendor , vendor_id , product_id , transport , battery , battery_status , battery_source kernel|upower , connected , source hid|input|bluetooth , gaming ), data.drivers , data.helpers ( solaar , piper , libratbag (the ratbagd program), libinput-gestures , upower : on the PATH or the package installed), data.missing , data.detected . Exit 0. offer [--for=detect|apple|logitech|both|none] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] plans the install of what the devices call for, through the Resolver and the Installer (one sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm for the official packages, yay for AUR ones). Logitech detected: solaar (the Linux Logi Options+; installs a udev rule with uaccess ), plus libratbag and piper when a mouse is a gaming mouse by its name (G-series, G Pro, Superlight, Lightspeed or "Gaming": the plan says it is a guess). Apple detected: libinput-gestures (AUR) when a Magic Trackpad is found or --for=apple is given and the desktop is not Plasma (swipes only; a Magic Mouse has no touchpad gestures here), and upower for the battery. --for replaces detection: detect is the default. logiops is not offered (owner decision). Without --yes it is a plan (exit 2); --dry-run exits 0; nothing to offer, or everything installed, exits 0. What it installed is remembered in ~/.local/state/bxrig/input-helpers.json . undo [--yes] [--dry-run] removes only the packages offer installed ( sudo pacman -Rns --noconfirm ; your settings in ~/.config stay) and the modprobe.d file apple wrote ( sudo rm -f ). A plan until --yes ; exit 4 when there is nothing recorded. apple [--scroll-speed=N] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] : the devices, the driver state, the Bluetooth service, upower, and the module options the kernel shows in /sys/module/hid_magicmouse/parameters ( scroll_speed , scroll_acceleration , emulate_scroll_wheel , emulate_3button ). Exit 4 when the kernel has no hid_magicmouse driver (the report is still printed). --scroll-speed=N takes a whole number from 0 to 63 (the range param_set_scroll_speed accepts in drivers/hid/hid-magicmouse.c , kernel default 32; anything else is exit 2) and writes /etc/modprobe.d/bxrig-magicmouse.conf ( options hid_magicmouse scroll_speed=N ) with sudo install -Dm644 : a plan (exit 2) until --yes . It applies the next time the module loads (reconnect or reboot). A built-in driver does not read modprobe.d : the plan and the result then say to add hid_magicmouse.scroll_speed=N to the kernel command line. A file with that name that BxRig did not write is never replaced (exit 8). Nothing else is written, and no sysfs value is changed. logitech [--json] : receivers and devices (with battery), the two Logitech drivers, whether 42-logitech-unify-permissions.rules (shipped by the solaar package) is installed, and, when Solaar is installed, solaar show (the lines of the form 1: NAME are counted as paired devices: the layout of Solaar's text is not verified). Exit 0. No gesture writer. Hyprland's native gesture syntax changed between versions (0.51 keys, the Lua config since 0.55) and is not verified here, so gestures stay with libinput-gestures ( input gestures , 13.29). Plasma has its own touchpad gestures in System Settings. Wizard: the Input page asks input_devices ( detect default, none , apple , logitech , both ); it is shown only when a relevant device is detected or the Mac-style keys are on. The init plan adds the optional step input-devices : bxrig input offer --for=CHOICE --yes (nothing for none ). Not verified on real hardware: Magic Trackpad 2, Magic Mouse 2 (and USB-C), an MX Master. Verified with a fake sysfs and fake tools in tests/input-test.sh , tests/input_devices_test.bxs and tests/macextras-test.sh . Unverified facts (see the research page): that upower shows these batteries (the kernel's own power_supply is read first), that Solaar, libratbag and logiops do not conflict on one device (use one tool per device), whether hid_magicmouse is built in on CachyOS kernels, Plasma gesture paths. 13.38 Time zone (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) bxrig time status|zone|sync|auto|ntp . zone shows the zone, zone --list lists them, zone ZONE sets it ( sudo timedatectl set-timezone , validated against timedatectl list-timezones ; exit 4 for an unknown one). sync sets the zone once from your IP address with tzupdate (AUR, installed first when missing): the command to run after you land. ntp on|off is timedatectl set-ntp . Everything that changes the system is a plan (exit 2) without --yes . auto on|off|status follows your location by itself. It installs geoclue (extra) and automatic-timezoned (AUR, 2.0.163). The AUR package ships no systemd unit and the daemon needs GeoClue to run without an agent (its README), so auto on writes /etc/systemd/system/automatic-timezoned.service (runs as root, which may set the zone without a polkit rule) and /etc/geoclue/conf.d/90-bxrig-timezone.conf ( [agent] whitelist= empty; [automatic-timezoned] allowed, system, any user), then systemctl enable --now . auto off disables the service and removes both files. The plan states the privacy tradeoff: GeoClue looks up your location online (Wi-Fi networks or IP address). Not verified on a real machine: the geoclue drop-in being read from conf.d , the daemon getting a location without an agent, and tzupdate flags (we run it with none). If the zone does not change, journalctl -u automatic-timezoned . time format [FORMAT|default] (2026-11-17) is the bar clock's text: Noctalia date format tokens (a {:%H:%M} field is unwrapped; text without a % is read as a MMM d - HH:mm pattern), default %b %-d - %H:%M ("Nov 5 - 04:00"). It is an appearance -style setting (acts at once, --dry-run ) and rewrites the Noctalia config through BarSettings ; the bxrig/clock plugin reads it as its format setting. Menu: Setup > Time. Verified: tests/time-test.sh (fake timedatectl, systemctl, sudo, pacman, yay, tzupdate). 13.39 Toggles, DNS, kernels and security (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) bxrig toggle stay-awake [on|off] runs noctalia msg caffeine-enable|disable|toggle (Noctalia IPC docs). Without Noctalia it exits 4 (on Plasma use System Settings > Power Management). Stay awake holds the screensaver and the lock off too (both are Noctalia idle behaviors, 13.66). bxrig dns [cloudflare|google|quad9|dhcp|custom IP[,IP...]] lists or sets the DNS servers of the active NetworkManager connections (loopback, bridge, tunnel and container devices are skipped) with nmcli connection modify NAME ipv4.dns ... ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes ipv6.dns ... ipv6.ignore-auto-dns yes , then connection up NAME . dhcp clears them. A plan (exit 2) without --yes ; a bad IP exits 2. bxrig kernel list|install NAME|remove NAME . list shows the running kernel, the installed kernel packages and the linux-cachyos* kernels you could add (nvidia, zfs, rc and headers packages are left out). install is sudo pacman -S --needed NAME NAME-headers (the name must match linux(-[a-z0-9]+)* and exist in the repos, else exit 4 or 2). remove refuses the running kernel (judged from uname -r and the package suffix) and the last installed kernel (exit 4). It never edits the bootloader and never picks the default: the boot entries come from the kernel packages' hooks and you choose in the boot menu. bxrig security status|fingerprint|fido2|ssh-server|passwordless-sudo . Guards: only /etc/pam.d/sudo is ever changed (never login, SDDM or the lock screen); the line is auth sufficient pam_fprintd.so or auth sufficient pam_u2f.so cue inserted before the first auth line and marked with a # bxrig KIND comment, so your password still works without the reader or key; a file with no auth line is left alone (exit 4); the original is kept once as /etc/pam.d/sudo.bxrig-backup ; off removes exactly the marked line; running on twice adds one line. fingerprint enroll runs fprintd-enroll ; fido2 register runs pamu2fcfg into ~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys , and fido2 on refuses (exit 4) until that file exists. passwordless-sudo on writes /etc/sudoers.d/50-bxrig-nopasswd ( USER ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL , user from $USER` and checked against `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*$ ) only after visudo -cf passes, with mode 440; off removes it. ssh-server on|off installs openssh and runs systemctl enable|disable --now sshd.service . Everything is a plan (exit 2) without --yes , and --dry-run prints the exact line or file. Agents: the Agent menu runs ai launch NAME ; there is no separate agent command. Menu: Trigger > Toggle (stay awake), Setup > DNS, Security, Time, Kernel. Verified: tests/tweaks-test.sh and tests/security-test.sh (fake nmcli, pacman, noctalia, uname, visudo, sudo and fake /etc/pam.d and /etc/sudoers.d ). Not verified on a real machine: PAM behavior with a real reader or key, nmcli on your connection names, kernel removal. 13.40 The command reference and bxrig help (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) One source: docs/reference/cli.json holds, for every command, its group, a one-sentence summary, its usage lines, examples, whether it needs --yes ( mutates ) and an optional note. bootstrap/gen-docs.sh writes docs/reference/commands.md (the docs page: flags, exit codes, the JSON envelope, an index by group, then every command with usage and examples) and src/bxrig/HelpData.bx (the same data inside the binary). bxrig help (and bare bxrig ) lists every command by group with its summary; bxrig help NAME prints the summary, usage, whether --yes is needed, examples and notes; --json returns the same data; an unknown name exits 2. Drift checks: gen-docs.sh --check fails when a command in src/Main.bx has no entry, an entry has no command, a usage line does not start with its command, an example names no real command, a summary does not end in a full stop, or the text contains an em dash. The usage lines of older commands are copied from the usage text in src/Main.bx ; the newer classes ( appearance , display , power , time , toggle , dns , kernel , security ) print their own usage, so their entries are written by hand and must be updated with the class. Verified: tests/help-test.sh (the groups, a command, JSON, unknown, and that the generated files are current). 13.41 NAS as a first-class namespace (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) bxrig nas keeps every NAS you use in ~/.config/bxrig/nas.json (name, host, protocol smb or nfs , user, optional SMB version, and the shares you mounted). discover browses the network with avahi-browse -rtp _smb._tcp and _nfs._tcp (IPv4 only). setup installs cifs-utils nfs-utils smbclient avahi nss-mdns rsync and enables avahi-daemon (a plan without --yes ; every tool was checked in the Arch repos and its binary exists after install). add NAME --host=H needs --user and a password for SMB ( --ask-password , typed hidden, or --password-file=F ); the password goes to the keyring as BXRIG_NAS_<NAME>_PASSWORD and never into nas.json . NFS needs neither. Names are ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$ . shares NAME lists SMB shares with smbclient -g -L HOST -A AUTHFILE (the auth file is a private temp file, deleted after; no password on a command line; IPC$ and other hidden shares are dropped) or NFS exports with showmount -e --no-headers . mount|unmount NAME SHARE mounts at ~/NAS/NAME/LEAF ( BXRIG_NAS_HOME overrides) with sudo mount -t cifs|nfs ; the SMB options are credentials=/etc/bxrig/nas/NAME.cred,uid,gid,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0600,dir_mode=0700 plus vers= only when you set one (otherwise the kernel negotiates the highest version both sides support). The credentials file is root-only (mode 600) because mount.cifs reads it as root ; the plan says so. auto on|off NAME SHARE writes <escaped-path>.mount and .automount units to /etc/systemd/system ( Options=...,nofail , TimeoutSec=20 , TimeoutIdleSec=600 , wanted by multi-user.target ), runs daemon-reload and enable --now , so a sleeping NAS never blocks login. off disables and removes them; a NAS with automatic mounts is not removed (exit 4) until they are off. test NAME [SHARE] checks: reachable (TCP 445 or 2049), signed in or exports readable, mounted ( findmnt ), writable (a probe file), free space. Exit 4 when a check fails. sync NAME SRC --to=SHARE[/PATH] is a plain rsync -a mirror to a mounted share. Nothing is deleted from the NAS unless you add --delete , and the plan says so in capitals. use NAME SHARE [--path=bxrig-backup] records targets.nas-NAME in ~/.config/bxrig/backup.json ( {type: nas, nas, share, path} ); backup data setup reads it. Verified: tests/nas-test.sh with fake avahi-browse, smbclient, showmount, findmnt, rsync, sudo and a fake /etc . Not verified on a real Synology: DSM share permissions, SMB signing, NFS export options, nss-mdns name resolution. 13.42 refresh and reinstall (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) No factory reset. bxrig refresh COMPONENT puts managed config back to what BxRig ships and never installs a package. Components: hyprland (runs keys apply , appearance apply , display apply ; with --starter also the starter hyprland.lua ), noctalia ( theme set CURRENT , appearance apply , noctalia msg config-reload ; with --starter also the Noctalia starter files), terminals (the starter config of each installed terminal, then the theme includes), shell ( starship.toml , the shell init and the line in .zshrc or .bashrc ), nvim ( editor refresh ), theme ( theme set CURRENT , appearance apply ), all , and list . Semantics are the config service's: a clean file is left alone, a missing or outdated one is written, a file you edited ( drifted ) is kept and reported, and --force overwrites it after a backup ( config history , config restore ). A link or special file in the way blocks (exit 8 in the service, shown as blocked). Without --yes it prints the plan and exits 2; --dry-run exits 0. reinstall is init --rerun : the way to install packages again. Verified: tests/refresh-test.sh (temp home, fake bxrig that logs the commands, a fake terminal): plan and dry run write nothing, files are written, a second run rewrites nothing clean, edits are kept, --force overwrites and takes a backup, each component runs its commands. 13.43 Backups: the config layer (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) Three layers, one command. bxrig backup config (your BxRig setup), backup snapshots (the system, Btrfs with snapper) and backup data (your files, restic) are built in that order; backup send and backup export move any of them, and timemachine shows them all. This section is the config layer; the others are added below as they land. A snapshot is ~/.local/share/bxrig/backups/config/ID.tar.gz (mode 600) plus ID.json . ID is yyyyMMddTHHmmss (with -xxxx when two land in the same second). Inside: files/ (paths under your home), packages.txt ( pacman -Qqe ), foreign.txt ( pacman -Qqm ), meta.json , and secrets.bxs only with --with-secrets (the output of bxrig secrets export , encrypted with a passphrase you type). What is tracked (under your home): .config/bxrig , hypr , noctalia , ghostty , kitty , foot , alacritty , starship.toml , nvim , btop , fish , git , mimeapps.list , xdg-terminals.list , .zshrc , .bashrc , .gitconfig , .ssh/config . backup config add|remove PATH changes the list (stored in backup.json ); SSH keys, gnupg , .. and absolute paths are refused. .git , node_modules and *.log are skipped. Restore shows a plan (which files are created or replaced; exit 2 without --yes ), takes a safety snapshot of the present first, then copies the files back ( --only=PATH limits it). --packages installs the explicit packages that are missing and exist in the repositories with sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm ; AUR and local ones are listed for yay , never installed from here. diff ID compares a snapshot with now (files same, changed, missing, and missing packages). Automatic: auto is on by default. Before update apply , system update , init , reinstall and refresh (with --yes , never --dry-run ) a snapshot is taken quietly, with the reason before <command> ; it never stops the command. The newest 30 are kept ( prune --keep=N ). Verified: tests/backup-config-test.sh (temp home, fake pacman, sudo and bxrig). Not verified: a restore on a different machine. backup snapshots (system snapshots). Btrfs root: snapper. setup [--home] installs snapper snap-pac (and grub-btrfs only when GRUB is in use), creates the root config ( snapper -c root create-config / ; --home adds /home ), sets the timeline to 5 hourly, 7 daily, 2 weekly, 1 monthly, 0 yearly ( snapper set-config TIMELINE_* ), and enables snapper-timeline.timer and snapper-cleanup.timer (and grub-btrfsd.service ). snap-pac takes a snapshot before and after every pacman transaction through its own hooks. Other filesystems: it installs Timeshift (rsync mode), which takes full copies and needs one visit to its window to pick a disk. list reads snapper --jsonout -c CONFIG list (snapshot 0, the live system, is left out); create [--description=T] is snapper create --description T -p ; delete ID ; changes ID is snapper status ID..0 ; restore ID PATH is snapper undochange ID..0 PATH (files changed since are replaced, files that did not exist then are removed, so the plan says so). There is no automatic whole-system rollback : rolling back a Btrfs root depends on your subvolume layout, so you boot the snapshot from the GRUB menu and follow the Arch wiki, or restore folders with restore . Everything that changes the system is a plan without --yes . Not verified on real Btrfs: the JSON shape of snapper --jsonout list (the parser accepts a bare array or an object holding one array), the timers, undochange . Tested with fakes in tests/backup-snapshots-test.sh . backup data (your files, restic). A target is a place a restic repository lives: local (a path), nas (made by nas use , at ~/NAS/NAME/SHARE/PATH ), sftp ( sftp:user@host:/path ; port as sftp:-p N user@host:/path ), rest ( rest:URL ), s3 ( s3:ENDPOINT/BUCKET/PATH , AWS when no endpoint; works for DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi, MinIO), b2 ( b2:BUCKET:PATH ), azure ( azure:CONTAINER:/PATH ), gs ( gs:BUCKET:/PATH , with GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID and GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS as the project and the service-account file) and rclone ( rclone:REMOTE:PATH ; FTP and any rclone service). The environment variable names ( AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID , AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY , AWS_DEFAULT_REGION , B2_ACCOUNT_ID , B2_ACCOUNT_KEY , AZURE_ACCOUNT_NAME , AZURE_ACCOUNT_KEY , RESTIC_REST_USERNAME , RESTIC_REST_PASSWORD ) and the address forms were read from restic's own documentation; the flags used ( -r via RESTIC_REPOSITORY , backup --tag --exclude --exclude-caches --one-file-system , forget --keep-daily|weekly|monthly --prune , snapshots --json , ls --json , restore --target --include , check --read-data-subset ) from the installed restic 0.19.1. Keys go straight to the keyring ( target add ... --ask-keys , typed hidden, or --keys-file with KEY=VALUE lines) as BXRIG_BACKUP_<TARGET>_<KEY> ; the repository password is generated at init (24 random bytes, hex) and kept as BXRIG_BACKUP_<TARGET>_PASSWORD , with a reminder that losing it loses the backups. restic is started with these in its environment , never on a command line, and no key is written to backup.json . run backs up the include list (default Projects code dev Documents .ssh , only the ones that exist) skipping the exclude list (default node_modules target .gradle __pycache__ .venv venv .cache .next *.tmp ) and cache folders, on one filesystem, tagged bxrig ; list , files , restore ID --to=DIR [--include=PATH] (into a folder you name, never over your files by itself), verify [--deep] ( restic check , --read-data-subset 5% ), forget (retention 7 daily, 4 weekly, 6 monthly by default, retention changes it; deletes older backups for good, so it is a plan first), schedule hourly|daily|off (user units bxrig-backup.service and .timer : ConditionACPower=true so it skips on battery, Persistent=true to catch up, a random delay up to 15 minutes; a failed scheduled run sends a Noctalia or notify-send notification). An unmounted NAS share exits 4 with the nas mount command. Verified: tests/backup-data-test.sh with a fake restic that records its arguments and the variables it was given. Not verified against a real cloud account, NAS or restic repository in this environment. backup send and backup export (moving backups). send ID|all --to=TARGET [--from=TARGET] is restic copy into a second repository (a NAS and a cloud bucket, for a 3-2-1 setup): the destination is RESTIC_REPOSITORY , the source goes in RESTIC_FROM_REPOSITORY with RESTIC_FROM_PASSWORD_COMMAND=printenv BXRIG_FROM_PW , so no password is on a command line. restic reads one set of AWS_* , B2_* ... variables, so two repositories that need different values for the same variable (two S3 accounts) are refused (exit 4) with a pointer to rclone sync . export data ID --to=FILE is restic dump --archive tar|zip --target FILE ID PATH (zip when the name ends in .zip ; --path limits it to a folder; an existing file is never overwritten), export config ID --to=FILE.tar.gz copies a config snapshot out as one file. Config snapshots travel with the data backups : ~/.local/share/bxrig/backups/config is in the default include list, so a NAS or cloud target protects them with no extra step. System snapshots are not exportable. Tested in tests/backup-move-test.sh with a fake restic. 13.44 BxTimeMachine, the backup screen (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) bxrig timemachine [--demo] [--local] (also bxrig bxtimemachine ) is BxTimeMachine , a full-screen terminal UI on MatchBox's canvas (the same one as the wizard) over bxrig backup timeline [--json] [--local] , which lists every backup in one structure: rows system (snapper), config (config snapshots), files-NAME (one per data target, from restic snapshots --json ) and mirror-NAME (recorded nas sync runs). A point is { id, time, epoch, label, tier, size } ; tier is by age (hourly up to a day, daily to a week, weekly to 5 weeks, monthly to a year, yearly after). A target that fails is a row with an error (unreachable, not initialized, NAS not mounted), never a failure of the whole timeline; --local leaves out the targets that need the network so the screen opens at once. BXRIG_TIMELINE_FILE injects a timeline (tests); BXRIG_NOW_EPOCH fixes the clock. The screen: places as rows over a time axis (newest on the right; zoom 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 1 year, all; the axis grows to keep the chosen backup in view), points coloured by tier, a guide line through the chosen moment, the chosen backup as a card with the older ones stacked behind it, counts by tier for the place, and the brand gradient with Powered by BoxLang. Keys: left and right (or h l) through time, up and down (k j) between places, plus and minus zoom, enter open, d diff, r restore, e export, s send, n back up now, / filter in the browser, ? help, q or esc leave; the mouse picks a point, a place or a zoom chip and the wheel moves through time. Under 90 by 30 cells it asks for a bigger window. What it runs: it only runs bxrig commands, and every change goes through a plan first : it runs the command with --dry-run , shows the plan, and runs it with --yes only on y . Open: backup data files ID --json , backup config show ID --json or backup snapshots changes N . Restore: backup data restore ID --to=~/Restored/ID [--include=PATH] , backup config restore ID [--only=PATH] or backup snapshots restore N PATH (a folder must be picked first). Export: backup export data|config . Send: backup send ID --from=PLACE --to=PLACE (file backups only; a destination picker). Back up now: backup data run , backup config now or backup snapshots create . Config snapshots reach a NAS or the cloud through the data backups (they are in its include list). --demo shows a made-up timeline (every kind of place and every tier) and runs nothing: plans and results say what the command would have been. tools/record-timemachine.py records the demo in a pseudo-terminal (pyte, Pillow, ffmpeg) into named screenshots and a video. A key, click or scroll returns an intent: {} , { action: "goto", page } , { action: "launch", target } (leave and run that screen, then come back to the same page) or { action: "cli", title, args } . A cli intent first runs the command with --dry-run and shows the output as the plan; only y runs it with --yes , and the result box follows. A development inbox: Mailpit ( axllent/mailpit ) in a container named bxrig-mail , SMTP on 127.0.0.1:1025 , web inbox and REST API on 127.0.0.1:8025 (both ports can be changed; ports are 1024 to 65535 and must differ, else exit 4). Everything is bound to 127.0.0.1 . The engine is the one db engine chose (podman by default). Thrown away on stop. Without --keep the container runs with --rm and no volume, so stop deletes it and its mail. With --keep it runs with --restart unless-stopped , the folder ~/.local/share/bxrig/mail bind-mounted at /data:Z and MP_DATABASE=/data/mailpit.db , so mail survives stop and start. remove deletes the container and the stored mail; --keep-data keeps the folder. start , remove , clear and delete plan first (exit 2 without --yes , --dry-run exits 0); test , open , list , show , env , stop and status act at once. The ports and keep are remembered in mail/meta.json . Container settings: MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY=1 , MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 (an app that logs in works with any user and password, no TLS) and MP_MAX_MESSAGES=5000 , taken from Mailpit's own Docker example. API used (from Mailpit's swagger): GET /api/v1/messages?limit=N ( total , unread , messages[] with ID , From{Name,Address} , To[] , Subject , Created , Size , Attachments as a count, Read , Snippet ), GET /api/v1/message/{ID} ( Text , HTML , Cc , Bcc , Date , Attachments[] with FileName , ContentType , Size ), DELETE /api/v1/messages (all, or a body { "IDs": [...] } ), POST /api/v1/send ( From{Email,Name} , To[{Email}] , Subject , Text ) and GET /view/{ID}.html (opened with xdg-open ). HTTP goes through curl . Without an answer, anything that needs the API exits 4. JSON names differ from the API's on purpose ( mid , sender , sender_address , recipient , subject_line , received , bytes , attachment_count , seen , preview ; for show : to_list , cc_list , bcc_list , sent , body_text , body_html , files[] with file_name , type , bytes ; for test : recipient , subject_line ): MatchBox keeps the capitalisation of the first spelling of a key it sees, so a field called id came out as ID after parsing the API's ID . Fields that do not clash ( total , unread , smtp , web ) keep their names. mail env prints the SMTP settings (host, port, no encryption, no login needed) for a generic list, BoxLang and ColdBox (words only: the exact setting names were not checked), Laravel ( .env ), Spring Boot, Node (nodemailer) and plain environment variables. Control Center page Mail : table of from, received, size, attachment mark and subject; the detail box shows the headers and the wrapped text body of the highlighted message. d plans mail delete ID , c plans mail clear , o runs mail open ID at once, t runs mail test , r reloads. The page reloads itself every 3 seconds (the provider's refreshSeconds() ; ListPage reloads in paint once enough ticks have passed, not while you are typing a filter, and keeps the cursor on the same message by its id ). Providers can also say detailLines() (default 2) to get a taller detail box. Demo data under tui mail --demo . Wizard and menu: one yes or no question mail_catcher (default no) after the databases questions; InitPlan adds the optional step mail-start ( bxrig mail start --yes ), so a missing container engine never stops the plan. Menu: Develop > Mail catcher. Install and the setup wizard (decided with the owner 2026-11-10; install, wizard and the init engine are built, the pages' later commands are not) 14.1 Install bootstrap/install.sh [--yes] [--dry-run] is the one install command. It prints the plan, asks one Proceed? [Y/n] at a terminal (without a terminal it needs --yes , else exit 2; --dry-run exits 0), then runs, in order: packages with yay and Rust, toolchains (mvm, bvm, BoxLang, nvm and Node, MatchBox), the bxrig binary, and the core apps ( bxrig profile-install core --yes ). External installer scripts run without a gate (section 2, rule 8). MatchBox (decided 2026-11-18, replaces the S3 build of the branch head): the toolchains stage installs MatchBox through mvm. Stable by default: mvm install latest , mvm use latest , only when no MatchBox is installed (a re-run leaves an installed one alone). --snapshot or BXRIG_MATCHBOX_CHANNEL=snapshot : mvm install snapshot , mvm use snapshot on every run (mvm skips an unchanged build). --matchbox-branch REF [--matchbox-repo OWNER/NAME] ( BXRIG_MATCHBOX_BRANCH , BXRIG_MATCHBOX_REPO ; the default repo is toolchain.matchbox.repo , the default branch of the alias --matchbox-from-source is toolchain.matchbox.ref , bxrig ): git clone --depth 1 --branch REF , cargo build --release --features bif-tui , installed as $BXRIG_HOME/matchbox/bin/matchbox` with `build.info` (repo, branch, commit, source); it is first on the installer's PATH (never replaces mvm's MatchBox) and is rebuilt only when the repo, the branch or the remote head (`git ls-remote`, unreadable counts as moved) changed. Choosing `--snapshot` removes an earlier branch build; no option leaves it. REF `^[A-Za-z0-9._/@+-]+$ (no leading dash, no .. , no leading or trailing slash) and OWNER/NAME are validated, invalid is exit 2, --snapshot with a branch is exit 2, and values reach git only as argv items. BXRIG_MATCHBOX_FILE=PATH installs a local build instead (source file ). Capability, not version: no check compares the MatchBox version with box.json . Only the stage that compiles bxrig needs a capable MatchBox: the binary stage without --binary (so also the stage of a github source and scripts/setup-local.sh ) runs matchbox probe.bxs , a three line script that creates createObject( "rust", "tui.TUI" ) , draws a frame and prints a marker; a MatchBox built without bif-tui (stable and snapshot today) stops it with exit 1 and This MatchBox (VERSION) cannot compile BxRig ... use --matchbox-branch bxrig , never switching MatchBox on its own. With --binary PATH (the web installer's prebuilt bxrig) any MatchBox is fine; the toolchains stage only notes whether the MatchBox can compile bxrig, and install.sh check prints matchbox: VERSION (compiles BxRig: yes|no) . --snapshot , --matchbox-branch , --matchbox-repo and --matchbox-from-source are accepted by the full install and by toolchains --yes ; --dry-run prints the MatchBox line and step. install.sh check is the read-only report; packages|toolchains|binary|core --yes re-run one stage. Disk (decided 2026-11-18, from a real Arch container run): a single stage needs 5 GB free in $HOME ( MIN_FREE_GB ); the whole install needs 8 GB ( FULL_FREE_GB ), checked up front, so a machine with 5 to 7 GB cannot pass stage 1 and fail at stage 2 after Rust was installed. The 8 GB: Rust about 2.5 GB (6 GB free before, 4 GB after), packages about 1.3 GB (pacman: 1334 MiB), the MatchBox branch build with its cargo target directory about 3 GB, Java, mvm, bvm, BoxLang and the bxrig binary about 0.5 GB, 0.7 GB of headroom. The plan prints Disk: need 8 GB for the whole install, N GB free (ok|not enough) ; the real run exits 1 with Not enough free disk space ... Nothing was changed. before any stage; --dry-run only reports; check prints disk-free: N GB (need 8 for the whole install) . Closing line: the core profile has no apps, so the last stage says Nothing to install. Choose the desktop and apps with \ bxrig init`. and the install ends with Tools installed. Run `bxrig init` for the desktop and apps. (at a terminal: Tools installed. and the wizard starts). **mvm failures:** mvm install is tried three times and its own output is shown; only output with 403, 429 or rate limit gets the rate-limit hint, anything else (a proxy, a TLS-inspecting firewall that mvm does not trust) gets Could not reach GitHub. Behind a corporate proxy or a TLS-inspecting firewall? ... and the branch-build alternative install.sh toolchains --yes --matchbox-branch bxrig`. When the wizard exists the install ends by starting it at a terminal. Required vs optional toolchains (decided 2026-11-10): the install always adds BoxLang (Java 21, bvm, mvm, MatchBox, Rust). nvm and Node.js are no longer part of it; they are the optional JavaScript toolchain: bxrig toolchain node [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] runs the pinned nvm installer from box.json toolchain.nvm (an external script: its URL is in the plan, it adds nvm to your shell startup files) and nvm install lts/* , skipping what is already there. Bun and Deno are catalog apps ( install bun deno ). 14.2 bxrig init A full-screen terminal wizard that asks the questions below, shows a review screen, then runs the matching commands. After the welcome screen it asks how to begin (decided with the owner 2026-11-27): a new install (the whole wizard from the defaults), answers imported from a file (a path typed on the screen, checked by Init.importAnswers ; the answers go over the defaults and the review follows, with a notice that counts what was imported and what this version does not use), or, when there are saved answers, those. --fresh , --rerun and --from=FILE skip the question. WizardApp takes opts.start , opts.presets ( new , saved ) and opts.importer . Answers are saved to ~/.config/bxrig/answers.json (mode 600, written atomically); a re-run starts from the saved answers. bxrig init the wizard (needs a terminal) bxrig init --answers FILE [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] headless: no TUI, the plan from FILE; same --yes / --dry-run rules as every mutating verb bxrig init --print-answers the saved answers The install after the review runs on the wizard's own screen (decided with the owner 2026-11-26): InitRun starts each plan step detached ( Proc.startTo : the output appended to a file, the exit code written to another; no new session, so the sudo ticket made by sudo -v just before is valid; stdin closed), InstallApp and InstallView read them every frame (a bar in the theme's colours, the running step with a spinner, its own (n/m) progress from the package manager, how long since it last printed), v opens the live log, Ctrl+C asks before killing the running step ( Proc.killTree ) and skipping the rest, r runs the failed steps again. One pick-one list with two groups: Network profiles (saved NetworkManager connections of type vpn or wireguard , through nmcli ) and VPN apps (NordVPN, NordLayer, Tailscale, Mullvad). vpn list [--json] the installed providers and profiles with their state; an empty list, exit 0, when nothing is installed (the bar icon hides itself then). data : { providers: [ { id, name, group (profiles|apps), kind, state, connected, location, detail, can_pick, coexist, verified, note } ], connected: [ids], allow_several, install: [ { id, name, install } ] } . state is connected , connecting , disconnected , login (log in first), unavailable (daemon not running) or unknown . A profile's id is nm:NAME . vpn status [NAME] what is connected (one provider with NAME). vpn locations NAME the places it can connect to: { provider, can_pick, current, locations: [ { value, label } ] } with the reserved first entries default (connect as it is) and, where the provider can clear a choice, none (Tailscale: no exit node), then the provider's own list (NordVPN countries, Tailscale exit nodes, Mullvad countries and cities, NordLayer gateways). vpn connect NAME [--location=VALUE] and vpn disconnect [NAME] start or stop a program, so they act at once and take --dry-run (the exception of 2.11). Without a NAME disconnect stops everything that is connected. Catalog split: catalog/apps.json (schema 4) says what an app is; catalog/install/DISTRO.json (schema 1) says how to install it: defaults ( terminal ), names (Arch package name to this distribution's, "" for none needed), repos (extra repositories, each with for packages, a check path under /etc , commands and files ), and apps ( source + targets , and on Arch repo / pkgbuild / aur_targets / script ). extends merges names , apps and defaults from a parent; a child's repos replaces the parent's. ubuntu.json extends debian.json . The theme is a generated file of theme set like the others: ~/.local/share/vicinae/themes/bxrig.toml (meta version 1, name, description, variant; colour keys only from Vicinae's theme parser's RECOGNIZED_KEYS). Vicinae watches the folder; theme set selects it again only while Vicinae is the launcher. Script commands are ~/.local/share/vicinae/scripts/bxrig/*.sh, rewritten by launcher scripts --yes ; a file BxRig no longer offers is deleted, other folders are not touched. Each sets BXRIG to this BxRig (BXRIG_SELF) and runs one command. launcher files [QUERY] opens vicinae://launch/files/search with fallbackText. The Vicinae menu uses vicinae dmenu --placeholder (it has no --prompt). 13.67 BoxLang agents: ai agents (decided with the owner 2026-11-24) bx-agents has a full command line ( bxAgents , every verb on one project: the current folder or --projectRoot ), so BxRig does not repeat it ( AiAgentHub.bx ). It adds only what bx-agents leaves to the machine. Where things live is bx-agents' own convention: an agent's data in ~/.bxagents/<name> (outside the project, so a build never replaces it), the person's settings in ~/.bxagents/Agent.yml . BxRig keeps its list in ~/.config/bxrig/agents.json ( root , default , entries: [ { path, port, added } ] ). Command Does ai agents [list] the projects: every folder of the projects folder with an Agent.yml or Agent.bx , then the ones added by path; name (the top-level name: of Agent.yml, else the folder), port, running, default ai agents install\|update [--snapshot\|--stable] [--yes] [--dry-run] bx-module install bx-agents@snapshot (the default for now), or @VERSION for --stable : the newest ForgeBox version without snapshot (exit 4 while there is none). Then /tmp/boxlang-jars is deleted, always, and the bxrig profile written. update also restarts the agents that run. Plan without --yes ai agents new NAME [flags] bxAgents new NAME [flags] in the projects folder, the terminal handed over (its own wizard). The name: letters, digits, - and _ , not a command word, not taken ai agents NAME VERB [args] bxAgents VERB --projectRoot=PROJECT [args] , exactly as typed (from the raw arguments), the terminal handed over, its exit code. Its flags are not checked against cli.json ai agents start\|stop\|status NAME the user unit bxrig-agent-NAME.service ai agents open NAME / default [NAME] its web page ( xdg-open , only while it runs) / the default agent (for the keyboard shortcut, PR 11b) ai agents dir [PATH] / add PATH / forget NAME [--yes] the projects folder ( BXRIG_AGENTS_DIR , else dir , else ~/Agents ) / a project elsewhere (refused when its name is taken: the data folder is chosen by name) / out of the list, its unit removed, the project and its data kept ai agents profile [--off] the bxrig profile alone Ports: from 8790, one per project path, kept; a freed one is used again. The unit: ExecStartPre=bxAgents build --projectRoot=P --no-banner , then ExecStart=/bin/sh -c "cd .build && BOXLANG_HOME=P/.build/runtime exec boxlang-miniserver --port N --host 127.0.0.1" , with Environment=BXRIG_SELF=PATH (BxRig's full path, for the agent's tools: a user service's PATH may not have ~/.local/bin ) and Restart=on-failure . BOXLANG_HOME is set on the server's line only: set for the whole unit (as in PR 11) it reached the build step too, which then found no bx-agents module (measured, fixed in 11b). Not bxAgents serve : it starts the miniserver and exits 0 (measured), which systemd takes for the end of the service and stops the server with it. Running the miniserver in .build with the miniserver.json the build wrote is what bx-agents' deploy targets do; the flags win over the file. WorkingDirectory is the project, because .build does not exist before the first build and systemd checks the folder first. The jar cache: BoxLang copies module jars to java.io.tmpdir/boxlang-jars ( DynamicClassLoader.copyJarsToTemp , BL-2629) named by path and modification time, and reuses a copy that exists. bx-module install keeps the zip's 1980 dates, so a reinstalled jar would load the old copy (measured: NoMethodException on a method the new jar has). It is deleted after every install ( BXRIG_BOXLANG_JARS names another folder). Test hooks: BXRIG_BXAGENTS (the bxAgents launcher, else BOXLANG_HOME/bin/bxAgents , else the PATH), BXRIG_MINISERVER (boxlang-miniserver, else the PATH), BXRIG_FORGEBOX_API (default https://forgebox.io/api/v1 ). The bxrig profile: in ~/.bxagents/Agent.yml , a marked block ( # >>> BxRig local AI ... , # <<< BxRig local AI <<< ) with profiles.bxrig = { description, provider: openai-compatible, model: ACTIVE, options.baseURL: BASE/v1 } . bx-agents layers that file over every agent at build and at start ( SettingsLayers ), mappings by key, so an agent uses BxRig's model with profile: bxrig . A file with a profiles: of its own is not rewritten (the lines to add are given). ai models use rewrites the block when it is there; it is never added unasked. Checked for real: profile: , providers.openai-compatible.options and a top-level options all reach the local server, from invoke and from the served app. Control Center: ai-boxlang (BoxLang agents, after Agents): ai agents --json ; Enter the chat in a new terminal ( setsid -f TERMINAL bxrig ai agents NAME chat ), o web page, s start or stop, d default, l journalctl --user -u UNIT , i install or update. Bar: the Agents panel's BoxLang tab ( boxlang.luau ). Java's home is not $HOME : bx-agents reads user.home , which comes from the account, so a test that changes HOME sets BXAGENTS_USER_CONFIG too. Tests: tests/ai_agents_test.bxs (pure), tests/ai-agents-test.sh (fake bx-module, bxAgents, systemctl, curl and xdg-open). Checked for real against bx-agents 1.0.0-snapshot (2026-11-24) and BoxLang 1.20.0-snapshot: install, new, build, invoke and models list through the pass-through, the unit's two commands, the served /__bxagents/invoke answering through the bxrig profile. Not yet on a real desktop: the interactive chat hand-over, a real systemd user session, the terminal opened from the Control Center and the bar tab in Noctalia. 13.68 Boxy, the desktop assistant (decided with the owner 2026-11-25) Boxy is a bx-agents project BxRig ships as a template ( templates/agents/boxy/ : Agent.bx , instructions.md , tools/BxRig.bx , packed with the binary). It is an Agent.bx (the class form) because a class can add bx-ai's approval step; an Agent.yml can not for its own tools. Command Does ai agents setup [--no-start] [--yes] [--dry-run] writes the template to PROJECTS/Boxy (refused when Boxy or the folder exists), writes the bxrig profile when it is missing, makes Boxy the default agent and starts it. Plan without --yes . Named setup , not boxy : words are compared without case, so boxy would have shadowed bxrig ai agents Boxy VERB ai agents chat [NAME] [--window] bxAgents chat --projectRoot=P , plus --connect=http://127.0.0.1:PORT when the agent runs (one agent for the chat, the web page and the bar); --window opens a terminal ( Ai.terminal() ) that runs it, for the shortcut. No NAME: the default agent ai agents open [NAME] as before; no NAME: the default agent ai agents ask TEXT [--agent=N] [--thread=T] POST /__bxagents/invoke { input, threadId } (the field is input : a body with message reaches the model as an empty question) to the running agent; { answer, thread, pending: [ { tool, args } ] } . The thread is bxrig- and 12 hex digits unless given ai agents approve\|reject THREAD [--agent=N] [--session] POST /__bxagents/resume { threadId, decision } ( approve , approve_session , reject ); the stream is read for the tools that ran ( tool frames with status: ok ), the answer ( chunk frames: choices[1].delta.content ) and what it waits for next ( suspended ) ai agents skills [NAME] [show\|approve\|remove SKILL] [--all] [--yes] the skills the agent saved in ~/.bxagents/NAME/skills/*/SKILL.md (name and description from the front matter). Reviewed means the SHA of SKILL.md matches the one kept in agents.json reviewed when you approved: saving over it flags it again. A flagged skill stays active (owner's choice). remove deletes the folder, plan first The approval step: Agent.bx calls withCheckpointer( aiMemory( memory: "cache" ) ) before withMiddleware( new HumanInTheLoopMiddleware( toolsRequiringApproval: NEEDS_OK, mode: "web" ) ) ; without the checkpointer first the class does not load (measured: "HumanInTheLoopMiddleware is attached to mode web ... but the agent has no checkpointer"). Verified for real: the run pauses before the tool runs, /pending names it, /resume approve runs it, reject does not. The tools: 36 @AITool functions in tools/BxRig.bx , each bxrig ARGS --json through systemExecute , BXRIG_SELF else bxrig ; the model gets the envelope's data as JSON (cut at 6000 characters) or what failed. The 19 that change something are in NEEDS_OK and pass --yes where the command asks for it (the approval was the plan). Argument descriptions come from the doc comment ( @arg text ); no argument is called name . Model: the bxrig profile ( configure() returns { profile: "bxrig" } ), which now sets options.timeout: 300 (measured: Qwen3.5 4B on 4 CPU cores took over 90 s, bx-ai's default, for its first answer with the 36 tools). Measured on 2026-11-25 against the served Boxy: Qwen3.5 0.8B listed the themes, asked for night_light_set {state: on} and reminder_add {stretch, 30m} , and once proposed an unasked brightness_set (held by the approval); Qwen3.5 4B listed the 24 themes from theme_list and asked for night_light_set {state: on} . Shortcuts: agent-chat Super+Period ( ai agents chat --window ), agent-web Super+Shift+Period ( ai agents open ), both styles, Hyprland. Setup: the wizard's AI page asks boxy ( now by default, later ); init then runs ai agents install --yes and ai agents setup --yes , both optional, after ai-setup . Bar: the Agents panel's Boxy tab ( boxy.luau ): the default agent with Start or Stop, Chat, Web, Ask with Approve and Reject, the count of skills to review with Review; Make Boxy when there is none. Tests: tests/ai_agents_test.bxs and tests/ai-agents-test.sh (the template copied as is; chat stopped and running; --window ; ask, approve, reject and --session against a fake agent API; the skill review), tests/init_plan_test.bxs (the two steps and their order). Checked for real against bx-agents 1.0.0-snapshot and BoxLang 1.20.0-snapshot: Boxy made from the template, built and served by its unit, its read-only tools answering from real bxrig output, changing ones waiting; ask , approve and reject against a served agent. Not yet on a real desktop: the chat in a terminal from the shortcut, a real systemd user session and the bar tab in Noctalia. 13.69 mcp : BxRig's tools for any coding agent or editor (decided with the owner 2026-11-25) The tools are Boxy's own ( templates/agents/boxy/tools/BxRig.bx , 36 @AITool functions, each bxrig ARGS --json ). The server runs on JVM BoxLang with bx-ai, which bx-agents installs (the owner's choice over a server written in BxRig: one tools file, and the MCP protocol kept by bx-ai). bx-ai's MatchBox build (bx-ai PR #341) was tried on 2026-11-25 and did not yet serve over stdio; serve can move to it later without changing the commands. Command Does mcp [--json] the server (ready when bx-agents is installed) and each of the 16 agents and editors: installed, linked read-only , write or not mcp tools the tools from the @AITool lines; the ones that change something are Boxy's NEEDS_OK list in its Agent.bx (19), the rest read (17) mcp serve [--write] what an agent starts: writes serve.bxs , BxRig.bx and changing.json to DATA/mcp when they differ, then runs boxlang serve.bxs there with BXRIG_SELF (BxRig's path, for the tools) and BXRIG_MCP_WRITE . serve.bxs registers aiToolRegistry().scanClass( new BxRig() ) (bx-ai's own @AITool scan, which keeps the parameters) on mcpServer( "bxrig" ) , without the changing tools unless BXRIG_MCP_WRITE=1 , and calls MCPRequestProcessor::processStdio . Without bx-agents: the reason on standard error, exit 4, nothing on standard output mcp link [AGENT...] [--write] [--yes] adds BXRIG mcp serve [--write] (BxRig's absolute path) to each named agent, else to every installed one. Plan without --yes mcp unlink [AGENT...] [--yes] takes it out of each named agent, else of every linked one Where: Claude Code ( claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user bxrig -- ... , claude mcp get|remove bxrig --scope user ) and Codex ( codex mcp add bxrig -- ... , get , remove ) by their own commands; the rest in their own files (paths in the guide): mcpServers.bxrig (Gemini CLI, Pi, Qwen Code, Antigravity, Cursor with type: stdio , Kiro with disabled: false , Copilot with type: local and tools: ["*"] ), "amp.mcpServers" (Amp), mcp.bxrig { type: local, command: [ ... ], enabled } (OpenCode, the V1 shape V2 reads), context_servers (Zed), servers with type: stdio (VS Code), a marked [mcp_servers.bxrig] table (Grok Build), a marked mcp add bxrig --command ... --args ... line (Crush's crushrc), a marked entry under extensions: (Goose's YAML; an inline extensions: {} becomes a block, any other inline form is refused). Formats from each agent's docs, read 2026-11-25. Files with comments: Zed's and VS Code's settings allow them; there BxRig's key goes in as a // BxRig MCP server block after the line with the first { , and unlink gives the file back byte for byte. Other agents' JSON with comments is refused. An agent BxRig picked itself is left out with the reason ( skipped ); a named one is a precondition (exit 4). The old file is kept as FILE.bxrig-backup . Until bx-ai's stdio fix ships (bugs found here: log lines on standard output, an error answer to notifications/initialized , @mcpTool scans without parameters; a separate session fixes them in bx-ai), serve pipes the server through grep "^{" and drops the Method not found: notifications/ line, so only MCP messages reach the agent. Measured 2026-11-25 with bx-agents 1.0.0-snapshot (bx-ai 3.8.0-snapshot): the server starts in about 1.5 to 2.7 s, lists 17 tools read-only and 36 with --write , answers theme_list from the real bxrig theme list --json , and refuses theme_set read-only ( Tool not found ). Tests: tests/mcp_test.bxs (the tools and NEEDS_OK , every format added and taken out again, JSON with comments, inline YAML), tests/mcp-test.sh (fake agents and a fake MCP server: plans, link by name and all, --write , a left-out agent, unlink giving files back, what reaches standard output, serve without bx-agents). 13.70 privacy : what leaves this machine (decided with the owner 2026-11-25) A report and two switches (the owner chose both). Facts per agent from each agent's docs, read 2026-11-25: where its model runs, whether BxRig can point it at the local server (or why not), its telemetry switch (or how to turn it off when BxRig can not), and the folder of its chats. An agent with no documented switch is said to have none; BxRig does not guess one. Command Does privacy [--json] BxRig's AI server; each installed agent ( runs , local : on , possible or no with why ); stored keys by name (the secrets backend) and provider keys set in the environment (never a value); the MCP servers in each agent's config ( this machine for a command, web: HOST for a URL); each agent's telemetry ( off , on , or no switch with how ); the chat folders that exist and ~/.bxagents ; cloud_agents privacy local-only [--off] [--yes] adds BxRig's local server (its chat models, 127.0.0.1 only) to OpenCode (as bxrig ai link opencode --default ), Crush (as bxrig ai link crush ), Pi ( providers.bxrig in ~/.pi/agent/models.json , api: openai-completions , a placeholder key Pi asks for), GitHub Copilot CLI (a bxrig provider and its models in ~/.copilot/providers.json ) and Goose ( ~/.config/goose/custom_providers/bxrig.json ); --off takes them out (Goose's file is removed). Every other agent says why it stays. Needs the server on 127.0.0.1 with a chat model (exit 4) privacy telemetry off\|on [AGENT...] [--yes] off : Claude Code env.DISABLE_TELEMETRY and env.DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING = "1" in ~/.claude/settings.json ; Codex a marked [analytics] enabled = false ; Gemini CLI and Qwen Code privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled: false ; Pi enableInstallTelemetry: false ; Goose a marked GOOSE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED: false ; Kiro kiro-cli settings telemetry.enabled false ; Zed telemetry { diagnostics, metrics } false (a marked block when the file has comments); VS Code telemetry.telemetryLevel: off . on takes BxRig's settings out again (each agent's own default). A setting of yours in the way is left to you Control Center: the Privacy page ( bxrig tui privacy , after Secrets): one row per AI, key, MCP server, telemetry switch and data folder; a cloud agent that could be local and a web MCP server are flagged; l / L local-only on/off, t / T telemetry off/on. Bar: a Privacy button in the Agents panel's Agents tab opens it. util.Marked holds the shared pieces for files someone else owns: a marked block cut and read, JSON set, unset and get by path, JSON with comments (comments stripped for checks; a block inserted after the first { line). Tests: tests/privacy_test.bxs (the facts, every telemetry format and back, the local providers and back, MCP servers by command or URL, the page rows and keys, util.Marked), tests/privacy-test.sh (fake agents: the report with no key value, plans, telemetry off and back on, local-only on and off, its preconditions). 13.71 android : Android apps with Waydroid (decided with the owner 2026-11-25) Opt-in at every level (the owner's rule): a default install and init do nothing about it; the wizard's Android question (Containers page) defaults to no ; every command that changes something is a plan until --yes . Formats and commands from Waydroid's source and docs, read 2026-11-25 ( tools/actions/status.py , app_manager.py , docs.waydro.id command-line options, install and Google Play certification pages). Command Does android [--json] the state: supported , wayland , binder ( ok , how ), installed , initialized , image ( GAPPS , FOSS , VANILLA ), session , container , running , ip . Text says it is off and how to turn it on when it is not set up android setup [--vanilla] [--yes] [--dry-run] plan, then the steps in order, on the terminal (sudo asks, the download shows its progress): Debian and Ubuntu add curl -s https://repo.waydro.id \| bash as root; waydroid through the distribution's package manager ( Packages.installArgv ); sudo waydroid init -s GAPPS ( VANILLA with --vanilla , -f when another image is already there); sudo systemctl enable --now waydroid-container.service ; the session in the background ( setsid -f waydroid session start ). Steps already done are left out; it stops at the first one that fails and a rerun continues. Refused with exit 4 and the reason on openSUSE (no package), without a Wayland session, or without binder android start / stop waydroid session start in the background and wait up to 25 s for Session: RUNNING ; waydroid session stop . They act at once (they start or stop a program) android apps waydroid app list parsed ( Name: , packageName: , tab-indented categories), by name. Needs it running (exit 4) android open [APP] no APP: waydroid show-full-ui . An APP is a package name, an app's name in any case, or a part of a name that matches one app (a part matching several is a usage error listing them). Starts Android first when it is stopped android install FILE.apk [--yes] waydroid app install FILE after a plan; a file that is not an .apk or does not exist is a usage error. The app has to support x86_64 android register [--open] the Android ID from sudo waydroid shell -- sh -c "sqlite3 /data/data/*/*/gservices.db 'select value from main where name = \"android_id\";'" (Waydroid's Google Play certification page), the page to register it ( https://www.google.com/android/uncertified , opened with --open ) and what to do next (wait, stop , start ). Only on the Google Play image; exit 4 before Play created the ID android remove [--data] [--yes] plan, then: stop the session, sudo systemctl disable --now waydroid-container.service , remove the package. --data adds one sudo rm -rf of Waydroid's own folders that exist ( /var/lib/waydroid , ~/.local/share/waydroid , ~/waydroid , ~/.waydroid ), worded as DELETE in the plan Binder: the kernel config ( zcat /proc/config.gz : CONFIG_ANDROID_BINDER_IPC=y or =m ), binder in /proc/filesystems (binderfs), or an installed binder_linux module. When it is missing BxRig names binder_linux-dkms (AUR) and does not install a kernel module itself. Test hooks: BXRIG_WAYDROID_DIR (default /var/lib/waydroid , where waydroid.cfg says which image) and BXRIG_PROC_FILESYSTEMS . Control Center: the Android page ( bxrig tui android , before Logs): off (a note and S for the setup plan), or the state row and one row per app ( Enter open, s start or stop, r register). Catalog: waydroid is an optional app on Arch only ( extra ); Debian and Ubuntu get it through the repository setup adds. Wizard and init: the android question ( no by default) and, on yes , one optional step bxrig android setup --yes . Tests: tests/android_test.bxs (the parsers, binder, the plan for Arch, Debian and Ubuntu, picking an app, the page, the wizard question and init step) and tests/android-test.sh (a fake Waydroid that keeps its state in files, fake sudo, pacman and systemctl: off by default, the plan, the steps in order, apps, open, install, register, stop and start, replacing the image, remove with and without --data , what refuses setup). Not tested on a real machine: there is no binder and no Wayland session in the test environment, so the first real run (Waydroid's own start, the Google Play image, registration) is on the owner's machine. 13.72 boxy : Boxy's character and voice (decided with the owner 2026-11-25) Everything is opt in. A default install shows Boxy in its own colours and does nothing with a microphone or a speaker. Voxtype's commands are from its README and manual ( voxtype record start|stop , --output-file ), the release bind from Hyprland's Lua binds ( { release = true } ), read 2026-11-25. Command Does boxy [--json] Boxy now: its text sprite, name, colour, outfit, state, the image for that state, and the speech setting boxy look [--name=N] [--color=theme\|#RRGGBB] [--outfit=auto\|none\|ID] [--holidays=LIST\|none] [--birthday=MM-DD] changes how Boxy looks, saved in ~/.config/bxrig/boxy.json . Bad values are exit 2. --color=theme (the default) follows the active theme's accent; an outfit ID is beanie , flower , sunglasses , leaf , santa , pumpkin or party boxy export [--dir=D] the four state images ( idle , listening , working , speaking ), as PNG when rsvg-convert or ImageMagick is there, else SVG boxy state [--json] what Boxy is doing and the image for it (made again first when the look changed) boxy listen start\|stop\|toggle hold to talk: voxtype record start --output-file F , then voxtype record stop , the words go to the default BoxLang agent (thread bxrig-voice ), the answer comes as a desktop notice and, when speech is on, aloud. Exit 4 without Voxtype boxy say TEXT speaks the text through the speech setting. Exit 4 when it is not set up or no player is found boxy voice [on\|off\|set] speech is off until set has a URL and model and on is run. set --url=U --model=M --voice=V [--key=SECRET_NAME] [--format=wav\|mp3\|opus\|flac] . Any OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech server: a cloud provider, or a local one boxy voice local [--lang=auto\|en\|es] [--voice=NAME] [--accent=latam\|castilian] [--speed=N] [--hear=auto\|en\|es] speech on this machine with bx-audio (decided with the owner 2026-11-26). A plan without --yes (exit 2); --yes fetches the voices ( bx-audio speak , a few minutes the first time), saves voice.engine = "bx-audio" and turns speech on. --lang=auto picks the voice from the text (Spanish: dora by default; English: joe ), --accent is passed to bx-audio as BX_AUDIO_ACCENT (Latin American by default, both offered). --voice needs --lang=en or es . --hear sets language in [whisper] of Voxtype's config.toml : Voxtype has no per-recording language flag. Exit 4 without bx-audio boxy voice list [--lang=en\|es] , boxy voice test [--lang=en\|es] the voices bx-audio offers; a spoken sample in the language The outfit in auto : the season (beanie Dec to Feb, flower Mar to May, sunglasses Jun to Aug, leaf Sep to Nov); the holiday outfits ( christmas Dec 20 to 26, halloween Oct 24 to 31, newyear Dec 31 to Jan 2) only for the holidays you list with --holidays ; the birthday outfit on the day you set. Test hook: BXRIG_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD . Never by voice: approving something Boxy wants to change stays on screen. A pending approval only produces a notice that says so. What leaves the machine: nothing, until speech is on, and with the local engine (bx-audio) nothing ever does. With speech on, each answer read aloud is sent to the speech server (the privacy report says where; a server on this machine is shown as such). The key is a stored secret name or an environment variable, passed to curl in a mode 600 config file that is deleted after the call, never on the command line. The key: Super+Comma (the traditional style; Super+Ctrl+Slash in the Mac style, where Super+Comma is Preferences) and the Copilot key ( Super+Shift+F23 ): the press starts listening, the release ( { release = true } ) sends. Four rows in keys show ; a press and its release do not count as a conflict. Surfaces: the Boxy page in the Control Center ( bxrig tui boxy , before Android: Boxy's sprite, the speech row, and the outfits, Enter puts one on, v speech, e images), the Boxy tab of the bar's Agents panel (the picture for what it is doing and a Talk button), and the sprite in bxrig boxy . The art is concept D, the antenna bot (owner, 2026-11-26): the antenna tip is the BoxLang swirl, lit and turning while it works (four pictures, frames in boxy and boxy state ; the bar turns them once a second). The tab also has Chat , Web and Logs , which open bx-agents' own chat ( bxrig ai agents chat ), web page and log viewer ( bxrig ai agents NAME logs --ui ); BxRig keeps no history of its own. The state file is ~/.local/state/bxrig/boxy-state.json ; a state nothing updated for three minutes reads as idle. Tests: tests/boxy_test.bxs (the calendar, colours, the four images and the sprite, the page, the bar source) and tests/boxy-test.sh (a fake Voxtype, notify-send, curl, bx-audio and player: the look and the outfit by date, export, speech off by default and never sent before it is on, the key kept off the command line, hold to talk, silence, no Voxtype, and local speech: the plan, the voices fetched, Spanish and English picked from the text, both accents, Voxtype's language, no bx-audio). Not tested on a real machine: a real microphone, Voxtype's service, the Hyprland release bind and Noctalia's image drawing.
