Answers whose command does not exist yet (`ssh_key`; and `workspaces`, `natural_scroll`, `layouts`, `theme`, `wallpaper` when Hyprland is not being set up, because only the Hyprland starter takes them) are saved and listed as `pending`, never dropped silently. `init` at a terminal runs the wizard, saves `answers.json`, then runs the plan (the review screen is the confirmation; `--dry-run` only prints). `install.sh` ends with `bxrig init` at a terminal and prints a hint otherwise.

### 14.4 Rules

* Every answer is optional; an unanswered page does nothing. The review screen lists exactly the commands that will run.
* `init` never runs a step the user did not choose, and never overwrites a file the user changed (the config service rules of section 6 apply).
* Starter configs are parametrized by the answers (workspaces, window style, layouts, theme, wallpaper, bar position, world clocks, natural scroll); the defaults are the current starters.
* Databases follow the earlier plan (`plan.md` section 7): Podman is the default engine and Docker is an explicit choice; services run as containers with start, stop, status and logs, persistent volumes and generated passwords kept in a mode-600 file.
* Runner integration (legacy `bxrig-runner`): launcher providers `system`, `noctalia`, `rofi`, `walker`, `krunner`, `vicinae`, `hyprrunner`, `custom`; menu providers `rofi`, `walker`, `vicinae`, `hyprrunner`; commands are JSON argument arrays, never shell strings; keybindings are never changed. Default on Hyprland is Noctalia (Super+Space).
* The TUI needs MatchBox's `bif-tui` in the native runner (task W2). Until then `init --answers` is the only form.

### 13.53 Shared helper classes (decided with the owner 2026-11-14, code review refactor)

One home per concept; command classes hold small collaborators in `variables.*` (there are no base classes on MatchBox).

* **Output: `Cli.say( command, code, data, asJson, lines = [], dry = false )`, `Cli.fail( command, code, msg, asJson )`, `Out`.** `Out` is the same bound to one command name (`variables.out = new bxrig.Out( variables.cli, "time" )`): `say`, `fail`, `usage` (2), `precondition` (4), `failed` (6), `sub( command )`. Every method returns the exit code. A class must not create `Out` from inside `Out`/`Cli.scoped` chains of its own class (MatchBox overflows the stack when a class `new`s itself).
* **Processes: `Proc`.** `exec( argv, timeout )` never throws (`{ exitCode, output, timeout }`, 127 and the reason when the program cannot start), `raw` may throw, `has( name )` is `command -v` with the name as an argument (never run the tool), `works( name )` is `name --version`, `isRoot()`, `self( args, timeout )` runs BxRig itself (`BXRIG_SELF`). `Installer.proc()` hands the same injected test runner to a class; `Installer.hasCommand` is `Proc.has`, so a tool without `--version` counts as installed.
* **Paths: `Env`.** `BXRIG_*_HOME`, then `XDG_*_HOME`, then `$HOME` for every folder: `xdgConfig( sub )`, `xdgData`, `xdgState`, `xdgCache` (shared with other programs) and BxRig's own `config`, `data` (`BXRIG_DATA_HOME` is the folder itself), `state`, `cache`. A user with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set now gets every BxRig file under it (`bxrig/`, `menus/`, `nvim/`, `strata/`); `tests/paths-test.sh` guards it. `new bxrig.Env( { HOME: "/h" } )` replaces the real environment in unit tests.
* **Text: `Text`** (`merge`, `pad`, `padLeft`, `lines`, `nl`).
* **Desktop entries: `DesktopEntry`.** `parse` (exact-case keys, only the `[Desktop Entry]` group, `launcher` for BxRig's own `X-BxRig-Launcher` entries), `dirs( withFlatpak )` (`BXRIG_APPS_DIRS`, older `BXRIG_DESKTOP_DIRS`), `entries( dirs, launchers, needExec )`, `iconName`, `cleanExec`, `render( lines )`. The Apps page leaves BxRig's launchers out; the `apps` launcher grid keeps them.
* **Package layout.** `src/bxrig/` has one class per command or feature (152 classes, 4,982 lines of generated `*Data.bx` among them); `src/bxrig/util/` has the 23 shared helpers, reached as `bxrig.util.NAME`: `Cli`, `Out`, `Exit`, `Mutation` (plans and dry runs), `Proc`, `Env`, `Text`, `Fmt`, `Names`, `JsonStore`, `SystemFile`, `SystemdUnit`, `Systemd`, `Pacman`, `Aur`, `Http`, `Urls`, `Desktop`, `DesktopEntry`, `Ini`, `Props`, `Lua` and the generated `Version`. A helper never holds a command's job and a command never holds a helper's; `tests/dry-test.sh` keeps the copies from coming back.
* **Command registry.** `docs/reference/cli.json` holds every command (name, group, summary, usage, examples, flags with types, note). `bootstrap/gen-docs.sh` writes `commands.md`, `command-flags.md`, `HelpData.bx` (`bxrig help`) and `CommandFlagData.bx` from it and fails when `Main.bx` has a command the file lacks (or the reverse), an example names no command, or a usage line uses a flag the command does not list. `CommandSpec` answers flags and usage at run time.
* **Unknown command exit.** A command that is not in `Main.bx` prints "Unsupported command" and exits 2 (it exited 0 before); the flag whitelist has no duplicates.
* **Tests.** `tests/lib/harness.sh` (binary, tmp, `fail`, `stub`, `code`), `tests/run-all.sh` (discovery, parallel), `tests/dry-test.sh` (ratchet of copied helpers and of tests missing from CI).

### 13.55 Audio, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi: core utilities, fallback terminal UIs, status commands (decided with the owner 2026-11-15)

BxRig builds no Bluetooth, audio or Wi-Fi pages of its own: the Noctalia bar already has the network, bluetooth and volume widgets and panels. What BxRig adds is the plumbing under them, a terminal fallback, and read-only status. Three steps, one commit each (the shapes below are the plan; the sections of the step commits say what was built).

**A. Core utilities, always installed.** Catalog entries with `tier: default` (installed by a plain `bxrig install`, no wizard question): `bluez` (`bluez`, `bluez-utils`, exists), `pipewire` (new: `pipewire`, `pipewire-pulse`, `wireplumber`, `libpulse`, which provides `pactl`), `mpv` (exists, default), `playerctl` (made default), `brightnessctl` (new; `setup hyprland` already installs it, the catalog entry makes the plain install and `Display` precondition message point at it). Every name was looked up on `https://archlinux.org/packages/search/json/?name=NAME` (all in `extra`); `verified_on` is the day of that lookup, nothing was installed. `bluetooth.service` is enabled by `setup hyprland` as one more plan step (`kind: "systemd"`, built with `Systemd.enableArgv( ..., sudo )`, shown and run by the same plan runner as every other step, skipped when `facts.bluetoothEnabled`); `bluez` and `bluez-utils` join `hyprlandPackages` so the unit exists when the step runs. `setup plasma` has the same step (skipped when enabled, left out of `--undo-keys`); when `bluez` is missing, `bluez` and `bluez-utils` join its package step. It remembers that it enabled the unit in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/bxrig/setup-plasma.json` (`{ bluetooth: true }`, mode 600) and `setup undo plasma` turns the unit off first, only when that record exists and the unit is enabled. `init` runs `setup hyprland` and `setup plasma` for the chosen desktops, so it gets the service from those steps; it adds no step of its own.

**B. Fallback terminal UIs** (default tier, they are small): `wiremix` (made default), `bluetui` (new, `extra` 0.8.2). `impala` (`extra` 0.9.0) is in the catalog as tier **optional** only: it needs `iwd` as the Wi-Fi backend with NetworkManager and wpa_supplicant disabled, so it cannot sit next to NetworkManager; no default install, no menu entry (open question for the owner). Menu, section Hardware: `Audio mixer (terminal)` runs `wiremix`, `Bluetooth devices (terminal)` runs `bluetui`, each in the configured terminal; `Audio`, `Bluetooth` and `Wi-Fi` open the Noctalia control center panel (`noctalia msg panel-toggle control-center`, the action of `Super+Alt+C`). The menu tree gets two entry kinds that run a program itself instead of `bxrig ARGV`: `tool` (in a terminal window that closes when the program ends; exit 4 when the program is not installed) and `exec` (detached, no window). No new key bindings; `Super+Ctrl+A/B/N/P/D` stay as they are.

**C. Read-only status** , all `--json` envelopes, all exit 0 or 4, no `--yes`, argv arrays through `Proc`:

|         Command          |    Class    |                                      Reads                                      |                 Exit 4 when                 |
|--------------------------|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `bxrig audio status`     | `Audio`     | `pactl --format=json info`, `list sinks`, `list sources`                        | `pactl` missing, or no sound server answers |
| `bxrig bluetooth status` | `Bluetooth` | `bluetoothctl show`, `devices Paired`, `devices Connected`, `bluetooth.service` | `bluetoothctl` missing                      |
| `bxrig wifi status`      | `Wifi`      | `nmcli -t` radio, device status, active access point                            | `nmcli` missing                             |

### 13.58 `vpn`: one list of VPNs with data-driven adapters (decided with the owner 2026-11-17)

The top bar has a VPN icon (plugin `bxrig/vpn`, section 13.59); this is the command behind it. One pick-one list with two groups: **Network profiles** (saved NetworkManager connections of type `vpn` or `wireguard`, through `nmcli`) and **VPN apps** (NordVPN, NordLayer, Tailscale, Mullvad).

* `vpn list [--json]` the installed providers and profiles with their state; **an empty list, exit 0, when nothing is installed** (the bar icon hides itself then). `data`: `{ providers: [ { id, name, group (profiles|apps), kind, state, connected, location, detail, can_pick, coexist, verified, note } ], connected: [ids], allow_several, install: [ { id, name, install } ] }`. `state` is `connected`, `connecting`, `disconnected`, `login` (log in first), `unavailable` (daemon not running) or `unknown`. A profile's id is `nm:NAME`.
* `vpn status [NAME]` what is connected (one provider with NAME). `vpn locations NAME` the places it can connect to: `{ provider, can_pick, current, locations: [ { value, label } ] }` with the reserved first entries `default` (connect as it is) and, where the provider can clear a choice, `none` (Tailscale: no exit node), then the provider's own list (NordVPN countries, Tailscale exit nodes, Mullvad countries and cities, NordLayer gateways).
* `vpn connect NAME [--location=VALUE]` and `vpn disconnect [NAME]` start or stop a program, so they act at once and take `--dry-run` (the exception of 2.11). Without a NAME `disconnect` stops everything that is connected. **Default: one at a time** : connecting first disconnects what is connected. `vpn set allow_several=true|false --yes` (saved in `~/.config/bxrig/vpn.json` through the config service, `--dry-run` shows the plan) lifts that, for Tailscale next to another VPN; a note says that two VPNs can clash on routes and DNS. Not tested against a real NordVPN plus Tailscale: the owner is to try it.
* Exit codes: 0 done or nothing to do; 2 bad usage, an unknown name, a bad `--location` (no leading dash, plain characters, up to 80), `set` without `--yes`; 4 no VPN installed (status, connect, disconnect, locations), a known provider that is not installed, or no NetworkManager for an `nm:` name; 6 a command failed.
* **Adapters are data.** `catalog/vpn-providers.json` (a resource) has one object per app: `binary`, `install` (catalog id), `status { argv, parser }`, `connect`, `connect_to` (with `{location}`) or `select` plus `select_order` (`before` or `after`, for apps that pick a place in a separate command) and `select_none`, `disconnect`, `locations { argv, parser }`, `default_label`, `none_label`, `coexist`, `verified`, `note`. The code (`VpnAdapters`) has no branch for any provider; the only code is the named parsers in `VpnParsers` (`nordvpn`, `nordlayer`, `tailscale`, `mullvad`, `words`). A provider of your own goes in `~/.config/bxrig/vpn-providers.json` (`{"providers":[...]}`, adds or replaces by id). Argv templates are arrays (rule 9): `{location}` is one argument, `{location*}` the location split on spaces.
* **Verified against the vendors' documentation on 2026-11-17** (each adapter's `note` says exactly what): NordVPN `status`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `countries` (support.nordvpn.com); Tailscale `up`, `down`, `set --exit-node=` (an empty value clears it), `exit-node list`, `status --json` (tailscale.com/kb/1080/cli); Mullvad `status`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `relay list`, `relay set location COUNTRY [CITY]` (mullvad.net); `nmcli connection show|up|down`, `-t` escaping of `:` (NetworkManager manual). **Not verified:** NordVPN `connect COUNTRY` by name (from `nordvpn help connect`, the page shows `connect CODE SERVER`); the exact text of `mullvad status` and `relay list` between app versions; the Tailscale JSON field names (the page only says "detailed JSON"); NordLayer `status`, `gateways` and `disconnect` (help.nordlayer.com confirms only `nordlayer connect GATEWAY-ID` and `nordlayer settings set`), so its parsers are tolerant and its adapter says `partial`.
* **Catalog:** `nordlayer` is a new catalog app (`aur`, target `nordlayer`, kind desktop, optional; the AUR RPC listed it on 2026-11-17 as version 3.6.0, a community package of the vendor's `.deb` from downloads.nordlayer.com; the vendor ships only `.deb` and `.rpm`, so there is no vendor package for Arch). The wizard's VPN question offers it (no extra step: log out and in, then log in with the app). Check the package before relying on it: it is not maintained by NordLayer.
* **Left out on purpose:** ExpressVPN and Surfshark (owner); Proton VPN (its command line was not verified: no adapter row until it is); WireGuard `wg-quick` (needs root for every up and down: a NetworkManager WireGuard profile covers it).
* The NordVPN post-install steps stay as they were: `vpn nordvpn setup [--yes]` (13.20) is routed through the same class.
* Tests: `tests/vpn_test.bxs` (parsers, adapters, the commands with a fake runner), `tests/vpn-test.sh` (fake `nordvpn`, `tailscale`, `nmcli`; no real VPN is touched).

### 13.66 The screensaver (decided with the owner 2026-11-18)

* **What it is.** After a while idle, terminal art in the theme's colours on every monitor, then the lock. Six effects take turns, a minute each, from a random first one: `sweep` (BXRIG in DOS Rebel with a gradient sweeping across it), `laptop` (the About laptop with a glint crossing BX), `rain` (BoxLang code falling in columns), `clock` (the time in DOS Rebel, drifting), `stars` (a starfield) and `logo` (your text in DOS Rebel or a picture in half blocks, drifting). Every effect moves, so nothing stays on the same pixels. Any key, click, scroll or mouse move closes it (mouse moves need MatchBox's `tui.set_mouse_motion`; events in the first half second are ignored).
* **Commands.** `screensaver [status] [--json]`; `on|off [--yes]` (off keeps the lock); `set screensaver=SECONDS lock=SECONDS effects=NAME,NAME [--yes]` (whole seconds, 0 for never, the lock after the screensaver); `logo text TEXT|image PATH|reset [--yes]` (1 to 10 letters, digits, spaces or `. _ ! : -`; a png, jpg, gif, webp or svg); `effects [--json]`; `start [--effect=NAME]`; `stop`; `preview [EFFECT]` (in this terminal); `run [--effect=NAME]` (what each window runs). A change without `--yes` is a plan. Exit 0, 2 usage, 4 no Hyprland, no terminal that can name its window, or not a terminal.
* **Settings:** `~/.config/bxrig/screensaver.json` `{ enabled, screensaver, lock, effects, logo }`; defaults on, 150 s, 300 s, every effect, the text BXRIG. A value that is not valid keeps its default.
* **Idle (Noctalia, docs.noctalia.dev services/idle).** Two behaviors in `[idle]`, `behavior_order = ["bxrig_screensaver", "bxrig_lock"]`: `bxrig_screensaver` is `action = "command"`, `command = "'BXRIG' screensaver start"`, `resume_command = "'BXRIG' screensaver stop"`, so coming back closes it; `bxrig_lock` is Noctalia's own `action = "lock"`. Both count from the start of idle and respect idle inhibitors (a video, `toggle stay-awake`). The starter `config.toml` carries the section; a change is sent to a running Noctalia with `noctalia msg config-set` (reported as `applied`, `not running` or `skipped`). `hypridle` is no longer started or installed: BxRig never wrote a config for it.
* **Windows (Hyprland).** `start` opens one terminal per monitor from `hyprctl monitors -j`, with the class `bxrig-screensaver` (ghostty, kitty, alacritty or foot, the xdg-terminals.list one first), through `hyprctl dispatch exec "[monitor NAME] ..."` and, when that fails, the Lua form `hl.dsp.exec_cmd(CMD, { monitor = NAME })`. The Hyprland module's window rule makes the class full screen with no animation, border, corners, shadow or blur. `start` does nothing when one is already open; `stop` kills the pids `hyprctl clients -j` gives for the class. With neither Hyprland nor Plasma, `start` exits 4.
* **Plasma (2026-11-18).** `ScreensaverPlasma`: the idle watcher is a user service, `~/.config/systemd/user/bxrig-screensaver-idle.service`, running `swayidle -w timeout SECONDS "BXRIG screensaver start --idle" resume "BXRIG screensaver stop"` (KWin implements ext-idle-notify-v1); `on`, `off` and `set` write, enable and restart it, or disable it, and name `swayidle` when it is missing (`setup plasma` installs it). `start --idle` first asks `org.freedesktop.PowerManagement.Inhibit.HasInhibit` and does nothing while something holds the screen awake, since KWin's idle timer has been reported to ignore inhibitors. `start` writes `templates/kwin-screensaver.js` to `~/.local/share/bxrig/kwin/`, loads it once over D-Bus (`org.kde.kwin.Scripting.loadScript`, then `start`), and opens one terminal per enabled output from `kscreen-doctor -j`; the script sends each new `bxrig-screensaver` window to a screen without one, full screen, above everything, without a border, off the taskbar and switcher (a forced screen window rule is not applied when a window opens on Wayland, KDE bug 514357). `stop` kills the terminals `pgrep -f` finds by the class. The lock is Plasma's own: `kscreenlockerrc [Daemon] Autolock` and `Timeout` in whole minutes (rounded up), `lock=0` sets `Autolock=false`; a running lock daemon is told with `qdbus6 org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver /ScreenSaver configure` (best effort). Not yet run on a real Plasma session: written against the KWin scripting API docs and checked with stubs.
* **UI.** Menu *System \> Screensaver* (start, preview, settings, on, off, three timings, logo reset); the Look page's *Screen* group (a switch and a timing choice: 2.5/5, 5/10, 10/20, 15/30 minutes); the wizard's Look page asks when it starts (2.5, 5 or 10 minutes, the lock at twice that, or off).
* **Tests:** `tests/screensaver_test.bxs` (settings, the idle section, each effect drawn and read back, the loop's rules) and `tests/screensaver-test.sh` (the CLI, Noctalia and Hyprland stubs, the screensaver in a pty closing on a key and a mouse move).

## Distributions (decided with the owner 2026-11-20)

* **Targets:** CachyOS and Arch (pacman, AUR), openSUSE Tumbleweed and Slowroll (zypper), Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and Debian 13 (apt). `util.Distro` reads `/etc/os-release` (`ID`, `ID_LIKE`, `VERSION_ID`); `BXRIG_DISTRO` (arch, suse, debian, ubuntu) overrides it, and tests and CI set it to `arch`. An unknown system reads the Arch catalog, and `setup` and the installer refuse it.
* **Catalog split:** `catalog/apps.json` (schema 4) says what an app is; `catalog/install/DISTRO.json` (schema 1) says how to install it: `defaults` (`terminal`), `names` (Arch package name to this distribution's, `""` for none needed), `repos` (extra repositories, each with `for` packages, a `check` path under `/etc`, `commands` and `files`), and `apps` (`source` + `targets`, and on Arch `repo`/`pkgbuild`/`aur_targets`/`script`). `extends` merges `names`, `apps` and `defaults` from a parent; a child's `repos` replaces the parent's. `ubuntu.json` extends `debian.json`. `Catalog.load(distro)` merges the entry into each app; an app without one is in `unavailable` and is not offered. Web apps need no entry.
* **Sources:** arch `pacman aur pkgbuild script unresolved`; suse `zypper flatpak script`; debian and ubuntu `apt flatpak script`. `catalog check` checks every install file (`checkAll`); `catalog coverage` reports offered and unavailable per distribution; `catalog list|show --distro=D` reads another one.
* **Package layer:** `util.Packages().native(proc, distro)` gives `Pacman`, `Zypper` or `Apt` with one interface (install, remove, upgrade argv, installed, versions, search rows, pending updates). Arch names are translated through `names` everywhere setup and the installer name a package. Apt runs `apt-get update` before an install or upgrade.
* **Flatpak fallback:** an app the distribution does not package is installed from Flathub with `flatpak install --user`; the plan adds `flatpak` itself and the Flathub remote when missing. Never as root.
* **Repositories:** Debian 13 adds `trixie-backports` (Hyprland, its tools, quickshell; skipped when an apt source already names it, `check_text`, and its packages install with `-t trixie-backports`, `release`, so their newer libraries come from it too); Debian 13 and Ubuntu 26.04 add Noctalia's apt repository (`pkg.noctalia.dev`, keyring package then the suite's `.sources` file). Added only when a package in the plan needs them and their file is not there yet.
* **Defaults:** Debian's terminal is kitty (no ghostty package); the rest use ghostty.
* **Arch-only:** the AUR (`pkg search --aur`, `pkg install --aur`), `kernel`, the boot splash (mkinitcpio), xremap's install (configuration works once it is installed), Nerd Fonts packages (`appearance font install` exits 4 elsewhere).
* **`catalog map DISTRO [--write] [--json]`:** run on that distribution; for each app tries the Arch names through `names`, then without `-bin`/`-git`/`-desktop-bin`/`-electron`, then Flathub by exact name; reports kept, found, flatpak, missing, and the Arch names BxRig installs itself that the distribution lacks. `--write` updates the install file. Exit 4 off that distribution.
* **Bootstrap:** `install.sh` and `web-install.sh` pick pacman, zypper or apt-get from `os-release`; yay only on Arch.
* **Not done yet:** the boot splash through dracut or initramfs-tools, xremap packages off Arch, Nerd Fonts off Arch, Packman codecs on openSUSE.
* **Tests:** `tests/distros_test.bxs` (families, the backends' argv and parsers, names, the merged catalogs, repo steps) and the CI containers (Tumbleweed, debian:trixie, ubuntu:26.04: install, `catalog check`, `setup hyprland --dry-run`).
* **Checked on WebTop (2026-11-20):** Debian 13 KDE and Ubuntu 26.04 KDE: `install` (apt), `setup hyprland --yes` (repos, packages, starter files), `setup status`, `pkg search|info`. `setup plasma` stops on Debian 13 (Plasma 6.3; HyprKwin needs 6.6). Flatpak installs could not run there (no user namespaces in the container).

## Scheduler (decided with the owner 2026-11-22)

* One scheduler for everything BxRig runs on a timer: a BoxLang scheduler class run by `boxlang schedule` in the user service bxrig-scheduler.service. Groups, pause and resume per group, a history and stats per task.
* The tasks live in \~/.config/bxrig/schedule.json. BxRig writes the runner (one fluent call per task: every, everyHour, everyDayAt, onWeekdays, ons, cron) on every change and restarts the service. A 5-field cron() did not fire on BoxLang 1.19, so `cron ...` is documented as needing 1.20.
* The JVM only dispatches: every run is `bxrig scheduler exec NAME`, which runs the command, records it (history/NAME.jsonl, last 500) and notifies. The runner writes each task's getStats() (with next_local and last_local on this machine's clock) for the next run time.
* install is a plan until --yes. It adds update-check, backup-data (when backups are scheduled) and boxlang-check, and turns off bxrig-update-check.timer and bxrig-backup.timer; from then on `update notifications` and `backup data schedule` change those tasks. Without BoxLang the timers stay as they were.
* Exit 10 from a task is "needs attention" where the task lists 10 in ok_codes (update-check, boxlang-check); notify modes are failure (default), attention, always and never.

* `calendar agenda` reads those files with bxrig.Ical (pure: VEVENT, all-day dates, UTC times moved by `date +%z`, TZID and floating times as local, DURATION, RRULE DAILY/WEEKLY with BYDAY/MONTHLY/YEARLY with INTERVAL, COUNT, UNTIL, EXDATE, cancelled events left out).
* `bxrig remind TEXT --at|--in` keeps reminders in \~/.config/bxrig/reminders.json; `remind due` shows the ones whose time has come as critical notices, once each.
* The scheduler owns the timing: calendar-sync every 15 minutes and reminders every minute, added by the first calendar or reminder when the scheduler is installed, and by `scheduler install` when calendars or reminders exist. `Scheduler.upsert` never adds a task twice.
* The Clock panel shows the agenda of today and tomorrow and the reminders still to come under the world clocks, with a check button per reminder.

### 13.67 BoxLang agents: `ai agents` (decided with the owner 2026-11-24)

bx-agents has a full command line (`bxAgents`, every verb on one project: the current folder or `--projectRoot`), so BxRig does not repeat it (`AiAgentHub.bx`). It adds only what bx-agents leaves to the machine. Where things live is bx-agents' own convention: an agent's data in `~/.bxagents/<name>` (outside the project, so a build never replaces it), the person's settings in `~/.bxagents/Agent.yml`. BxRig keeps its list in `~/.config/bxrig/agents.json` (`root`, `default`, `entries: [ { path, port, added } ]`).

|                                Command                                 |                                                                                                                                                          Does                                                                                                                                                           |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ai agents [list]`                                                     | the projects: every folder of the projects folder with an `Agent.yml` or `Agent.bx`, then the ones added by path; name (the top-level `name:` of Agent.yml, else the folder), port, running, default                                                                                                                    |
| `ai agents install\|update [--snapshot\|--stable] [--yes] [--dry-run]` | `bx-module install bx-agents@snapshot` (the default for now), or `@VERSION` for `--stable`: the newest ForgeBox version without `snapshot` (exit 4 while there is none). Then `/tmp/boxlang-jars` is deleted, always, and the `bxrig` profile written. `update` also restarts the agents that run. Plan without `--yes` |
| `ai agents new NAME [flags]`                                           | `bxAgents new NAME [flags]` in the projects folder, the terminal handed over (its own wizard). The name: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, not a command word, not taken                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ai agents NAME VERB [args]`                                           | `bxAgents VERB --projectRoot=PROJECT [args]`, exactly as typed (from the raw arguments), the terminal handed over, its exit code. Its flags are not checked against cli.json                                                                                                                                            |
| `ai agents start\|stop\|status NAME`                                   | the user unit `bxrig-agent-NAME.service`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ai agents open NAME` / `default [NAME]`                               | its web page (`xdg-open`, only while it runs) / the default agent (for the keyboard shortcut, PR 11b)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ai agents dir [PATH]` / `add PATH` / `forget NAME [--yes]`            | the projects folder (`BXRIG_AGENTS_DIR`, else `dir`, else `~/Agents`) / a project elsewhere (refused when its name is taken: the data folder is chosen by name) / out of the list, its unit removed, the project and its data kept                                                                                      |
| `ai agents profile [--off]`                                            | the `bxrig` profile alone                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

* **Ports:** from 8790, one per project path, kept; a freed one is used again.
* **The unit:** `ExecStartPre=bxAgents build --projectRoot=P --no-banner`, then `ExecStart=/bin/sh -c "cd .build && BOXLANG_HOME=P/.build/runtime exec boxlang-miniserver --port N --host 127.0.0.1"`, with `Environment=BXRIG_SELF=PATH` (BxRig's full path, for the agent's tools: a user service's PATH may not have `~/.local/bin`) and `Restart=on-failure`. `BOXLANG_HOME` is set on the server's line only: set for the whole unit (as in PR 11) it reached the build step too, which then found no bx-agents module (measured, fixed in 11b). Not `bxAgents serve`: it starts the miniserver and exits 0 (measured), which systemd takes for the end of the service and stops the server with it. Running the miniserver in `.build` with the `miniserver.json` the build wrote is what bx-agents' deploy targets do; the flags win over the file. `WorkingDirectory` is the project, because `.build` does not exist before the first build and systemd checks the folder first.
* **The jar cache:** BoxLang copies module jars to `java.io.tmpdir/boxlang-jars` (`DynamicClassLoader.copyJarsToTemp`, BL-2629) named by path and modification time, and reuses a copy that exists. `bx-module install` keeps the zip's 1980 dates, so a reinstalled jar would load the old copy (measured: `NoMethodException` on a method the new jar has). It is deleted after every install (`BXRIG_BOXLANG_JARS` names another folder).
* **Test hooks:** `BXRIG_BXAGENTS` (the bxAgents launcher, else `BOXLANG_HOME/bin/bxAgents`, else the PATH), `BXRIG_MINISERVER` (boxlang-miniserver, else the PATH), `BXRIG_FORGEBOX_API` (default `https://forgebox.io/api/v1`).
* **The `bxrig` profile:** in `~/.bxagents/Agent.yml`, a marked block (`# >>> BxRig local AI ...`, `# <<< BxRig local AI <<<`) with `profiles.bxrig = { description, provider: openai-compatible, model: ACTIVE, options.baseURL: BASE/v1 }`. bx-agents layers that file over every agent at build and at start (`SettingsLayers`), mappings by key, so an agent uses BxRig's model with `profile: bxrig`. A file with a `profiles:` of its own is not rewritten (the lines to add are given). `ai models use` rewrites the block when it is there; it is never added unasked. Checked for real: `profile:`, `providers.openai-compatible.options` and a top-level `options` all reach the local server, from `invoke` and from the served app.
* **Control Center:** `ai-boxlang` (BoxLang agents, after Agents): `ai agents --json`; Enter the chat in a new terminal (`setsid -f TERMINAL bxrig ai agents NAME chat`), `o` web page, `s` start or stop, `d` default, `l` `journalctl --user -u UNIT`, `i` install or update. Bar: the Agents panel's BoxLang tab (`boxlang.luau`).
* **Java's home is not `$HOME`:** bx-agents reads `user.home`, which comes from the account, so a test that changes `HOME` sets `BXAGENTS_USER_CONFIG` too.
* Tests: `tests/ai_agents_test.bxs` (pure), `tests/ai-agents-test.sh` (fake bx-module, bxAgents, systemctl, curl and xdg-open). Checked for real against bx-agents 1.0.0-snapshot (2026-11-24) and BoxLang 1.20.0-snapshot: install, new, build, invoke and models list through the pass-through, the unit's two commands, the served `/__bxagents/invoke` answering through the `bxrig` profile. |-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

The thread is `bxrig-` and 12 hex digits unless given                                                                               |

Without bx-agents: the reason on standard error, exit 4, nothing on standard output |

* **Where:** Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user bxrig -- ...`, `claude mcp get|remove bxrig --scope user`) and Codex (`codex mcp add bxrig -- ...`, `get`, `remove`) by their own commands; the rest in their own files (paths in the guide): `mcpServers.bxrig` (Gemini CLI, Pi, Qwen Code, Antigravity, Cursor with `type: stdio`, Kiro with `disabled: false`, Copilot with `type: local` and `tools: ["*"]`), `"amp.mcpServers"` (Amp), `mcp.bxrig { type: local, command: [ ... ], enabled }` (OpenCode, the V1 shape V2 reads), `context_servers` (Zed), `servers` with `type: stdio` (VS Code), a marked `[mcp_servers.bxrig]` table (Grok Build), a marked `mcp add bxrig --command ... --args ...` line (Crush's crushrc), a marked entry under `extensions:` (Goose's YAML; an inline `extensions: {}` becomes a block, any other inline form is refused). |                                                        Command                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `boxy [--json]`                                                                                                       | Boxy now: its text sprite, name, colour, outfit, state, the image for that state, and the speech setting                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `boxy look [--name=N] [--color=theme\|#RRGGBB] [--outfit=auto\|none\|ID] [--holidays=LIST\|none] [--birthday=MM-DD]`  | changes how Boxy looks, saved in `~/.config/bxrig/boxy.json`. Bad values are exit 2. `--color=theme` (the default) follows the active theme's accent; an outfit ID is `beanie`, `flower`, `sunglasses`, `leaf`, `santa`, `pumpkin` or `party`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `boxy export [--dir=D]`                                                                                               | the four state images (`idle`, `listening`, `working`, `speaking`), as PNG when `rsvg-convert` or ImageMagick is there, else SVG                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `boxy state [--json]`                                                                                                 | what Boxy is doing and the image for it (made again first when the look changed)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `boxy listen start\|stop\|toggle`                                                                                     | hold to talk: `voxtype record start --output-file F`, then `voxtype record stop`, the words go to the default BoxLang agent (thread `bxrig-voice`), the answer comes as a desktop notice and, when speech is on, aloud. Exit 4 without Voxtype                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `boxy say TEXT`                                                                                                       | speaks the text through the speech setting. Exit 4 when it is not set up or no player is found                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `boxy voice [on\|off\|set]`                                                                                           | speech is **off** until `set` has a URL and model and `on` is run. `set --url=U --model=M --voice=V [--key=SECRET_NAME] [--format=wav\|mp3\|opus\|flac]`. Any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` server: a cloud provider, or a local one                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `boxy voice local [--lang=auto\|en\|es] [--voice=NAME] [--accent=latam\|castilian] [--speed=N] [--hear=auto\|en\|es]` | speech on this machine with bx-audio (decided with the owner 2026-11-26). A plan without `--yes` (exit 2); `--yes` fetches the voices (`bx-audio speak`, a few minutes the first time), saves `voice.engine = "bx-audio"` and turns speech on. `--lang=auto` picks the voice from the text (Spanish: `dora` by default; English: `joe`), `--accent` is passed to bx-audio as `BX_AUDIO_ACCENT` (Latin American by default, both offered). `--voice` needs `--lang=en` or `es`. `--hear` sets `language` in `[whisper]` of Voxtype's `config.toml`: Voxtype has no per-recording language flag. Exit 4 without bx-audio |
| `boxy voice list [--lang=en\|es]`, `boxy voice test [--lang=en\|es]`                                                  | the voices bx-audio offers; a spoken sample in the language                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

* **The outfit in `auto`:** the season (beanie Dec to Feb, flower Mar to May, sunglasses Jun to Aug, leaf Sep to Nov); the holiday outfits (`christmas` Dec 20 to 26, `halloween` Oct 24 to 31, `newyear` Dec 31 to Jan 2) only for the holidays you list with `--holidays`; the birthday outfit on the day you set. Test hook: `BXRIG_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`.
* **Never by voice:** approving something Boxy wants to change stays on screen. A pending approval only produces a notice that says so.
* **What leaves the machine:** nothing, until speech is on, and with the local engine (bx-audio) nothing ever does. With speech on, each answer read aloud is sent to the speech server (the privacy report says where; a server on this machine is shown as such). The key is a stored secret name or an environment variable, passed to curl in a mode 600 config file that is deleted after the call, never on the command line.
* **The key:** `Super+Comma` (the traditional style; `Super+Ctrl+Slash` in the Mac style, where Super+Comma is Preferences) and the Copilot key (`Super+Shift+F23`): the press starts listening, the release (`{ release = true }`) sends. Four rows in `keys show`; a press and its release do not count as a conflict.
* **Surfaces:** the Boxy page in the Control Center (`bxrig tui boxy`, before Android: Boxy's sprite, the speech row, and the outfits, Enter puts one on, `v` speech, `e` images), the Boxy tab of the bar's Agents panel (the picture for what it is doing and a Talk button), and the sprite in `bxrig boxy`. The art is concept D, the antenna bot (owner, 2026-11-26): the antenna tip is the BoxLang swirl, lit and turning while it works (four pictures, `frames` in `boxy` and `boxy state`; the bar turns them once a second). The tab also has **Chat** , **Web** and **Logs** , which open bx-agents' own chat (`bxrig ai agents chat`), web page and log viewer (`bxrig ai agents NAME logs --ui`); BxRig keeps no history of its own. The state file is `~/.local/state/bxrig/boxy-state.json`; a state nothing updated for three minutes reads as idle.
* Tests: `tests/boxy_test.bxs` (the calendar, colours, the four images and the sprite, the page, the bar source) and `tests/boxy-test.sh` (a fake Voxtype, notify-send, curl, bx-audio and player: the look and the outfit by date, export, speech off by default and never sent before it is on, the key kept off the command line, hold to talk, silence, no Voxtype, and local speech: the plan, the voices fetched, Spanish and English picked from the text, both accents, Voxtype's language, no bx-audio). **Not tested on a real machine:** a real microphone, Voxtype's service, the Hyprland release bind and Noctalia's image drawing.

title: Command reference
body: Command reference Every command is bxrig NAME ... . This page is generated from docs/reference/cli.json ; the same data answers bxrig help and bxrig help NAME in the terminal. The command contract has the details behind each one. How commands behave Flag What it does --json Print one JSON object instead of text (see below). Every command takes it. --yes Apply a change that installs packages or edits system files. Without it you get the plan and exit code 2. --dry-run Print the plan or the exact commands and exit 0. Nothing is changed. --force Where it exists: replace a file BxRig would otherwise keep because you edited it. Settings that only touch your own config (a theme, the bar, the font) act at once and need no --yes . Exit codes Code Meaning 0 Done, or nothing to do (also --dry-run ). 1 A check came out negative (for example package-status says it is missing). 2 Usage error, or a plan was printed because --yes was not given. 3 Timeout, or the item is not available. 4 A precondition failed: not Arch or CachyOS, a tool or a monitor that is not there, an unknown name. 5 The official (pacman) phase failed. 6 The AUR phase, or the command you asked for, failed. 7 Partial success: some items were done, some failed. 8 Config conflict: a file you edited, or another run is in progress. 9 Internal error. 10 update check : an update is available. JSON { "schema": 1, "command": "dns", "version": "0.11.0", "ok": true, "exit": 0, "dry_run": false, "data": { }, "warnings": [] } data is different for every command; ok is true when exit is 0. Scripts should read exit and data , never the text. All commands Start here : init , refresh , reinstall , wizard , status , doctor , update , scheduler , ascii , about , banner , version , menu , apps , help Install and remove : install , remove , pkg , catalog , plan , install-plan , optional-plan , profile-plan , profile-install-plan , profile-install , optional-install , profile-list , optional-list , desktop-list , tui-list , web-list , package-status , package-source , dev-plan , prerequisites , apps-doctor , web , toolchain Desktop setup : setup , session , tiling , plasma , keys , runner , launcher , default , layout , assets , launchers , config Look and feel : theme , appearance , screensaver , hotcorners , display , power , time , calendar , remind , accessibility , toggle , nightshift , notify System and security : system , security , dns , kernel , ssh , git , secrets , vpn , cloud , settings , dotfiles , nas , backup , timemachine , java , sdk , mail , tui , bxtimemachine , privacy Develop : boxlang , editor , db , containers , vm , android , boxy , ai , mcp , skills Everyday tools : screenshot , qr , share , record , browser , files , webcam , clipboard , emoji , forcequit , window , overview , quicklook , dolphin , dictation , strata , gpu , input , audio , bluetooth , wifi , airplay Start here Set up the machine, see where it stands, keep it current. bxrig init {#bxrig-init} The setup wizard: asks the questions, shows a review, then installs on a progress screen (press v for the live log) and keeps a log file. bxrig init [--from=FILE] [--fresh | --rerun] [--plain] | init --answers=FILE [--yes [--screen]] [--dry-run] [--json] | init --print-answers [--from-system] [--json] | init --export=FILE [--force] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig init bxrig init --answers=answers.json --yes bxrig init --print-answers --from-system --json bxrig refresh {#bxrig-refresh} Put a managed config back to what BxRig ships, with a backup first and without installing anything. bxrig refresh hyprland|noctalia|terminals|shell|nvim|theme|all [--starter] [--force] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] bxrig refresh list [--json] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig refresh list bxrig refresh terminals --dry-run bxrig refresh hyprland --yes bxrig refresh shell --yes --force A file you edited is kept and reported; --force overwrites it after a backup (see config history and config restore). --starter also rewrites the starter hyprland.lua or Noctalia config.toml, which are yours. bxrig reinstall {#bxrig-reinstall} Run the setup wizard again from your saved answers (the same as init --rerun). bxrig reinstall [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] bxrig reinstall This is the way to install packages again. refresh only puts config files back. bxrig wizard {#bxrig-wizard} Wizard pieces for scripts: render the demo screens or a pages file. bxrig wizard --demo [--out=FILE] | --pages=FILE [--out=FILE] [--answers=FILE] bxrig wizard --demo bxrig status {#bxrig-status} What is installed and configured on this machine, compared with what BxRig would do. bxrig status [--json] bxrig status bxrig status --json bxrig doctor {#bxrig-doctor} Checks every tool BxRig needs (git, curl, unzip, jq, Java 21, mvm, bvm, BoxLang, MatchBox, Rust, Cargo), one status line each. Exit 4 when one is missing. --dev adds advice on your developer setup. bxrig doctor [--dev] [--json] bxrig doctor bxrig doctor --dev bxrig doctor --json --dev checks git name and email, an SSH key, the SSH agent, commit signing, a container engine and EDITOR. They print warn with the command that fixes them and never change the exit code. bxrig update {#bxrig-update} Check for a BxRig update, apply it, pick a channel, turn the daily notification on or off. bxrig update check [--notify] | apply [--yes] | channel [stable|beta] | notifications on|off|status [--json] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig update check bxrig update apply --yes bxrig update channel beta bxrig update notifications on Exit 10 from update check means an update is available. bxrig scheduler {#bxrig-scheduler} One scheduler on the BoxLang JVM: the update check, backups, BoxLang checks and your own tasks, with run history. bxrig scheduler [status|list] [--group=G] [--json] bxrig scheduler show NAME [--limit=N] | history NAME [--limit=N] [--json] bxrig scheduler add NAME --when=WHEN [--group=G] [--notify=failure|attention|always|never] [--timeout=SECONDS] -- COMMAND... bxrig scheduler remove NAME | enable NAME | disable NAME | pause GROUP | resume GROUP | run NAME [--json] bxrig scheduler install [--yes] [--dry-run] | uninstall [--yes] [--dry-run] | reload [--json] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig scheduler bxrig scheduler install --yes bxrig scheduler show backup-data bxrig scheduler add photos-to-nas --when="daily 23:00" --group=sync -- rsync -a ~/Pictures nas:/photos bxrig scheduler add tidy-downloads --when="weekly sun 10:00" -- bxrig files tidy bxrig scheduler pause backups WHEN is every N minutes, every N hours, hourly, daily HH:MM, weekdays HH:MM, weekly DAY HH:MM or cron M H DOM MON DOW. install writes the runner (a BoxLang scheduler class) and bxrig-scheduler.service ( boxlang schedule on it), adds the update check, the file backup and the BoxLang check as tasks, and turns off bxrig-update-check.timer and bxrig-backup.timer; it is a plan until --yes. Every run is recorded in ~/.local/state/bxrig/scheduler/history; a failure sends a notice. Exit 10 from a task counts as "needs attention" where the task lists it as ok. bxrig ascii {#bxrig-ascii} Text in large letters (FIGlet fonts) or a picture as text art, painted with a colour or a gradient. bxrig ascii TEXT... [--font=dos-rebel|ansi-shadow|calvin-s] [--color=COLOR | --gradient=SPEC] [--direction=horizontal|vertical|diagonal] [--plain] [--json] bxrig ascii fonts [--json] bxrig ascii image PATH [--width=N] [--style=blocks|ascii] [--plain] [--json] bxrig ascii BxRig bxrig ascii "Hello" --font=ansi-shadow --gradient=sunset bxrig ascii OK --color=#00ff78 bxrig ascii Rainbow --gradient=rainbow --direction=diagonal bxrig ascii Theme --gradient=theme bxrig ascii deploy --gradient=#ff5f6d,#ffc371,#00dbff bxrig ascii fonts bxrig ascii image ~/Pictures/logo.png bxrig ascii image logo.svg --width=60 bxrig ascii image photo.jpg --style=ascii --width=80 COLOR is #rrggbb, #rgb, theme (the accent of the theme that is on) or a name (black, white, gray, red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, magenta, pink, boxlang, bxrig). SPEC is a preset (brand, theme, sunset, ocean, fire, forest, candy, rainbow) or two or more colours separated by commas. Without --color or --gradient the brand gradient is used in a terminal and no colour into a pipe; --plain and NO_COLOR leave colour out. With no TEXT the first line of stdin is drawn. ascii image draws a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG (read by the embedded bx-image module) WIDTH columns wide (default 48): blocks are half blocks in 24-bit colour, ascii is a brightness ramp in the picture's colours; transparent pixels stay blank. bxrig about {#bxrig-about} About this rig: the BxRig laptop logo beside the hardware, your dev stack and the look (fastfetch). bxrig about [--wait] [--plain] [--json] bxrig about bxrig about --plain bxrig about --json Runs fastfetch with /.config/bxrig/fastfetch.jsonc; the logo ( /.config/bxrig/theme/fastfetch-logo.ans) follows the theme and is rewritten by bxrig theme set . A missing logo or config is written first. Without fastfetch the logo, version and tagline are shown. --wait asks for Enter before returning (the launcher's About window uses it). bxrig banner {#bxrig-banner} The BXRIG wordmark in block letters, painted in the colors of the current theme (the retro greeting). bxrig banner [--plain] [--json] bxrig banner bxrig banner --plain bxrig banner --json Five rows, painted top to bottom with the theme's accent, magenta and cyan. A pipe, --plain and NO_COLOR give plain text; --json gives the lines and the three colors. bxrig version {#bxrig-version} The BxRig version and build. bxrig version [--json] bxrig version bxrig menu {#bxrig-menu} The control center: every command as a menu on your launcher (Rofi, Walker, Wofi, Fuzzel or Vicinae). bxrig menu | menu items [--json] | menu search TEXT [--json] | menu open [ROUTE] [--json] bxrig menu ids [--json] | menu file [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] bxrig menu level [PATH] [--json] bxrig menu bxrig menu search 'time zone' bxrig menu open capture bxrig menu ids bxrig menu file --yes bxrig menu level "Trigger > Capture" --json Bind it to a key; the first entry, Search, lists every entry as one flat list. menu open ROUTE opens one submenu (system, capture, toggle, hardware, agent, shortcuts, trigger > capture); menu open lists the routes. A tick marks the current value (bar position, dock, window look, theme mode, power profile). Entries that do not apply here are hidden (laptop, touchpad, touchscreen, webcam, hybrid GPU, Hyprland, Plasma, installed apps); Install hides apps you have. Your own ~/.config/bxrig/menu.json adds entries (a program or a bxrig command under a submenu id), hides and renames entries by id: menu ids lists the ids, menu file --yes writes an example, menu file checks yours. level lists the entries at one level (the top level, or the submenu at PATH) with a glyph and colour role for each: the data the Noctalia menu panel draws. bxrig apps {#bxrig-apps} Your installed catalog apps, as a list or a launcher grid. bxrig apps | apps list [--json] bxrig apps list bxrig help {#bxrig-help} This list, or the usage of one command. bxrig --help and bxrig -h print the same list. bxrig help [COMMAND] bxrig help bxrig help appearance Install and remove Apps from the catalog, any package from the repositories or the AUR, and the reverse. bxrig install {#bxrig-install} Install catalog apps by id (or a whole group or profile). bxrig install [NAME] [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] [--yes] [--dry-run] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig install --dry-run bxrig install --yes With no name it installs the default set; without --yes it prints the plan and changes nothing. bxrig remove {#bxrig-remove} Uninstall catalog apps (their packages or web launchers). bxrig remove ID_OR_PACKAGE... [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig remove lazygit --yes Protected packages (the base system, the kernel, bxrig itself) are refused. bxrig pkg {#bxrig-pkg} Search, inspect, install and remove any package from the repositories and the AUR. bxrig pkg search TEXT [--source=all|repo|aur] [--limit=N] | info NAME | installed [--explicit] | install NAME... [--aur] [--yes] [--dry-run] | remove NAME... [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig pkg search ripgrep bxrig pkg install ripgrep --yes bxrig pkg remove htop --yes bxrig catalog {#bxrig-catalog} Browse the app catalog. bxrig catalog list [--group=G] [--category=C] [--tier=default|optional] [--kind=K] [--source=S] [--distro=D] [--json] | show ID [--distro=D] | groups | check | coverage [--distro=D] | version bxrig catalog map suse|debian|ubuntu [--write] [--json] bxrig catalog coverage bxrig catalog list --distro=suse --tier=default bxrig catalog groups bxrig catalog list --group=ai --tier=default bxrig catalog show lazygit bxrig plan {#bxrig-plan} Show what installing would do, without doing it. bxrig plan [NAME] [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] bxrig plan bxrig plan --shell=hyprland --json bxrig install-plan {#bxrig-install-plan} The install plan for the selection (same as plan). bxrig install-plan [NAME] [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] bxrig optional-plan {#bxrig-optional-plan} The plan for the optional apps. bxrig optional-plan [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] bxrig profile-plan {#bxrig-profile-plan} The plan for one profile. bxrig profile-plan NAME [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] bxrig profile-plan jvm bxrig profile-install-plan {#bxrig-profile-install-plan} The install steps for one profile. bxrig profile-install-plan NAME [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] bxrig profile-install {#bxrig-profile-install} Install a profile (jvm, containers, terminal, editors, ...). bxrig profile-install NAME [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] [--yes] [--dry-run] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig profile-install terminal --yes bxrig optional-install {#bxrig-optional-install} Install the optional apps of the catalog. bxrig optional-install [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] [--yes] [--dry-run] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxrig profile-list {#bxrig-profile-list} List the profiles. bxrig profile-list [--json] bxrig optional-list {#bxrig-optional-list} List the optional apps. bxrig optional-list [--json] bxrig desktop-list {#bxrig-desktop-list} List the desktop apps in the catalog. bxrig desktop-list [--json] bxrig tui-list {#bxrig-tui-list} List the terminal apps in the catalog. bxrig tui-list [--json] bxrig web-list {#bxrig-web-list} List the web apps in the catalog. bxrig web-list [--json] bxrig package-status {#bxrig-package-status} Whether a catalog app is installed. bxrig package-status ID bxrig package-status lazygit bxrig package-source {#bxrig-package-source} Where a catalog app comes from (pacman, AUR, PKGBUILD, web). bxrig package-source ID bxrig package-source lazygit bxrig dev-plan {#bxrig-dev-plan} What the developer toolchain install would use: Java 21, Maven, Gradle, BVM, MVM. bxrig dev-plan bxrig prerequisites {#bxrig-prerequisites} The same check as doctor: one status line per tool BxRig needs. bxrig prerequisites [--json] bxrig apps-doctor {#bxrig-apps-doctor} Checks the catalog apps for missing or broken installs. bxrig apps-doctor [--json] bxrig web {#bxrig-web} Web apps: create one from a URL, install a set (Google, Microsoft, Apple, BoxLang). bxrig web add [NAME URL] [--browser=brave|chromium|google-chrome|edge|firefox] [--yes] | list | rm NAME [--yes] | install google|microsoft|apple|boxlang|all [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] Changes the system: needs --yes . # Command reference

Every command is `bxrig NAME ...`. This page is generated from `docs/reference/cli.json`; the same data answers `bxrig help` and `bxrig help NAME` in the terminal. The [command contract](/architecture/COMMAND-CONTRACT/index.html) has the details behind each one.

## How commands behave

|    Flag     |                                               What it does                                                |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--json`    | Print one JSON object instead of text (see below). Every command takes it.                                |
| `--yes`     | Apply a change that installs packages or edits system files. Without it you get the plan and exit code 2. |
| `--dry-run` | Print the plan or the exact commands and exit 0. Nothing is changed.                                      |
| `--force`   | Where it exists: replace a file BxRig would otherwise keep because you edited it.                         |

Settings that only touch your own config (a theme, the bar, the font) act at once and need no `--yes`.

### Exit codes

| Code |                                               Meaning                                               |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | Done, or nothing to do (also `--dry-run`).                                                          |
| 1    | A check came out negative (for example `package-status` says it is missing).                        |
| 2    | Usage error, or a plan was printed because `--yes` was not given.                                   |
| 3    | Timeout, or the item is not available.                                                              |
| 4    | A precondition failed: not Arch or CachyOS, a tool or a monitor that is not there, an unknown name. |
| 5    | The official (pacman) phase failed.                                                                 |
| 6    | The AUR phase, or the command you asked for, failed.                                                |
| 7    | Partial success: some items were done, some failed.                                                 |
| 8    | Config conflict: a file you edited, or another run is in progress.                                  |
| 9    | Internal error.                                                                                     |
| 10   | `update check`: an update is available.                                                             |

### JSON

```json
{ "schema": 1, "command": "dns", "version": "0.11.0", "ok": true, "exit": 0, "dry_run": false, "data": { }, "warnings": [] }
```

`data` is different for every command; `ok` is true when `exit` is 0. Scripts should read `exit` and `data`, never the text.

## Start here

Set up the machine, see where it stands, keep it current.

### `bxrig init` {#bxrig-init}

The setup wizard: asks the questions, shows a review, then installs on a progress screen (press v for the live log) and keeps a log file.

```text
bxrig init [--from=FILE] [--fresh | --rerun] [--plain] | init --answers=FILE [--yes [--screen]] [--dry-run] [--json] | init --print-answers [--from-system] [--json] | init --export=FILE [--force]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig init
bxrig init --answers=answers.json --yes
bxrig init --print-answers --from-system --json
```

### `bxrig refresh` {#bxrig-refresh}

Put a managed config back to what BxRig ships, with a backup first and without installing anything.

```text
bxrig refresh hyprland|noctalia|terminals|shell|nvim|theme|all [--starter] [--force] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
bxrig refresh list [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig refresh list
bxrig refresh terminals --dry-run
bxrig refresh hyprland --yes
bxrig refresh shell --yes --force
```

> A file you edited is kept and reported; --force overwrites it after a backup (see config history and config restore). --starter also rewrites the starter hyprland.lua or Noctalia config.toml, which are yours.

### `bxrig reinstall` {#bxrig-reinstall}

Run the setup wizard again from your saved answers (the same as init --rerun).

```text
bxrig reinstall [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig reinstall
```

> This is the way to install packages again. refresh only puts config files back.

### `bxrig wizard` {#bxrig-wizard}

Wizard pieces for scripts: render the demo screens or a pages file.

```text
bxrig wizard --demo [--out=FILE] | --pages=FILE [--out=FILE] [--answers=FILE]
```

```bash
bxrig wizard --demo
```

### `bxrig status` {#bxrig-status}

What is installed and configured on this machine, compared with what BxRig would do.

```text
bxrig status [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig status
bxrig status --json
```

### `bxrig doctor` {#bxrig-doctor}

Checks every tool BxRig needs (git, curl, unzip, jq, Java 21, mvm, bvm, BoxLang, MatchBox, Rust, Cargo), one status line each. Exit 4 when one is missing. --dev adds advice on your developer setup.

```text
bxrig doctor [--dev] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig doctor
bxrig doctor --dev
bxrig doctor --json
```

> --dev checks git name and email, an SSH key, the SSH agent, commit signing, a container engine and EDITOR. They print warn with the command that fixes them and never change the exit code.

### `bxrig update` {#bxrig-update}

Check for a BxRig update, apply it, pick a channel, turn the daily notification on or off.

```text
bxrig update check [--notify] | apply [--yes] | channel [stable|beta] | notifications on|off|status [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig update check
bxrig update apply --yes
bxrig update channel beta
bxrig update notifications on
```

> Exit 10 from `update check` means an update is available.

### `bxrig scheduler` {#bxrig-scheduler}

One scheduler on the BoxLang JVM: the update check, backups, BoxLang checks and your own tasks, with run history.

```text
bxrig scheduler [status|list] [--group=G] [--json]
bxrig scheduler show NAME [--limit=N] | history NAME [--limit=N] [--json]
bxrig scheduler add NAME --when=WHEN [--group=G] [--notify=failure|attention|always|never] [--timeout=SECONDS] -- COMMAND...
bxrig scheduler remove NAME | enable NAME | disable NAME | pause GROUP | resume GROUP | run NAME [--json]
bxrig scheduler install [--yes] [--dry-run] | uninstall [--yes] [--dry-run] | reload [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig scheduler
bxrig scheduler install --yes
bxrig scheduler show backup-data
bxrig scheduler add photos-to-nas --when="daily 23:00" --group=sync -- rsync -a ~/Pictures nas:/photos
bxrig scheduler add tidy-downloads --when="weekly sun 10:00" -- bxrig files tidy
bxrig scheduler pause backups
```

> WHEN is every N minutes, every N hours, hourly, daily HH:MM, weekdays HH:MM, weekly DAY HH:MM or cron M H DOM MON DOW. install writes the runner (a BoxLang scheduler class) and bxrig-scheduler.service (`boxlang schedule` on it), adds the update check, the file backup and the BoxLang check as tasks, and turns off bxrig-update-check.timer and bxrig-backup.timer; it is a plan until --yes. Every run is recorded in \~/.local/state/bxrig/scheduler/history; a failure sends a notice. Exit 10 from a task counts as "needs attention" where the task lists it as ok.

### `bxrig ascii` {#bxrig-ascii}

Text in large letters (FIGlet fonts) or a picture as text art, painted with a colour or a gradient.

```text
bxrig ascii TEXT... [--font=dos-rebel|ansi-shadow|calvin-s] [--color=COLOR | --gradient=SPEC] [--direction=horizontal|vertical|diagonal] [--plain] [--json]
bxrig ascii fonts [--json]
bxrig ascii image PATH [--width=N] [--style=blocks|ascii] [--plain] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig ascii BxRig
bxrig ascii "Hello" --font=ansi-shadow --gradient=sunset
bxrig ascii OK --color=#00ff78
bxrig ascii Rainbow --gradient=rainbow --direction=diagonal
bxrig ascii Theme --gradient=theme
bxrig ascii deploy --gradient=#ff5f6d,#ffc371,#00dbff
bxrig ascii fonts
bxrig ascii image ~/Pictures/logo.png
bxrig ascii image logo.svg --width=60
bxrig ascii image photo.jpg --style=ascii --width=80
```

> COLOR is #rrggbb, #rgb, theme (the accent of the theme that is on) or a name (black, white, gray, red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, magenta, pink, boxlang, bxrig). SPEC is a preset (brand, theme, sunset, ocean, fire, forest, candy, rainbow) or two or more colours separated by commas. Without --color or --gradient the brand gradient is used in a terminal and no colour into a pipe; --plain and NO_COLOR leave colour out. With no TEXT the first line of stdin is drawn. `ascii image` draws a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG (read by the embedded bx-image module) WIDTH columns wide (default 48): blocks are half blocks in 24-bit colour, ascii is a brightness ramp in the picture's colours; transparent pixels stay blank.

### `bxrig about` {#bxrig-about}

About this rig: the BxRig laptop logo beside the hardware, your dev stack and the look (fastfetch).

```text
bxrig about [--wait] [--plain] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig about
bxrig about --plain
bxrig about --json
```

> Runs fastfetch with ~/.config/bxrig/fastfetch.jsonc; the logo (~/.config/bxrig/theme/fastfetch-logo.ans) follows the theme and is rewritten by `bxrig theme set`. A missing logo or config is written first. Without fastfetch the logo, version and tagline are shown. --wait asks for Enter before returning (the launcher's About window uses it).

### `bxrig banner` {#bxrig-banner}

The BXRIG wordmark in block letters, painted in the colors of the current theme (the retro greeting).

```text
bxrig banner [--plain] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig banner
bxrig banner --plain
bxrig banner --json
```

> Five rows, painted top to bottom with the theme's accent, magenta and cyan. A pipe, --plain and NO_COLOR give plain text; --json gives the lines and the three colors.

### `bxrig version` {#bxrig-version}

The BxRig version and build.

```text
bxrig version [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig version
```

### `bxrig menu` {#bxrig-menu}

The control center: every command as a menu on your launcher (Rofi, Walker, Wofi, Fuzzel or Vicinae).

```text
bxrig menu | menu items [--json] | menu search TEXT [--json] | menu open [ROUTE] [--json]
bxrig menu ids [--json] | menu file [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
bxrig menu level [PATH] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig menu
bxrig menu search 'time zone'
bxrig menu open capture
bxrig menu ids
bxrig menu file --yes
bxrig menu level "Trigger > Capture" --json
```

> Bind it to a key; the first entry, Search, lists every entry as one flat list. `menu open ROUTE` opens one submenu (system, capture, toggle, hardware, agent, shortcuts, trigger \> capture); `menu open` lists the routes. A tick marks the current value (bar position, dock, window look, theme mode, power profile). Entries that do not apply here are hidden (laptop, touchpad, touchscreen, webcam, hybrid GPU, Hyprland, Plasma, installed apps); Install hides apps you have. Your own \~/.config/bxrig/menu.json adds entries (a program or a bxrig command under a submenu id), hides and renames entries by id: `menu ids` lists the ids, `menu file --yes` writes an example, `menu file` checks yours. level lists the entries at one level (the top level, or the submenu at PATH) with a glyph and colour role for each: the data the Noctalia menu panel draws.

### `bxrig apps` {#bxrig-apps}

Your installed catalog apps, as a list or a launcher grid.

```text
bxrig apps | apps list [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig apps list
```

### `bxrig help` {#bxrig-help}

This list, or the usage of one command. `bxrig --help` and `bxrig -h` print the same list.

```text
bxrig help [COMMAND]
```

```bash
bxrig help
bxrig help appearance
```

## Install and remove

Apps from the catalog, any package from the repositories or the AUR, and the reverse.

### `bxrig install` {#bxrig-install}

Install catalog apps by id (or a whole group or profile).

```text
bxrig install [NAME] [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] [--yes] [--dry-run]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig install --dry-run
bxrig install --yes
```

> With no name it installs the default set; without --yes it prints the plan and changes nothing.

### `bxrig remove` {#bxrig-remove}

Uninstall catalog apps (their packages or web launchers).

```text
bxrig remove ID_OR_PACKAGE... [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig remove lazygit --yes
```

> Protected packages (the base system, the kernel, bxrig itself) are refused.

### `bxrig pkg` {#bxrig-pkg}

Search, inspect, install and remove any package from the repositories and the AUR.

```text
bxrig pkg search TEXT [--source=all|repo|aur] [--limit=N] | info NAME | installed [--explicit] | install NAME... [--aur] [--yes] [--dry-run] | remove NAME... [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig pkg search ripgrep
bxrig pkg install ripgrep --yes
bxrig pkg remove htop --yes
```

### `bxrig catalog` {#bxrig-catalog}

Browse the app catalog.

```text
bxrig catalog list [--group=G] [--category=C] [--tier=default|optional] [--kind=K] [--source=S] [--distro=D] [--json] | show ID [--distro=D] | groups | check | coverage [--distro=D] | version
bxrig catalog map suse|debian|ubuntu [--write] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig catalog coverage
bxrig catalog list --distro=suse --tier=default
bxrig catalog groups
bxrig catalog list --group=ai --tier=default
bxrig catalog show lazygit
```

### `bxrig plan` {#bxrig-plan}

Show what installing would do, without doing it.

```text
bxrig plan [NAME] [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig plan
bxrig plan --shell=hyprland --json
```

### `bxrig install-plan` {#bxrig-install-plan}

The install plan for the selection (same as plan).

```text
bxrig install-plan [NAME] [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json]
```

### `bxrig optional-plan` {#bxrig-optional-plan}

The plan for the optional apps.

```text
bxrig optional-plan [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json]
```

### `bxrig profile-plan` {#bxrig-profile-plan}

The plan for one profile.

```text
bxrig profile-plan NAME [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig profile-plan jvm
```

### `bxrig profile-install-plan` {#bxrig-profile-install-plan}

The install steps for one profile.

```text
bxrig profile-install-plan NAME [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json]
```

### `bxrig profile-install` {#bxrig-profile-install}

Install a profile (jvm, containers, terminal, editors, ...).

```text
bxrig profile-install NAME [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] [--yes] [--dry-run]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig profile-install terminal --yes
```

### `bxrig optional-install` {#bxrig-optional-install}

Install the optional apps of the catalog.

```text
bxrig optional-install [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] [--yes] [--dry-run]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

### `bxrig profile-list` {#bxrig-profile-list}

List the profiles.

```text
bxrig profile-list [--json]
```

### `bxrig optional-list` {#bxrig-optional-list}

List the optional apps.

```text
bxrig optional-list [--json]
```

### `bxrig desktop-list` {#bxrig-desktop-list}

> updates only reads: repository and AUR counts and the package list, and whether a restart is needed (exit 4 without checkupdates from pacman-contrib). update takes a snapshot first, then updates the repository (--repo), the AUR (--aur, exit 4 without yay or paru) or both (--all, the default). lock and suspend act at once; logout, reboot and shutdown need --yes (the menu asks first). restart shell stops and starts Noctalia (or restarts Plasma's plasmashell service); audio restarts PipeWire and WirePlumber; wifi and bluetooth unblock the radio and turn it on. password runs passwd on your terminal. firmware asks fwupd (LVFS: BIOS/UEFI, SSDs, docks) for updates; update installs them on your terminal. speedtest network runs speedtest-cli; disk writes and reads 1 GiB in \~/.cache with direct I/O; dns is dns bench; last shows the last result of each test (only the latest is kept, in \~/.local/state/bxrig/speedtest-last.json).

```text
bxrig ai ask TEXT [--model=ID] [--json]
bxrig ai agents [list] [--json]
bxrig ai agents install|update [--snapshot|--stable] [--yes] [--dry-run]
bxrig ai agents new NAME [bxAgents new flags]
bxrig ai agents NAME VERB [bxAgents flags]
bxrig ai agents start|stop|status NAME [--json]
bxrig ai agents open [NAME]
bxrig ai agents chat [NAME] [--window]
bxrig ai agents ask TEXT [--agent=NAME] [--thread=ID] [--json]
bxrig ai agents approve|reject THREAD [--agent=NAME] [--session] [--json]
bxrig ai agents setup [--no-start] [--yes] [--dry-run]
bxrig ai agents skills [NAME] [show|approve|remove SKILL] [--all] [--yes] [--json]
bxrig ai agents default [NAME]

bxrig ai list
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig ai setup --yes
bxrig ai models recommend
bxrig ai models pull gemma-4-e4b --yes
```
