### `bxrig mcp` {#bxrig-mcp}

BxRig's own tools for any coding agent or editor, as an MCP server (Boxy's tools, read-only unless --write).

```text
bxrig mcp [--json] | tools | serve [--write] | link [AGENT...] [--write] [--yes] | unlink [AGENT...] [--yes] [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig mcp
bxrig mcp link --yes
bxrig mcp link pi-agent claude-code --write --yes
bxrig mcp tools
```

### `bxrig skills` {#bxrig-skills}

Agent skills for BoxLang and BxRig: install, update, remove.

```text
bxrig skills list [--tag=T] | search TEXT | show OWNER/REPO/SLUG | install [bxrig|boxlang|matchbox|OWNER/REPO/SLUG]... [--yes] | installed | update [--yes] | remove NAME [--yes] | status | link [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig skills install --yes
bxrig skills list
bxrig skills status
```

## Everyday tools

Screenshots, clipboard, windows, dictation and hardware helpers.

### `bxrig screenshot` {#bxrig-screenshot}

Screenshots: screen, region, window, OCR text, QR codes, a color picker, or a menu.

```text
bxrig screenshot screen|region|window [--edit] | ocr | qr | color | menu [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig screenshot region
bxrig screenshot screen --edit
bxrig screenshot ocr
bxrig screenshot color
```

### `bxrig qr` {#bxrig-qr}

Make a QR code from text (printed in the terminal, or saved with --out).

```text
bxrig qr TEXT [--out=FILE.png] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig qr https://boxlang.io
bxrig qr 'wifi text' --out=wifi.png
```

### `bxrig share` {#bxrig-share}

Send files, a folder or the clipboard to a phone or computer nearby with LocalSend, or open it to receive.

```text
bxrig share file [PATH...] | folder [PATH] | clipboard [--to=DEVICE] [--dry-run] [--json]
bxrig share receive [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig share file report.pdf
bxrig share folder ~/Photos/trip --to="Pixel 9"
bxrig share clipboard
bxrig share receive
```

> Sending uses LocalSend's command line, localsend-cli (LocalSend 1.18 and later): without --to it lists the devices it finds and you pick one, on your terminal (the menu opens one). Without a path a file chooser asks (kdialog on Plasma, else zenity). clipboard sends what you copied as a text file. receive opens the LocalSend app. Exit 4 when localsend-cli or LocalSend is missing.

### `bxrig record` {#bxrig-record}

Screen recording: start, stop, toggle, with desktop or microphone audio if you like.

```text
bxrig record [toggle|start|stop|status] [--region] [--audio=desktop|mic] [--webcam[=bottom-right|bottom-left|top-right|top-left]] [--webcam-size=small|medium|large] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig record toggle
bxrig record start --region
bxrig record toggle --audio=desktop
bxrig record toggle --webcam
bxrig record start --webcam=top-left --webcam-size=small --audio=mic
```

> --audio=desktop adds what the speakers play, --audio=mic the default microphone (both through pactl). Desktop and microphone together are not offered: wf-recorder takes one audio source. Exit 2 for another audio value. --webcam puts your webcam in a corner while it records (bottom-right unless you name another), so it is in the video; it ends with the recording. Hyprland pins it (the BxRig module's rules); on Plasma it is a small window you can drag.

### `bxrig browser` {#bxrig-browser}

Your default browser in a private window.

```text
bxrig browser private [URL] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig browser private
bxrig browser private https://example.com --dry-run
```

> Reads the default web browser (set by `default browser` or the wizard) and starts it with its private flag: Firefox --private-window, Chromium, Brave and Chrome --incognito, Edge --inprivate. Another browser exits 4.

### `bxrig files` {#bxrig-files}

Your default file manager in the folder of the focused window.

```text
bxrig files here [DIR] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig files here
bxrig files here ~/Documents
```

> Without DIR it uses the working directory of the focused window's newest child process (Hyprland), else your home folder, and opens it with xdg-open, so `default filemanager` decides which file manager.

### `bxrig webcam` {#bxrig-webcam}

A small live webcam preview, on or off with one key.

```text
bxrig webcam toggle|status [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig webcam toggle
bxrig webcam status
```

> mpv on /dev/video0 in a window of class bxrig-webcam, which the Hyprland module floats and sizes. Exit 4 without mpv or a webcam.

### `bxrig clipboard` {#bxrig-clipboard}

Clipboard history (cliphist): pick, list, show, copy, clear, status.

```text
bxrig clipboard pick | status [--json]
bxrig clipboard list [QUERY] [--limit=N] [--json]
bxrig clipboard show ID | copy ID [--json]
bxrig clipboard clear [--yes]
```

```bash
bxrig clipboard pick
bxrig clipboard list token --json
bxrig clipboard copy 42
```

> list gives the history newest first as rows { id, kind, preview, chars } (text and images). show prints one entry in full (text up to 4000 characters). copy puts an entry back on the clipboard. The launcher panel uses these three.

### `bxrig emoji` {#bxrig-emoji}

The emoji picker (rofimoji).

```text
bxrig emoji
```

```bash
bxrig emoji
```

### `bxrig forcequit` {#bxrig-forcequit}

Pick a window or process and force quit it.

```text
bxrig forcequit
```

```bash
bxrig forcequit
```

### `bxrig window` {#bxrig-window}

Minimize, restore and snap windows, and the quake console.

```text
bxrig window minimize|restore|quake [--json]
bxrig window quake send [--json]
bxrig window snap left|right|top|bottom [--json]
bxrig window close-all | tiled-fullscreen [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig window minimize
bxrig window restore
bxrig window quake
bxrig window quake send
bxrig window snap left
bxrig window tiled-fullscreen
```

> quake shows or hides the special workspace qconsole (the default terminal starts there the first time); quake send moves the focused window onto it. snap left\|right\|top\|bottom floats the focused window onto that half of its monitor. Hyprland only. close-all asks every window to close (apps with unsaved work still ask), then goes to workspace 1; tiled-fullscreen makes the app full screen inside its tile (again to undo).

### `bxrig overview` {#bxrig-overview}

The workspace and window overview.

```text
bxrig overview [setup]
```

```bash
bxrig overview
```

### `bxrig quicklook` {#bxrig-quicklook}

Quick Look for files (Kiview): preview with a key.

```text
bxrig quicklook [PATH] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig quicklook photo.jpg
```

### `bxrig dolphin` {#bxrig-dolphin}

Dolphin diagnostics: why it is slow or missing features.

```text
bxrig dolphin doctor [--fix] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig dolphin doctor
bxrig dolphin doctor --fix
```

### `bxrig dictation` {#bxrig-dictation}

Dictation with Superwhisper or Voxtype: setup and toggle.

```text
bxrig dictation setup [superwhisper|voxtype] [--yes] | status | key [ENGINE] | toggle [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig dictation setup voxtype --yes
bxrig dictation status
bxrig dictation toggle
```

### `bxrig strata` {#bxrig-strata}

Strata, the file manager: its integrations.

```text
bxrig strata integrations [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig strata integrations --dry-run
```

### `bxrig gpu` {#bxrig-gpu}

GPU check: driver, rendering, NVIDIA specifics; the mode of a laptop with two GPUs.

```text
bxrig gpu doctor [--json]
bxrig gpu mode [status] [--json]
bxrig gpu mode hybrid|integrated [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig gpu doctor
bxrig gpu mode
bxrig gpu mode integrated --yes
```

> mode needs two GPUs (counted in /sys/bus/pci/devices) and supergfxctl (supergfxd); a switch is `supergfxctl -m Hybrid|Integrated`, then log out or reboot.

### `bxrig input` {#bxrig-input}

Input devices: Apple Magic Mouse and Trackpad, Logitech, the helpers for them, the older doctor and trackpad gestures.

```text
bxrig input status [--json]
bxrig input offer [--for=detect|apple|logitech|both|none] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
bxrig input apple [--scroll-speed=0..63] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
bxrig input logitech [--json]
bxrig input undo [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
bxrig input doctor | gestures [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
bxrig input touchpad|touchscreen [on|off|toggle|status] [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxrig input status
bxrig input offer --dry-run
bxrig input apple --scroll-speed=48 --yes
bxrig input logitech
bxrig input touchpad off
```

> touchpad and touchscreen switch the device off and on in a Hyprland session (hyprctl eval hl.device); a login turns it back on.

### `bxrig audio` {#bxrig-audio}

Sound server status: outputs, inputs, volumes and the defaults.

```text
bxrig audio status [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig audio status
bxrig audio status --json
```

> Read only, through `pactl`. Volume and mixing are in the bar panel (Super+Ctrl+A) and in the terminal mixer in the Hardware menu. Exit 4 when `pactl` is missing or no sound server answers.

### `bxrig bluetooth` {#bxrig-bluetooth}

Bluetooth status: the service, the adapter and the paired devices.

```text
bxrig bluetooth status [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig bluetooth status
bxrig bluetooth status --json
```

> Read only, through `bluetoothctl` and `systemctl`. Pairing is in the bar panel (Super+Ctrl+B) and in the terminal UI in the Hardware menu. Exit 4 when `bluetoothctl` is missing.

### `bxrig wifi` {#bxrig-wifi}

Wi-Fi status: the radio, the Wi-Fi devices and the network you are on; a QR code to join it.

```text
bxrig wifi status [--json]
bxrig wifi qr [--out=FILE.png] [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig wifi status
bxrig wifi status --json
bxrig wifi qr
bxrig wifi qr --out=wifi.png
```

> Read only, through `nmcli` (NetworkManager). Joining a network is in the bar panel (Super+Ctrl+N). Exit 4 when `nmcli` is missing. qr draws the network you are on as a QR code a phone camera reads to join (qrencode); the password is in the code only, never printed.

### `bxrig airplay` {#bxrig-airplay}

AirPlay receiver: on, off, status.

```text
bxrig airplay on|off|status [--json]
```

```bash
bxrig airplay on
```

markdown:
# Distributions

BxRig runs on:

|         Distribution          |  Package manager  |                                                            Notes                                                             |
|-------------------------------|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| CachyOS, Arch Linux           | pacman, AUR (yay) | The reference platform: every app and feature.                                                                               |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed, Slowroll | zypper            | Flatpak for apps zypper lacks.                                                                                               |
| Ubuntu 26.04 LTS              | apt               | Noctalia from its own apt repository. Flatpak for apps apt lacks.                                                            |
| Debian 13 (trixie)            | apt               | Hyprland from trixie-backports, Noctalia from its own apt repository. kitty is the default terminal (Debian has no ghostty). |

BxRig works out which one you are on from `/etc/os-release`. Other systems are not supported.

## The catalog per distribution

The app catalog has two parts:

* `catalog/apps.json` says what each app is: its name, category, tier and profiles. It is the same everywhere.
* `catalog/install/DISTRO.json` says how to install it on that distribution: the packages, Flathub, or a script. `ubuntu.json` extends `debian.json` and lists only what differs.

An app that a distribution's file does not list is not offered there. `bxrig catalog show ID` says so.

```bash
bxrig catalog coverage                 # how many apps each distribution offers
bxrig catalog list --distro debian     # the catalog as another distribution sees it
bxrig catalog check                    # validates every install file
```

When the distribution has no package for an app, BxRig installs it from Flathub, for your user only (`flatpak install --user`). It adds the Flathub remote, and installs flatpak first, when they are missing.

## Extra repositories

Some packages come from outside the main archive. BxRig adds these repositories only when the install needs them, and only once:

* **Debian 13:** `trixie-backports`, for Hyprland and its tools (hyprland, hypridle, hyprlock, uwsm, the portal, quickshell). They install with `apt-get install -t trixie-backports`, so the newer libraries they need come from backports too. A system that already lists backports is left as it is.
* **Debian 13 and Ubuntu 26.04:** Noctalia's apt repository at pkg.noctalia.dev, for the `noctalia` shell.

## Plasma tiling (HyprKwin)

`bxrig setup plasma` installs HyprKwin, which needs Plasma 6.6 or newer on Wayland. Debian 13 ships Plasma 6.3, so `setup plasma` stops there with that reason; use `bxrig setup hyprland` instead. Check your version with `bxrig setup status`.

## What is Arch-only

* **The AUR.** `bxrig pkg search --aur` and AUR installs work only on Arch.
* **`bxrig kernel`.** Kernel switching uses Arch's kernel packages.
* **The boot splash.** It is built with mkinitcpio.
* **xremap.** On other distributions, install it yourself (its release binary or `cargo install`). BxRig then configures it the same way.
* **Nerd Fonts packages.** openSUSE, Debian and Ubuntu do not package them. `bxrig appearance font install` says so and points to nerdfonts.com.

## Contributing an install file

`bxrig catalog map DISTRO` proposes the install file for a distribution. Run it on that distribution (a container is enough). It asks the package manager for each app's Arch package names, then Flathub, and reports each app as found, flatpak or missing. With `--write` it updates `catalog/install/DISTRO.json`. Review the result before you commit it.

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD":/src -w /src debian:trixie bash
bxrig catalog map debian --write
```

Arch names spelled differently on a distribution go in the file's `names` map (for example `fd` is `fd-find` on Debian). An empty value means the distribution needs nothing for that package. In a file that `extends` another, `{ "source": "none" }` drops an app the parent offers and this release lacks.

# BxRig

**BxRig** brings an opinionated, beautiful and efficient desktop to Linux, built for developers. It turns a fresh CachyOS or Arch install into a finished developer rig: Hyprland with Noctalia (KDE Plasma stays installed beside it), BoxLang and MatchBox, your apps, your shell, your AI agents, all chosen in one guided setup. It is a single native program written in [BoxLang](https://boxlang.io) and compiled with [MatchBox](https://matchbox.boxlang.io).

**Supported: CachyOS, Arch Linux, openSUSE Tumbleweed and Slowroll, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and Debian 13.** See [Distributions](/start/distributions/index.html) for what each one offers.

*This is the documentation for version 1.0.x.*

![BxRig: the BxRig theme with its wallpaper, the bar and a themed terminal](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig.webp)

Twenty-four themes, each with its own wallpaper: see them all in [Themes](/customize/themes/index.html).

## Pick your path

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["New here"] --> B["Start here"]
    B --> C["Daily desktop"]
    C --> D["Customize"]
    D --> E["Build, AI, data, maintain"]
    E --> F["Developer: extend BxRig"]
```

Install in one command, answer the wizard, take the first-hour tour.

Themes, bar, fonts, shortcuts and your own config files, from the first tweak to deep tweaking.

The control center, shortcuts, launcher and system settings.

Add a command, a theme, an app, a shortcut, a wizard page, a bar plugin or an agent skill.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash
```

It checks your machine, downloads and verifies the release, installs everything, then starts the setup wizard. See [Install](/start/install/index.html).

## What you get

|                   Section                   |                                  What is in it                                   |
|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Start here](/start/index.html)             | Install, the wizard, your first hour, troubleshooting                            |
| [Daily desktop](/desktop/index.html)        | Hyprland and Noctalia, the menu, shortcuts, the launcher, monitors and power     |
| [Customize](/customize/index.html)          | Themes, bar and dock, fonts, accessibility, Boxy's look, your own config         |
| [Build software](/build/index.html)         | BoxLang and MatchBox, developer tools, databases, VMs, the mail catcher, Android |
| [AI](/ai/index.html)                        | Coding agents, local models, your own BoxLang agents, MCP and privacy            |
| [Apps and your data](/data/index.html)      | The app catalog, BxTimeMachine backups, NAS, the scheduler                       |
| [Keep it healthy](/maintain/index.html)     | Updates and channels, security, caches                                           |
| [Developer](/developer/index.html)          | Architecture, tutorials for every extension point, tests, releases               |
| [Reference](/reference/commands/index.html) | Every command and flag, config files                                             |

## How it behaves

* Nothing changes until you say so: every command prints a plan and needs `--yes`.
* Files you edit are kept. BxRig only rewrites files it wrote itself.
* Everything is also a command, with `--json` output, so you can script it.

title: How it fits together
body: How it fits together BxRig is one BoxLang program compiled with MatchBox into a single binary. This page is the map. The full rules are in the command contract . The shape of the code bxrig time zone Europe/Madrid --yes travels through three layers. The diagram shows who calls whom. flowchart TD U["bxrig command line"] --> M["src/Main.bx: checks flags, routes by name"] M --> F["src/bxrig: one class per feature, for example Time"] F --> H["src/bxrig/util: shared helpers"] H --> H1["Cli and Out: output and --json"] H --> H2["Mutation: plan, dry run, run"] H --> H3["Proc: starts programs"] H --> H4["Env: paths and variables"] H --> H5["ConfigService: safe file writes"] R["Data files as MatchBox resources"] --> F Layer Where Job Router src/Main.bx One case per command. Checks flags against docs/reference/cli.json , then hands the words to a class. Features src/bxrig/*.bx One class per feature ( Time , Theme , Db , Shortcuts , ...). Holds the logic and returns an exit code. Helpers src/bxrig/util/*.bx The one home for each concern: output, processes, paths, file writes, parsing. Data catalog/ , templates/ , themes/ , skills/ , assets/ , cli.json Packed into the binary as MatchBox resources and read through bxrig.util.Res . From source they are read from disk. Tip: Before you write a helper, search src/bxrig/util/ . If it exists, use it. See Code rules . The rules every changing command follows Four promises, the same for every command that installs, writes or removes something. Plan first. Without --yes the command prints the exact plan, changes nothing and exits 2. --dry-run is safe. With --dry-run it prints the plan or the exact commands and exits 0. --json is one object. Every command can print a single JSON envelope instead of text. Exit codes mean something. Scripts can tell "bad usage" from "tool missing" from "step failed". Settings that only touch your own config (a theme, the bar) act at once and take --dry-run . Anything that installs packages or writes system files always needs --yes . # How it fits together

BxRig is one BoxLang program compiled with MatchBox into a single binary. This page is the map. The full rules are in the [command contract](/architecture/COMMAND-CONTRACT/index.html).

## The shape of the code

`bxrig time zone Europe/Madrid --yes` travels through three layers. The diagram shows who calls whom.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  U["bxrig command line"] --> M["src/Main.bx: checks flags, routes by name"]
  M --> F["src/bxrig: one class per feature, for example Time"]
  F --> H["src/bxrig/util: shared helpers"]
  H --> H1["Cli and Out: output and --json"]
  H --> H2["Mutation: plan, dry run, run"]
  H --> H3["Proc: starts programs"]
  H --> H4["Env: paths and variables"]
  H --> H5["ConfigService: safe file writes"]
  R["Data files as MatchBox resources"] --> F
```

|  Layer   |                                 Where                                 |                                                         Job                                                          |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Router   | `src/Main.bx`                                                         | One `case` per command. Checks flags against `docs/reference/cli.json`, then hands the words to a class.             |
| Features | `src/bxrig/*.bx`                                                      | One class per feature (`Time`, `Theme`, `Db`, `Shortcuts`, ...). Holds the logic and returns an exit code.           |
| Helpers  | `src/bxrig/util/*.bx`                                                 | The one home for each concern: output, processes, paths, file writes, parsing.                                       |
| Data     | `catalog/`, `templates/`, `themes/`, `skills/`, `assets/`, `cli.json` | Packed into the binary as MatchBox resources and read through `bxrig.util.Res`. From source they are read from disk. |

> **Tip:** Before you write a helper, search `src/bxrig/util/`. If it exists, use it. See [Code rules](/developer/code-rules/index.html).

## The rules every changing command follows

Four promises, the same for every command that installs, writes or removes something.

1. **Plan first.** Without `--yes` the command prints the exact plan, changes nothing and exits 2.
2. **`--dry-run` is safe.** With `--dry-run` it prints the plan or the exact commands and exits 0.
3. **`--json` is one object.** Every command can print a single JSON envelope instead of text.
4. **Exit codes mean something.** Scripts can tell "bad usage" from "tool missing" from "step failed".

Settings that only touch your own config (a theme, the bar) act at once and take `--dry-run`. Anything that installs packages or writes system files always needs `--yes`.

### Life of a changing command

The diagram follows one run from the command line to the exit code.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["bxrig NAME ARGS"] --> B{"Valid input and tools present?"}
  B -- "no" --> E1["Exit 2 usage or 4 precondition"]
  B -- "yes" --> C{"Was --yes given?"}
  C -- "no" --> P["Print Plan, change nothing, exit 2"]
  C -- "yes" --> D{"Was --dry-run given?"}
  D -- "yes" --> DR["Print Dry run, exit 0"]
  D -- "no" --> W["Run the steps in order"]
  W --> F["Files: backup, atomic write, journal"]
  F --> R["Result envelope, exit 0, 6 or 7"]
```

All of this comes from two helpers, so a command never writes it by hand:

* `Out.plan` and `Mutation.run` print the plan, honour `--dry-run` and run the steps (the first failing step stops the run, exit 6).
* `ConfigService` writes files: it takes a backup, replaces the file atomically, records a journal entry and holds a lock (a file you edited or a symlink target is a conflict, exit 8).

### Exit codes in plain language

| Code |   Name in code   |                     Means                      |
|------|------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | `ok`             | Done, or nothing to do.                        |
| 2    | `usage` / `plan` | Bad usage, or you only got the plan.           |
| 4    | `precondition`   | A tool, monitor or name is missing.            |
| 6    | `failed`         | The step you asked for failed.                 |
| 7    | `partial`        | Some items worked, some did not.               |
| 8    | `conflict`       | A file you edited, or another run is active.   |
| 9    | `internal`       | A bug. `Application.bx` prints it and exits 9. |

The full list (1, 3, 5, 10 too) is in `src/bxrig/util/Exit.bx` and the [contract](/architecture/COMMAND-CONTRACT/index.html). Use the name, never the number: `out.precondition( ... )`, `xit.usage()`.

### The `--json` envelope

Every result has the same outer shape, built by `Cli.envelope`. Only `data` differs per command.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "command": "time zone",
  "version": "0.11.0-dev",
  "ok": false,
  "exit": 2,
  "dry_run": false,
  "data": { "commands": [ "sudo timedatectl set-timezone Europe/Madrid" ] },
  "warnings": []
}
```

`ok` is true only when `exit` is 0. A plan is exit 2 with the plan in `data`. A dry run is exit 0 with `dry_run` true.

## Advanced

* **MatchBox quirks** (no base classes, no postfix operators on indexes, case-insensitive string compare) are listed in [Code rules](/developer/code-rules/index.html).
* **Auto snapshot.** Before `refresh`, `reinstall`, `init` and system updates run with `--yes`, `Main.bx` takes a quiet config snapshot (`bxrig backup config auto off` turns it off).
* **Internal errors.** An uncaught exception reaches `onError` in `src/Application.bx`: it prints `bxrig: internal error: ...` and exits 9.
* **Logging.** `Cli.say` writes one line per result to MatchBox's `bxrig` log (`~/.matchbox/logs/bxrig.log`). Exit 0 is information, 2 and 10 debug, 1, 3 and 4 warning, anything else error.
* **Where files live.** State, journal and backups are under `~/.local/state/bxrig/`, config under `~/.config/bxrig/`, always asked from `Env`. See [config files](/reference/config-files/index.html).

# The desktop

BxRig sets up **Hyprland with Noctalia** as the main desktop. **KDE Plasma** stays installed and gets tiling and a status panel.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig session set hyprland      # or plasma: what the login screen starts
bxrig menu                      # the control center menu (Super+Alt+Space)
bxrig screenshot region         # Print
```

![The notification center: every notification, by day](/assets/screenshots/notification-center.webp)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Login screen"] --> B["Hyprland and Noctalia"]
  A --> C["KDE Plasma"]
  B --> D["bxrig.lua: shortcuts, generated"]
  B --> E["hyprland.lua: yours"]
  C --> F["Tiling and panels"]
```

## Pick your desktop

Choose either (or both) at the login screen, or run `bxrig session set hyprland|plasma`.

## Hyprland and Noctalia

`bxrig setup hyprland` installs the packages one by one and writes the starter configuration once. `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` is yours. BxRig owns `~/.config/hypr/bxrig.lua`, which it regenerates from the [shortcut table](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html); never edit that file by hand. See [Your own config](/customize/your-own-config/index.html).

### The bar's panels

The Noctalia bar carries three BxRig panels and the notifications. Each opens from its button on the bar or a key.

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ![The world clock: every time zone, how far it is from you, and day or night](/assets/screenshots/panel-world-clock.webp) **World clock** · the globe before the time, or <kbd>Super</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>W</kbd>. The zones are yours: `bxrig time world add Asia/Tokyo --yes` | ![The coding agents panel](/assets/screenshots/panel-agents.webp) **Coding agents** · <kbd>Super</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd>. The agents you have installed, their accounts and limits; launch one with a click. **Edit agents** (or `bxrig ai panel add\|remove ID --yes`) chooses which show |
| ![The theme switcher](/assets/screenshots/panel-theme-switcher.webp) **Theme switcher** · <kbd>Super</kbd>+<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd>. See [Themes](/customize/themes/index.html)                                                                             | ![Stacked notifications](/assets/screenshots/notifications.webp) **Notifications** stack in the top corner, rounded and in the theme's colors. <kbd>Super</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>,</kbd> acts on the newest, <kbd>Super</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>,</kbd> opens them all                        |

### Detach a panel into a window

Every bar panel (system, quick settings, themes, clock, power, VPN, developer, agents) has a **Detach** button in its header. It closes the popup and opens the same panel as a window a little bigger than the popup, centered on the screen. The window stays open when you click elsewhere, so you can keep it beside your work. **Dock** in the window's header closes it and brings the popup back.

Panels that have a terminal version also get a terminal button: the system panel opens the Control Center dashboard, the agents panel its Agents page, and the theme switcher its Themes page, each with `bxrig tui PAGE` in your terminal. A terminal is a normal window, so that one you can resize and tile.

The window is a second entry of the same plugin (`panel-window`, `themes-window`), so it also opens from a key or a script: `noctalia msg panel-toggle bxrig/clock:panel-window`. Noctalia fixes a panel's size in its manifest, so the window has one size and cannot be dragged to resize.

![The system panel as a window](/assets/screenshots/panel-window-system.webp)

![The agents panel as a window, with the terminal button](/assets/screenshots/panel-window-agents.webp)

![The theme switcher as a window](/assets/screenshots/panel-window-themes.webp)

## KDE Plasma

* **Tiling:** `bxrig setup plasma` installs HyprKwin and turns on the Bluetooth service (`bluetooth.service`, if it is not on yet). Layouts: dwindle, master, monocle, scrolling, stage. `bxrig tiling on|off|status|layout NAME`.
* **Panels:** `bxrig plasma panels apply` replaces your panels with a top status panel (launcher, workspace pager, active window, clock, weather, media, system vitals, tray, in rounded islands with Panel Colorizer) and a bottom dock. Your old layout is backed up first: `bxrig plasma panels undo --yes` restores it. From Hyprland it is applied at your next Plasma login.
* **Virtual desktops:** `bxrig plasma desktops 4`.
* **World clock:** the panel clock reads `Nov 15 - 22:16`; click it for every time zone you chose in the wizard (`bxrig time world`).

![The Plasma panel clock with its time zones](/assets/screenshots/plasma-world-clock.webp)

## Everyday tools

The shortcuts below are the Traditional style unless noted. Every key is a row of the [shortcut table](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html), in the style you chose.

|                    Do                     |                                                                   Command                                                                   |                                    Shortcut                                    |
|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| Screenshot                                | `bxrig screenshot screen\|region\|window`                                                                                                   | `Print` (region); Mac style also `Super+Shift+3` / `4` / `5` (the `5` menu)    |

| QR codes                                  | `bxrig screenshot qr`, `bxrig qr TEXT`                                                                                                      |                                                                                |
| Color picker                              | `bxrig screenshot color`                                                                                                                    | `Super+Print`                                                                  |

| Time, battery, weather                    | `bxrig notify time\|battery\|weather`                                                                                                       | `Super+Ctrl+Alt+T` / `B` / `W`                                                 |
| Night shift                               | `bxrig nightshift on\|off\|toggle`                                                                                                          | menu only                                                                      |
| Hide or show the bar, the dock            | `bxrig appearance bar toggle`, `appearance dock toggle`                                                                                     | `Super+Ctrl+Alt+F`, `Super+Alt+D`                                              |
| Emoji                                     | `bxrig emoji`                                                                                                                               | `Super+Ctrl+E`                                                                 |
| Force quit                                | `bxrig forcequit`                                                                                                                           | `Super+Alt+Escape`                                                             |
| Overview                                  | `bxrig overview`                                                                                                                            | `Super+Ctrl+Up`                                                                |
| Minimize / restore                        | `bxrig window minimize\|restore`                                                                                                            | `Super+H` / `Super+Shift+H`                                                    |
| Maximize                                  | (Hyprland binding)                                                                                                                          | `Super+M`                                                                      |
| Snap to a half                            | `bxrig window snap left\|right\|top\|bottom`                                                                                                | `Super+Alt+` arrows                                                            |
| Center a floating window                  | (Hyprland binding)                                                                                                                          | `Super+Alt+Shift+C`                                                            |
| Last workspace                            | (Hyprland binding)                                                                                                                          | `Super+Ctrl+Tab`                                                               |
| Window / workspace to another monitor     | (Hyprland binding)                                                                                                                          | `Super+Ctrl+Shift+` / `Super+Alt+Shift+` arrows                                |
| Next layout on this workspace             | (Hyprland binding)                                                                                                                          | `Super+Shift+J`                                                                |
| Narrower / wider column                   | (Hyprland binding)                                                                                                                          | `Super+Minus` / `Super+Equal`                                                  |
| Quake console                             | `bxrig window quake`, `window quake send`                                                                                                   | `Super+Shift+Grave` / `Super+Ctrl+Grave`                                       |
| Private browser window                    | `bxrig browser private [URL]`                                                                                                               | `Super+Alt+Shift+B` (Mac style `Super+Shift+N`)                                |
| File manager in this folder               | `bxrig files here [DIR]`                                                                                                                    | `Super+Alt+Shift+F`                                                            |
| Lock                                      | `bxrig system lock`                                                                                                                         | `Super+Ctrl+L`                                                                 |
| Pull-down AI shell                        | `bxrig ai shell`                                                                                                                            | ``Super+```                                                                    |

The quake console is the special workspace `qconsole`: the first press starts your default terminal on it. The private window uses the default browser (`bxrig default browser`). The webcam preview needs `mpv`, and recording with audio needs `pactl`.

Night shift on Hyprland runs `wlsunset` with your time zone's sunrise and sunset (no network lookup); on Plasma it turns on Plasma's own Night Light.

## Trackpads and Apple devices

`bxrig input gestures --yes` sets up three-finger swipes (workspaces, overview) with `libinput-gestures`. `bxrig input doctor` checks Magic Mouse and Magic Trackpad support (the kernel driver, loaded or built in, Bluetooth, the `input` group). `bxrig input status` finds Apple Magic and Logitech devices and `bxrig input offer` installs the helpers for them (Solaar for Logitech, libratbag and Piper for gaming mice, upower): see [Mice, trackpads and keyboards](/desktop/input/index.html). For Option-key characters like a Mac, pick the **English (US, Macintosh)** keyboard layout in the wizard. `bxrig airplay on` starts an AirPlay receiver.

## Hot corners

Rest the pointer in a screen corner to run an action. The defaults are Mac-like: top left the overview, top right the notifications, bottom left the desktop, bottom right the lock screen. Change any corner, on Hyprland (Noctalia) and Plasma (KWin screen edges) alike:

```bash
bxrig hotcorners                                      # what each corner does
bxrig hotcorners set top-left=launcher bottom-right=lock --yes
bxrig hotcorners off --yes
```

Actions: `none`, `overview`, `notifications`, `desktop`, `lock`, `launcher`, `agents`, `themes`. Plasma has no corner action for notifications, agents and themes; those corners do nothing there and the command says so.

## Screensaver

After 2.5 minutes idle, BXRIG art in your theme's colours fills every monitor; after 5 minutes the screen locks. Any key or mouse move closes it. Six effects take turns, a minute each: a gradient sweeping across BXRIG, the BxRig laptop with a glint, BoxLang code rain, a drifting clock, a starfield and your own logo.

```bash
bxrig screensaver preview              # try it in this terminal (preview clock for one effect)
bxrig screensaver                      # the settings and the effects
bxrig screensaver set screensaver=300 lock=600 --yes
bxrig screensaver set effects=clock,stars --yes
bxrig screensaver logo text ACME --yes # or: logo image ~/Pictures/logo.png, logo reset
bxrig screensaver off --yes            # no screensaver; the lock stays
```

On Hyprland, Noctalia runs it as an idle behavior. On Plasma, a small user service (swayidle) starts it and Plasma's own lock screen follows the `lock=` setting; `bxrig setup plasma` installs swayidle. On both, a video or **Stay awake** holds it off. It is also in the menu (*System \> Screensaver*) and on the Control Center's Look page.

## Boot splash

`bxrig setup boot --yes` puts the BxRig splash on the boot screen (Plymouth): the laptop fades in over a soft glow while the dots pulse, and an encrypted disk asks for its password on the same screen. It shows the plan first, keeps a backup of `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf`, and tells you where to add `splash` for your boot loader. `bxrig setup undo boot --yes` puts the previous theme back.

Look and hardware have their own pages: [Appearance](/customize/appearance/index.html) for the bar, dock, windows and fonts, and [Displays, power and time](/desktop/system/index.html) for monitors, laptop power and the time zone. The [menu](/desktop/menu/index.html) has all of it as one menu.

Next: [The menu](/desktop/menu/index.html), [Shortcuts](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html), [Appearance](/customize/appearance/index.html).

# Themes

Pick one of 24 color themes, each with its own wallpaper, and it follows you into the shell, terminals, btop, window borders and Neovim.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig theme list                  # all themes, the current one marked
bxrig theme set tokyo-night       # apply one now
bxrig theme next                  # or random
```

![The BxRig theme: its wallpaper, the bar and a themed terminal](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig.webp)

Setting a theme acts at once. `--dry-run` shows what would be written without changing anything.

## One theme, many places

A theme is one `colors.toml`. Setting it writes the files below.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["colors.toml"] --> B["Noctalia: bar, launcher, panels"]
  A --> C["Terminals and btop"]
  A --> D["Hyprland borders"]
  A --> E["GTK and Qt apps"]
  A --> F["Neovim, tmux, fzf"]
  A --> G["Wallpaper"]
```

## Light, dark or automatic

```bash
bxrig theme mode auto             # theme, dark, light or auto
bxrig theme status
```

## Pick from the switcher

On Hyprland the Themes row of the bar's quick settings popover (the sliders button), or <kbd>Super</kbd>+<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd>, opens the theme switcher: type to filter, see the theme's wallpaper, <kbd>Enter</kbd> applies it everywhere at once.

![The theme switcher, filtered to Kanagawa](/assets/screenshots/panel-theme-search.webp)

The Themes page of the Control Center (`bxrig tui themes`) is the selector: every theme with a color swatch, a filter (type to search, `d` for dark and `l` for light), a preview of the highlighted one (palette roles, a sample terminal and its wallpaper), `r` to preview it live (the whole Control Center is recoloured, nothing is applied; `r` again stops), and `Enter` for the plan and `y` to apply.

Setting a theme acts at once. `--dry-run` shows what would be written without changing anything.

## The 24 themes

BxRig ships 24 themes in the `colors.toml` format: fourteen of ours (six dark, five light, among them the neon 80s `bxrig-retro`, and three accessible ones: `bxrig-contrast-dark`, `bxrig-contrast-light` and `bxrig-colorblind`, see [Accessibility](/customize/accessibility/index.html)) and ten community themes.

Ours: BxRig, BxRig Cyan, BxRig Forest, BxRig Midnight and BxRig Ember (dark), BxRig Light, BxRig Dawn, BxRig Paper, BxRig Mint and BxRig Sky (light). Community themes: catppuccin, catppuccin-latte, tokyo-night, gruvbox, nord, rose-pine, kanagawa, everforest, matte-black and flexoki-light (MIT, credited in `themes/NOTICE.md`). Each one below is shown with its wallpaper and `btop` in a themed terminal.

|                                                                                                        |                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ![BxRig](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig.webp) **BxRig** · `bxrig` · dark                             | ![BxRig Cyan](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-cyan.webp) **BxRig Cyan** · `bxrig-cyan` · dark                          |
| ![BxRig Forest](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-forest.webp) **BxRig Forest** · `bxrig-forest` · dark | ![BxRig Midnight](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-midnight.webp) **BxRig Midnight** · `bxrig-midnight` · dark          |
| ![BxRig Ember](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-ember.webp) **BxRig Ember** · `bxrig-ember` · dark     | ![BxRig Light](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-light.webp) **BxRig Light** · `bxrig-light` · light                     |
| ![BxRig Dawn](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-dawn.webp) **BxRig Dawn** · `bxrig-dawn` · light        | ![BxRig Paper](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-paper.webp) **BxRig Paper** · `bxrig-paper` · light                     |
| ![BxRig Mint](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-mint.webp) **BxRig Mint** · `bxrig-mint` · light        | ![BxRig Sky](/assets/screenshots/themes/bxrig-sky.webp) **BxRig Sky** · `bxrig-sky` · light                             |
| ![Catppuccin](/assets/screenshots/themes/catppuccin.webp) **Catppuccin** · `catppuccin` · dark         | ![Catppuccin Latte](/assets/screenshots/themes/catppuccin-latte.webp) **Catppuccin Latte** · `catppuccin-latte` · light |
| ![Tokyo Night](/assets/screenshots/themes/tokyo-night.webp) **Tokyo Night** · `tokyo-night` · dark     | ![Gruvbox](/assets/screenshots/themes/gruvbox.webp) **Gruvbox** · `gruvbox` · dark                                      |
| ![Nord](/assets/screenshots/themes/nord.webp) **Nord** · `nord` · dark                                 | ![Rosé Pine](/assets/screenshots/themes/rose-pine.webp) **Rosé Pine** · `rose-pine` · light                             |
| ![Kanagawa](/assets/screenshots/themes/kanagawa.webp) **Kanagawa** · `kanagawa` · dark                 | ![Everforest](/assets/screenshots/themes/everforest.webp) **Everforest** · `everforest` · dark                          |
| ![Matte Black](/assets/screenshots/themes/matte-black.webp) **Matte Black** · `matte-black` · dark     | ![Flexoki Light](/assets/screenshots/themes/flexoki-light.webp) **Flexoki Light** · `flexoki-light` · light             |

## Your own themes

`bxrig theme install https://github.com/someone/name-theme` installs a theme repository in the same format (https only). Theme folders you already have from other setups are found automatically. A theme is a folder with `colors.toml`, an optional `neovim.lua` and an optional `backgrounds/` folder:

```bash
bxrig theme import ~/my-theme --name=mine
bxrig theme remove mine
```

Every bundled theme, BxRig's own included, uses the standard `colors.toml`: `mode`, `accent`, `selection`, `muted`, the background shades (`background`, `dark_background`, `darker_background`, `lighter_background`), the foreground shades (`foreground`, `dark_foreground`, `light_foreground`, `bright_foreground`) and the named colours (`red` to `brown`, then `bright_red` to `bright_magenta`). The terminal palette comes from them: black is `background`, white is `foreground`, bright black is `muted`, bright white is `bright_foreground`, and the cursor is `bright_foreground`. The older `color0` to `color15` list is still read, for themes you install from elsewhere.

## Neovim and the prompt

`bxrig editor lazyvim --yes` installs the LazyVim starter plus the BxRig layer: transparent background, BoxLang syntax highlighting ([vim-boxlang](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/vim-boxlang)), no news popups, the neo-tree extra, and live theme following. An existing `~/.config/nvim` is never touched. To add only BoxLang syntax to a LazyVim config you already have: `bxrig editor boxlang --yes`.

The starter Starship prompt shows your BoxLang version, like Java, in folders with `.bx`, `.bxs`, `.bxm`, `.cfc`, `.cfm` or `.cfs` files, `box.json` or `Application.bx`. The starter file is written once, so an existing prompt keeps what you have; `bxrig config diff starship` shows what is new.

## Advanced

### What changes, by app

|                      Where                      |                                                                                                                                                                           How                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Noctalia (bar, launcher, panels, notifications) | a generated palette and the light or dark mode                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Ghostty, kitty, alacritty, foot                 | generated files that the starter configs include                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| btop                                            | a generated theme file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Hyprland window borders                         | the accent color, read by the managed `bxrig.lua`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Neovim (LazyVim setup)                          | the matching colorscheme, applied live without a restart                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| KDE Plasma                                      | switches between Breeze Light and Breeze Dark                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| GTK 3 and 4 apps                                | `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` and `gtk-3.0/gtk.css` (libadwaita colors; adw-gtk3 for GTK 3), plus the dark or light preference through gsettings                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Qt apps                                         | qt6ct and qt5ct color schemes (set the style to qt6ct in your environment)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| tmux, fzf                                       | `theme/tmux.conf` and `theme/fzf.sh`, with a one-line hint to source them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| rofi, fuzzel, wofi                              | a rofi theme (and a `config.rasi` stub when you have none), `fuzzel.ini`, wofi `style.css`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Wallpaper                                       | a theme brings its own wallpaper (3840x2400, drawn by code so it is sharp on a high-density screen); use `--keep-wallpaper` to skip it. BxRig also ships a collection of extra wallpapers in `~/Pictures/BxRig` (`bxrig-tron`, `bxrig-neon`, `bxrig-city`, `bxrig-aurora`, `bxrig-orbit`, `bxrig-circuit`, `bxrig-rain`, `bxrig-waves`) to pick by hand |

A theme can name a font with a `font = "ID"` line in its `colors.toml` (an id of `bxrig appearance font list`; other tools ignore the line). `bxrig-retro` names `sharetech`, Share Tech Mono Nerd (Arch package `ttf-sharetech-mono-nerd`): once it is installed (`bxrig appearance font install sharetech --yes`) `theme set` makes it the shell and terminal font, and until then the plan says so. Other themes leave your font alone.

`bxrig banner` prints the BXRIG wordmark in the colors of the current theme (`--json` gives the lines); the retro theme uses it as a terminal greeting.

VS Code is opt-in: `bxrig theme vscode` shows a plan, `--yes` merges the colors into `workbench.colorCustomizations` of Code, Code - OSS, VSCodium or Cursor (a backup is kept; a settings file with comments is left alone). Not themed: the Starship prompt, browsers and icons. Your own config files are never edited. Terminal configs you wrote yourself need one include line, which `bxrig theme set` prints.

Bar, dock, windows, fonts and backgrounds are in [Appearance](/customize/appearance/index.html).

Next: [Appearance](/customize/appearance/index.html), [Accessibility](/customize/accessibility/index.html), [Your own config](/customize/your-own-config/index.html).

# Updates and channels

Use this page to update BxRig, get told when something is waiting, and update the system safely.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig update check              # exit 10 means an update is available
bxrig update apply --yes        # download, verify, replace atomically
bxrig system update --yes       # snapshot first, then the system packages
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Channel: stable or beta"] --> B["Signed version info"]
  B --> C["bxrig update check"]
  C -->|"exit 10"| D["bxrig update apply"]
  D --> E["Verify signature and SHA-256"]
  E --> F["Replace the program atomically"]
  G["bxrig system update"] --> H["Snapshot"] --> I["pacman and AUR update"]
```

The diagram shows both flows: BxRig updates itself from its channel after verifying, and the system update takes a snapshot first.

## Pick a channel

| Channel  |                        What it is                         |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `stable` | Tagged releases                                           |
| `beta`   | The bleeding edge: a build of every push to `development` |

```bash
bxrig update channel            # show
bxrig update channel beta       # switch
```

Both are also in the control center (Settings, Updates).

## Update BxRig

```bash
bxrig update check              # exit 10 means an update is available
bxrig update apply --yes        # download, verify, replace atomically
```

The release information is signed (Ed25519) and the binary's SHA-256 is checked against it; a bad signature or checksum changes nothing.

`bxrig update` replaces only the `bxrig` program. MatchBox (the toolchain) is not touched; move it with `mvm update`, or run the installer again with `--snapshot` or `--matchbox-branch REF` (see [getting started](/start/install/index.html#which-matchbox)).

## Get told about updates

```bash
bxrig update notifications on     # a daily user timer shows a desktop notification
bxrig update notifications off
```

The notification covers BxRig and pending system packages.

## See what is waiting

```bash
bxrig system updates            # counts, the package list and whether a restart is needed
bxrig system updates --json     # the same as data for scripts and the System panel in the bar
```

It reads only: repository packages from `checkupdates` (the `pacman-contrib` package) and AUR packages from `yay -Qua` or `paru -Qua`. It exits 0 even when updates are waiting, and 4 when `checkupdates` is missing or cannot reach the mirrors.

## Update the system

```bash
bxrig system update             # the plan: the snapshot step, then the update steps (exit 2)
bxrig system update --yes       # snapshot first (snapper or timeshift), then pacman -Syu and yay -Sua
bxrig system update --repo --yes   # the snapshot and the repository packages only
bxrig system update --aur --yes    # the snapshot and the AUR packages only (yay, else paru; exit 4 without one)
```

`--all` is the default. Every scope takes the snapshot first, and says so when snapper and timeshift are both missing. In a terminal each step is named as it starts, and a restart is mentioned at the end when the kernel was replaced.

`bxrig skills update --yes` refreshes the agent skills BxRig installed.

## Advanced

### When a restart is needed

`system updates` sets `needs_reboot` to true for either of two cases:

* **Pending.** An update in the list replaces a kernel (`linux`, `linux-lts`, `linux-zen`, `linux-cachyos` and the other flavours, not their `-headers` or `-docs`), `systemd`, `glibc`, `linux-firmware`, a CPU microcode package (`intel-ucode`, `amd-ucode`) or the NVIDIA driver. `reboot_pending` is true.
* **Stale.** The kernel that runs is gone from `/usr/lib/modules`, which means an update already replaced it. `reboot_stale` is true.

`reboot_reasons` says why in words. The last full system upgrade comes from `/var/log/pacman.log`.

### Unsigned test builds

An install made with `install.sh --source github:...` (an unsigned test build, see [getting started](/start/install/index.html)) is not tracked: `update check` reports an update because the program differs from the channel's, and `update apply --yes` replaces it with that channel's build.

Next: [Security](/maintain/security/index.html) · [Backups](/data/backups/index.html) · [Scheduler](/data/scheduler/index.html)

title: Appearance
body: Appearance Change how the shell and the windows look, one setting at a time. Each change acts at once, is remembered, and can be shown first with --dry-run . For colors, see Themes . Try it bxrig appearance bar layout minimal # minimal, standard (the default), dense, status bxrig appearance dock off # on, off, toggle bxrig appearance font cascadia # the coding font bxrig appearance background random # or: list, set NAME, next bxrig appearance status shows what you have chosen, and bxrig appearance apply pushes it all again. The menu has all of this under Appearance. Pick a bar bxrig appearance bar layout picks one of three bars. Standard is the default. They all end with quick settings and then the control center, and they use bare icons coloured by the theme: only the logo button and the Launchpad grid carry a plate (a tile with an outline, so it stays visible on dark and Retro bars).
