# The menu

`bxrig menu` is one menu for everything BxRig does, shown on your launcher. Press `Super+Alt+Space`, type to search, press Enter. On the Noctalia desktop it opens as a panel with icons and a breadcrumb (see [Launcher](/desktop/launcher/index.html#the-menu)); elsewhere it opens in your menu program. To search everything in one list (apps, menu actions, themes, a calculator and the clipboard) use the launcher on `Super+Space`.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig menu                    # open it (Super+Alt+Space)
bxrig menu search theme       # find an entry by words
bxrig menu open capture       # one submenu on its own
```

> **Screenshot wanted:** the BxRig menu open on the launcher (Super+Alt+Space), showing the section list.

It opens on Rofi, Walker, Wofi, Fuzzel or Vicinae: pick one with `bxrig runner set NAME` (see the [launcher](/desktop/launcher/index.html)).

## Every entry is a command

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Super+Alt+Space"] --> B["Menu on your launcher"]
  B --> C["Section"]
  C --> D["Entry"]
  D --> E["A bxrig command"]
  E --> F["Plan first, then done"]
```

`bxrig menu items` lists the entries with the command each one runs, and `bxrig menu search TEXT` finds one. Entries that print something open in a terminal and wait for Enter; entries that need a choice (a theme, a font, a time zone, a monitor) ask you in the same menu.

## Jump to one submenu

`bxrig menu open capture` opens one submenu on its own. `bxrig menu open` lists the routes; System, Capture, Toggle, Hardware and Agent have keys (`Super+Escape`, `Super+Ctrl+C`, `Super+Ctrl+O`, `Super+Ctrl+H`, `Super+Shift+Ctrl+A`).

## What the menu shows

* **A tick on the current value.** The bar position and style, the dock, the window look, the theme mode, the layout and the power profile show a ✓ on what is set now.
* **Only what applies here.** Laptop entries (laptop panel, lid, power tools) show on a laptop; the touchpad and touchscreen switches when you have one (Hyprland); webcam entries when there is a webcam; GPU mode on a laptop with two GPUs. Install lists only the apps you do not have yet.

## Add your own entries

`~/.config/bxrig/menu.json` adds entries, hides entries and renames them. `bxrig menu file --yes` writes an example; `bxrig menu ids` lists the id of every entry. This file is yours: see [Your own config](/customize/your-own-config/index.html).

```json
{
	"add": [
		{ "under": "trigger", "label": "Open my notes", "command": [ "xdg-open", "~/Notes" ] },
		{ "under": "system", "label": "Disk usage", "command": [ "ncdu", "~" ], "terminal": true },
		{ "under": "appearance", "label": "Next theme", "bxrig": [ "theme", "next" ] }
	],
	"hide": [ "trigger.share-localsend" ],
	"rename": { "system.lock": "Lock now" }
}
```

`command` runs a program (in a terminal with `"terminal": true`), `bxrig` runs a BxRig command. Leave out `under` to add at the top. A mistake in the file is shown as a warning by `bxrig menu file` and `bxrig menu items`; the menu still opens.

## Advanced

The sections of the menu:

|       Section        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        What is in it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Search               | Every entry of the menu as one flat list; type to filter, press Enter to run it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Apps                 | Your installed apps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Install              | Any package from the repositories or the AUR, the catalog by group (AI, Development, Terminal, Gaming), web apps, virtual machines, fonts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Remove               | Packages, catalog apps, web apps, themes, virtual machines, agent skills. It asks first.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

| Shortcuts            | List, search, rebind and run a shortcut, check conflicts, write them to Hyprland and Plasma, pick the Traditional or Mac style. See [Shortcuts](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Hardware             | Monitors, laptop panel, mirror, brightness, webcam preview, GPU check, GPU mode (hybrid laptops), touchpad and touchscreen on or off, a Wi-Fi QR code, Network and speed (the System panel's Network tab on Hyprland, the Control Center Network page elsewhere), network and disk speed tests, input devices and gestures, Audio, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi (they open the Noctalia control center panel, like `Super+Alt+C`), the terminal fallbacks `Audio mixer (terminal)` (wiremix) and `Bluetooth devices (terminal)` (bluetui), the status checks for audio, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, AirPlay. |
| Setup                | Power, Display, Defaults (browser, terminal, file manager, editor), Keyboard, Security, Time, DNS (with "Test and pick the fastest", `dns bench`), Kernel, Cloud storage, Backup, NAS.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Update               | BxRig updates, the system update (a snapshot first), firmware updates, restarting the shell, audio, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth when one is stuck, changing your password, skills, re-apply appearance and display.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Develop              | BoxLang, databases, virtual machines, containers, the editor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Agent                | Open an agent, the pull-down AI shell, sessions, local models, API keys.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Learn, About, System | Docs and cheat sheets, the status of this machine, lock, suspend, log out, reboot, shut down.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Next: [Shortcuts](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html), [Control Center](/desktop/control-center/index.html), [Appearance](/customize/appearance/index.html).

markdown:
# Accessibility

Zoom, reduce motion and three high-contrast themes, all off until you turn them on.

## Try it

Turn them on from the Control Center (`bxrig tui accessibility`), the menu (Appearance \> Accessibility), the Quick panel (Zoom) or the command line.

```bash
bxrig accessibility                       # what is on
bxrig accessibility zoom on               # the zoom keys start working
bxrig accessibility reduce-motion on      # no window, bar or app animations
bxrig accessibility contrast dark         # dark, light, colorblind, or off to go back to your theme
```

They are settings: they act at once, and `--dry-run` shows the commands first.

The three settings and what they switch:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["bxrig accessibility"] --> B["Zoom keys"]
  A --> C["Reduce motion"]
  A --> D["Contrast theme"]
```

![The accessibility commands and the zoom keys](/assets/screenshots/accessibility-cli.webp)

## Zoom

The same keys as on a Mac (Option is `Alt`, Cmd is `Super`):

|       Keys        |                  What it does                   |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `Super+Alt+8`     | Zoom on or off (back to the last zoom you used) |
| `Super+Alt+Equal` | Zoom in, half a step each time (up to 10x)      |
| `Super+Alt+Minus` | Zoom out                                        |

While zoom is off the keys only say how to turn it on, so they never surprise you. On Hyprland the screen zooms around the pointer (`cursor:zoom_factor`). On Plasma BxRig loads KWin's Zoom effect and uses its shortcuts; Plasma's own keys, `Meta+=` and `Meta+-`, work too.

## Reduce motion

Turns off the animations of windows and workspaces (Hyprland), of the bar and panels (Noctalia), of GTK apps (`enable-animations`) and of Plasma (its animation speed). `bxrig accessibility reduce-motion off` brings them back.

## Contrast themes

|         Theme          |                                    Look                                    |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `bxrig-contrast-dark`  | white on black, a yellow accent                                            |
| `bxrig-contrast-light` | black on white, a blue accent                                              |
| `bxrig-colorblind`     | blue and orange instead of red and green (Okabe-Ito hues), on a dark slate |

![BxRig Contrast Dark in the Themes page](/assets/screenshots/theme-contrast-dark.webp)

![BxRig Colorblind in the Themes page](/assets/screenshots/theme-colorblind.webp)

Every text colour in them is at least 7:1 against the background (WCAG AAA); a test checks it. Their wallpapers are plain, and Neovim gets the matching high-contrast or colour-blind GitHub colorscheme. `bxrig accessibility contrast off` goes back to the theme you had before. They are ordinary themes too: `bxrig theme set bxrig-colorblind` works.

Next: [Themes](/customize/themes/index.html), [Shortcuts](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html), [Boxy's look and voice](/customize/boxy-look/index.html).

# Add a command

You will add `bxrig dnsflush`, a made-up command that empties the system DNS cache. It changes the machine, so it shows a plan first and needs `--yes`. That makes it a good tour of every part.

The model is `bxrig gpu mode` (`src/bxrig/GpuMode.bx`, and the `gpu` case in `src/Main.bx`): a small class that calls `Mutation` for its plan.
> **Note:** `dnsflush` is an example. Do not commit it, or pick your own name and tool.

## What you will touch

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["1 cli.json entry"] --> B["2 case in Main.bx"]
  B --> C["3 class in src/bxrig"]
  C --> D["4 gen-docs.sh"]
  D --> E["5 test and CI list"]
```

## 1. Describe it in the registry

Open `docs/reference/cli.json` and add an entry to a group (here `tools`). The registry feeds `bxrig help`, flag checking and the docs.

```json
{
 "name": "dnsflush",
 "summary": "Empty the system DNS cache.",
 "usage": [
  "dnsflush [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]"
 ],
 "examples": [
  "bxrig dnsflush",
  "bxrig dnsflush --yes"
 ],
 "mutates": true,
 "flags": []
}
```

Rules `gen-docs.sh` enforces: the summary ends with a full stop, every usage line starts with the command name, every example starts with `bxrig` and names a real command, and every `--flag` you mention is either global (`--json`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--quiet`) or listed in `flags`. `"mutates": true` adds the "needs `--yes`" note to the docs and to `bxrig help`.

## 2. Route it in `Main.bx`

Add one `case` before `default:`. Wrong usage prints the registry's usage text and exits 2. Doctor's `case` (`src/Main.bx`) is the model.

```boxlang
case "dnsflush":
	// Empties the DNS cache. See bxrig.DnsFlush.
	if ( p.len() != 1 ) {
		println( new bxrig.CommandSpec().usage( cmd ) );
		CLIExit( xit.usage() );
	}
	CLIExit( new bxrig.DnsFlush( cli ).run( structKeyExists( args.options, "yes" ), structKeyExists( args.options, "dry-run" ), asJson ) );
	break;
```

Use `xit.usage()`, never a bare `2`. `Main.bx` has already checked the flags against the registry, so an unknown `--flag` never reaches your class.

## 3. Write the class

Create `src/bxrig/DnsFlush.bx`. Every function and the class carry a DocBox comment (see [Code rules](/developer/code-rules/index.html)).

```boxlang
/**
 * `bxrig dnsflush [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]`: empties the system DNS cache with systemd-resolved.
 *
 * Works with bxrig.util.Mutation (plan, dry run, run) and bxrig.util.Proc (starts the program).
 * Exit: 0 done or dry run, 2 a plan without --yes, 4 resolvectl is missing, 6 the flush failed.
 */
class DnsFlush {

	/**
	 * Builds the command.
	 *
	 * @param cli The shared output helper made in Main.bx (bxrig.util.Cli).
	 * @param runner A fake program runner for tests; "" runs real programs.
	 *
	 * @return This object.
	 */
	function init( cli, runner = "" ) {
		variables.cli = arguments.cli;
		variables.proc = new bxrig.util.Proc( arguments.runner );
		return this;
	}

	/**
	 * Shows the plan, or flushes the DNS cache when --yes is given.
	 *
	 * @param yes True when --yes was passed.
	 * @param dry True when --dry-run was passed.
	 * @param asJson True when --json was passed.
	 *
	 * @return The exit code: 0, 2 (plan), 4 (no resolvectl) or 6 (failed).
	 */
	function run( yes, dry, asJson ) {
		var out = variables.cli.scoped( "dnsflush" );
		// Check the tool first: a missing tool must be exit 4, before any plan is printed.
		if ( !variables.proc.has( "resolvectl" ) ) return out.precondition( "resolvectl was not found (systemd-resolved)", arguments.asJson );
		return new bxrig.util.Mutation( out, variables.proc ).run( "flush the DNS cache", [ [ "resolvectl", "flush-caches" ] ], arguments.yes, arguments.dry, arguments.asJson, {}, [], 30 );
	}
}
```

What the helpers give you for free:

|                               You write                               |                                                                              You get                                                                              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `cli.scoped( "dnsflush" )`                                            | An `Out` bound to the command name for the `--json` envelope.                                                                                                     |
| `out.precondition( msg, asJson )`                                     | `error: msg` (or `{ "error": ... }`) and exit 4. Also `out.usage` (2) and `out.failed` (6).                                                                       |
| `Mutation.run( title, cmds, yes, dry, asJson, data, shown, timeout )` | "Plan: ..." and exit 2 without `--yes`; "Dry run: ..." and exit 0 with `--dry-run`; otherwise runs each argv in order and stops at the first failure with exit 6. |
| `proc.has( "tool" )`                                                  | A `command -v` check. Programs run only through `Proc`, with an argv array.                                                                                       |

If your command writes a file, do not write it yourself: build an entry and pass it to `ConfigService` for the backup, atomic replace and journal.

## 4. Regenerate the docs

```bash
bash bootstrap/gen-docs.sh
```

This rewrites `docs/reference/commands.md`, `docs/reference/command-flags.md` and `src/bxrig/CommandFlagData.bx`. It fails when `Main.bx` and `cli.json` disagree (a `case` with no entry, or an entry with no `case`). Commit both the source and the generated files; CI runs it with `--check`.

## 5. Test it

Create `tests/dnsflush-test.sh`. It runs the real binary against a fake `resolvectl`, so no root and no network is needed. More in [Tests](/developer/tests/index.html).

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# `bxrig dnsflush` with a fake resolvectl. Usage: dnsflush-test.sh BINARY
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/harness.sh"
export LOG="$tmp/log"; : > "$LOG"
stub resolvectl 'echo "resolvectl $*" >> "$LOG"'
run() { env HOME="$tmp/home" PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" LOG="$LOG" "$@"; }

[[ "$(code "$binary" dnsflush)" == 2 ]] || fail 'without --yes it is a plan (exit 2)'
[[ ! -s "$LOG" ]] || fail 'the plan ran something'
run "$binary" dnsflush --dry-run --json | jq -e '.dry_run and .data.commands[0] == "resolvectl flush-caches"' >/dev/null || fail 'dry run'
run "$binary" dnsflush --yes >/dev/null
grep -qF 'resolvectl flush-caches' "$LOG" || fail '--yes did not run the flush'
[[ "$(code "$binary" dnsflush extra)" == 2 ]] || fail 'extra words are a usage error'
[[ "$(code "$binary" dnsflush --bogus)" == 2 ]] || fail 'an unknown flag is a usage error'
echo "dnsflush-test: ok"
```

Then make CI know about it, or `tests/dry-test.sh` fails:

1. Add `bash tests/dnsflush-test.sh "$candidate"` next to the other test lines in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
2. Add `tests/dnsflush-test.sh` to the `bash -n` list in the same file.

## 6. Run it all

```bash
scripts/dev-build.sh
bash tests/dnsflush-test.sh dist/bxrig
dist/bxrig dnsflush              # the plan, exit 2
dist/bxrig dnsflush --dry-run
bash scripts/format.sh
bash tests/dry-test.sh
```

## Checklist

* Entry in `docs/reference/cli.json`, then `bootstrap/gen-docs.sh`
* `case` in `src/Main.bx` with `xit.usage()` on bad usage
* Class in `src/bxrig/` with DocBox on the class and every function
* Plan, `--dry-run` and `--yes` through `Mutation` (or `ConfigService` for files)
* Output through `Out`, so `--json` works
* A shell test, listed twice in `ci.yml`
* `bash scripts/format.sh` and `bash tests/dry-test.sh` pass

## Advanced

* **Commands with sub-verbs** (`time zone`, `gpu mode`) collect the words after the command into an array and pass them to a `run( words, ... )` method that dispatches on the first word; see `Time.run` in `src/bxrig/Time.bx`.
* **A command that only changes your own settings** (a theme, the bar) may act at once without `--yes`, but must take `--dry-run` and be documented as an exception in the [contract](/architecture/COMMAND-CONTRACT/index.html) (section 2, rule 11).
* **Commands that pass flags to another program** (`secrets run`, `scheduler add ... --`, `ai agents NAME VERB`) are exempt from the flag check in `Main.bx`.
* **Unit tests.** Logic that needs no binary can be tested from source with a `tests/NAME_test.bxs` that uses `lib.Check`; see `tests/out_test.bxs`.

title: BoxLang agents
body: BoxLang agents bx-agents builds AI agents in BoxLang: an Agent.yml , instructions, tools, skills, routines, a web chat and a terminal chat. It has its own full command line, bxAgents . BxRig installs it, keeps your agent projects in one folder, runs each agent in the background, and points them at your local model when you want. Try it bxrig ai agents install --yes # bx-agents, once bxrig ai agents setup --yes # makes ~/Agents/Boxy, starts it, makes it your default agent bxrig ai agents ask how is my battery flowchart LR U["You"] --> B["Boxy agent"] B --> M["Local model or provider"] B --> T["BxRig tools"] T --> A{"Changes something?"} A -->|"yes"| Q["You approve or reject"] A -->|"no"| R["Runs and answers"] Q --> R The diagram shows how a request to Boxy turns into a BxRig command, with your approval before any change. Talk to Boxy Boxy is BxRig's own agent: it knows this machine. Ask it how the battery is doing, what is on your agenda, to switch to a dark theme, add a reminder, install an app, start a database or take a screenshot. The setup wizard offers both steps above on its AI page. Then: Keys or command What Super+Period a chat with your default agent (Boxy) in a terminal Super+Shift+Period its web page bxrig ai agents chat the chat in this terminal bxrig ai agents ask how is my battery one question, the answer printed Approve what it changes Every tool that changes something waits for your OK: Approve, Reject, or approve for the rest of the conversation, in the chat, on the web page or in the bar. From a terminal: bxrig ai agents ask switch to the dawn theme # Boxy wants to run theme_set {"theme":"dawn"} bxrig ai agents approve bxrig-1f2e3d4c5b6a # or: reject Its tools run BxRig's own commands, so it can do only what BxRig does, through the same plans and checks. Other agents and editors can use the same tools: bxrig mcp link --yes (see MCP and privacy ). Make your own agent bxrig ai agents new Boxy # bx-agents' own wizard, in ~/Agents/Boxy bxrig ai agents new Boxy --model=openai-compatible/qwen3.5-0.8b --no-wizard bxrig ai agents # your agents: running or not, the address, the default one new runs bxAgents new in your projects folder, so every question and flag is bx-agents' own. You can make one anywhere else with bxAgents new and tell BxRig about it: bxrig ai agents add ~/work/shop-support . Boxy is your project in ~/Agents/Boxy : change its instructions ( instructions.md ), its tools ( tools/BxRig.bx ) or its model ( Agent.bx ), and bxrig ai agents start Boxy rebuilds it. Run agents in the background bxrig ai agents start Boxy # builds it, then serves it on 127.0.0.1 bxrig ai agents open Boxy # its web page bxrig ai agents status Boxy bxrig ai agents stop Boxy bxrig ai agents default Boxy # the agent your keyboard shortcut opens Each agent runs as a user service ( bxrig-agent-boxy.service ) on its own port, from 8790 up, and only on this machine. Routines and gateways run while it does. Its log: journalctl --user -u bxrig-agent-boxy.service . The BoxLang agents page ( bxrig tui ai-boxlang ) lists your agents: Enter opens the chat in a new terminal, o the web page, s starts or stops it, d makes it the default, l shows its log and i installs or updates bx-agents. The bar's Agents panel has a Boxy tab, for your default agent: Start or Stop, Chat, its web page, a box to ask it something with Approve and Reject when it wants to change something, and its new skills to review. The BoxLang tab lists every agent with Chat, its web page and Start or Stop. Review the skills it saves After a task that took real steps, Boxy (or any agent) can save a skill, its own notes on how to do it again. bx-agents asks you to approve each save in the chat. BxRig flags the ones you have not reviewed since, and the bar shows how many: bxrig ai agents skills # Boxy's own skills: new or reviewed bxrig ai agents skills show morning-check # read one bxrig ai agents skills approve morning-check # mark it reviewed (--all for every one) bxrig ai agents skills remove morning-check --yes A skill stays active while it waits for your review. When the agent saves over one you reviewed, it is flagged again. Another agent: bxrig ai agents skills NAME ... . # BoxLang agents

[bx-agents](https://bxagents.ai) builds AI agents in BoxLang: an `Agent.yml`, instructions, tools, skills, routines, a web chat and a terminal chat. It has its own full command line, `bxAgents`. BxRig installs it, keeps your agent projects in one folder, runs each agent in the background, and points them at your [local model](/ai/local-ai/index.html) when you want.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig ai agents install --yes      # bx-agents, once
bxrig ai agents setup --yes        # makes ~/Agents/Boxy, starts it, makes it your default agent
bxrig ai agents ask how is my battery
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U["You"] --> B["Boxy agent"]
  B --> M["Local model or provider"]
  B --> T["BxRig tools"]
  T --> A{"Changes something?"}
  A -->|"yes"| Q["You approve or reject"]
  A -->|"no"| R["Runs and answers"]
  Q --> R
```

The diagram shows how a request to Boxy turns into a BxRig command, with your approval before any change.

## Talk to Boxy

Boxy is BxRig's own agent: it knows this machine. Ask it how the battery is doing, what is on your agenda, to switch to a dark theme, add a reminder, install an app, start a database or take a screenshot. The setup wizard offers both steps above on its AI page. Then:

|             Keys or command             |                        What                         |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `Super+Period`                          | a chat with your default agent (Boxy) in a terminal |
| `Super+Shift+Period`                    | its web page                                        |
| `bxrig ai agents chat`                  | the chat in this terminal                           |
| `bxrig ai agents ask how is my battery` | one question, the answer printed                    |

![The BoxLang agents page of the Control Center](/assets/screenshots/ai-boxlang-page.webp)

## Approve what it changes

Every tool that changes something waits for your OK: Approve, Reject, or approve for the rest of the conversation, in the chat, on the web page or in the bar. From a terminal:

```bash
bxrig ai agents ask switch to the dawn theme
# Boxy wants to run theme_set {"theme":"dawn"}
bxrig ai agents approve bxrig-1f2e3d4c5b6a      # or: reject
```

Its tools run BxRig's own commands, so it can do only what BxRig does, through the same plans and checks. Other agents and editors can use the same tools: `bxrig mcp link --yes` (see [MCP and privacy](/ai/mcp-and-privacy/index.html)).

## Make your own agent

```bash
bxrig ai agents new Boxy                    # bx-agents' own wizard, in ~/Agents/Boxy
bxrig ai agents new Boxy --model=openai-compatible/qwen3.5-0.8b --no-wizard
bxrig ai agents                             # your agents: running or not, the address, the default one
```

`new` runs `bxAgents new` in your projects folder, so every question and flag is bx-agents' own. You can make one anywhere else with `bxAgents new` and tell BxRig about it: `bxrig ai agents add ~/work/shop-support`.

Boxy is your project in `~/Agents/Boxy`: change its instructions (`instructions.md`), its tools (`tools/BxRig.bx`) or its model (`Agent.bx`), and `bxrig ai agents start Boxy` rebuilds it.

## Run agents in the background

```bash
bxrig ai agents start Boxy      # builds it, then serves it on 127.0.0.1
bxrig ai agents open Boxy       # its web page
bxrig ai agents status Boxy
bxrig ai agents stop Boxy
bxrig ai agents default Boxy    # the agent your keyboard shortcut opens
```

Each agent runs as a user service (`bxrig-agent-boxy.service`) on its own port, from 8790 up, and only on this machine. Routines and gateways run while it does. Its log: `journalctl --user -u bxrig-agent-boxy.service`.

The **BoxLang agents** page (`bxrig tui ai-boxlang`) lists your agents: `Enter` opens the chat in a new terminal, `o` the web page, `s` starts or stops it, `d` makes it the default, `l` shows its log and `i` installs or updates bx-agents.

The bar's Agents panel has a **Boxy** tab, for your default agent: Start or Stop, Chat, its web page, a box to ask it something with Approve and Reject when it wants to change something, and its new skills to review. The **BoxLang** tab lists every agent with Chat, its web page and Start or Stop.

## Review the skills it saves

After a task that took real steps, Boxy (or any agent) can save a skill, its own notes on how to do it again. bx-agents asks you to approve each save in the chat. BxRig flags the ones you have not reviewed since, and the bar shows how many:

```bash
bxrig ai agents skills                       # Boxy's own skills: new or reviewed
bxrig ai agents skills show morning-check    # read one
bxrig ai agents skills approve morning-check # mark it reviewed (--all for every one)
bxrig ai agents skills remove morning-check --yes
```

A skill stays active while it waits for your review. When the agent saves over one you reviewed, it is flagged again. Another agent: `bxrig ai agents skills NAME ...`.

## Advanced

### What Boxy can do

|     Area     |                                                          Tools                                                          |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| This machine | status, updates waiting, battery and power profile, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound, displays, backups                          |
| The look     | the themes and switching them, light or dark, night light, do not disturb, staying awake, brightness, the power profile |
| Plans        | the agenda from your calendars, reminders, the time zone                                                                |
| Apps         | searching the catalog, installing and removing apps, finding a shortcut                                                 |
| Capture      | a screenshot, a screen recording                                                                                        |
| Development  | your databases and virtual machines (start and stop them), the local AI models                                          |
| System       | updating the system (a snapshot first), locking the screen, backing up your files now                                   |

### A model that fits

Boxy has 36 tools. A very small model (Qwen3.5 0.8B) handles plain requests (list the themes, turn on the night light, a reminder in 30 minutes) but now and then proposes a change you did not ask for; the approval catches it. A 4B model (Qwen3.5 4B) answered every test request right. Pick a bigger one with `bxrig ai models recommend` and `bxrig ai models use ID`: the `bxrig` profile follows. On a computer without a graphics card the first answer can take a minute or two, so the `bxrig` profile gives the model 300 seconds.

### Install and update bx-agents

```bash
bxrig ai agents install             # the plan
bxrig ai agents install --yes       # the latest snapshot (the default for now)
bxrig ai agents install --stable --yes
bxrig ai agents update --yes        # the newest again, and restart the agents that run
```

bx-agents is installed for your whole machine with `bx-module` (into `~/.boxlang/modules`), like any BoxLang module. Install also offers your local model to every agent.

### Every bxAgents verb works

```bash
bxrig ai agents Boxy chat                  # the terminal chat
bxrig ai agents Boxy invoke --message="What is on my calendar today?"
bxrig ai agents Boxy routines list
bxrig ai agents Boxy skills find calendar
bxrig ai agents Boxy logs agent
```

`bxrig ai agents NAME VERB ...` is `bxAgents VERB --projectRoot=PROJECT ...`, with your words passed on exactly as you typed them. `bxAgents --help` lists the verbs.

### Your local model profile

Install writes a `bxrig` profile into your bx-agents settings (`~/.bxagents/Agent.yml`): your active local model at BxRig's server. An agent uses it with one line in its `Agent.yml`:

```yaml
profile: bxrig
```

When you change the active model (`bxrig ai models use ID`), the profile follows. Only BxRig's own marked block in that file is written; your other settings stay. `bxrig ai agents profile --off` removes it.

### Where things are

|                                       What                                        |                                             Where                                              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Your agent projects                                                               | `~/Agents/NAME` (`bxrig ai agents dir PATH` moves the folder, `BXRIG_AGENTS_DIR` overrides it) |
| Each agent's data: chats, notes, files, skills, logs                              | `~/.bxagents/NAME`, bx-agents' own place, outside the project, so a build never touches it     |
| Your bx-agents settings, for every agent                                          | `~/.bxagents/Agent.yml`                                                                        |
| BxRig's list: ports, the default, projects added by path, the skills you reviewed | `~/.config/bxrig/agents.json`                                                                  |
| The service of each agent                                                         | `~/.config/systemd/user/bxrig-agent-NAME.service`                                              |

Each agent keeps its data by its name, so two agents can not share a name.

To back up your agents, keep `~/Agents` and `~/.bxagents`. `bxrig ai agents Boxy backup` makes a zip of one agent's data.

Next: [Local AI](/ai/local-ai/index.html) · [MCP and privacy](/ai/mcp-and-privacy/index.html)

# Control Center

`bxrig tui` opens one terminal screen with a list of pages on the left and the open page on the right.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig tui                   # opens on the Dashboard, sidebar open
bxrig tui databases         # one page on its own, sidebar collapsed
bxrig tui list              # every page id and title (--json for scripts)
```

![The Control Center dashboard](/assets/screenshots/control-center-dashboard.webp)

## Dashboard

The first page shows what needs your attention, then the state of the machine:

* **Needs attention:** updates waiting, a backup older than two days (or none yet), a disk over 85% full, a battery under 20%. Move to a line and press Enter, or press its key, to see the plan of the fix. Nothing changes until you press `y`.
* **System:** CPU load, memory, disk and battery.
* **Running:** your databases and VMs, with ports.
* **Backups:** how fresh each place is. Enter opens BxTimeMachine, and you come back to the Dashboard when you leave it.

Each part is read on its own. If one cannot be read, the rest still shows.

|                                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ![The Apps page: installed apps with details](/assets/screenshots/control-center-apps.webp) **Apps** | ![The Maven page: every version, install with one key](/assets/screenshots/control-center-maven.webp) **Maven** (Java, Gradle and BoxLang look the same) |

## One page at a time

`bxrig tui PAGE` opens that page alone, with the page list collapsed, so it feels like an app of its own: `bxrig tui databases`, `bxrig tui ports`, `bxrig tui mail`. An unknown page prints the list and exits 2. The top row shows where you are, `BXRIG › Databases`.

Open and close the page list with the backslash key or `Ctrl+b` (while a page is taking text, such as a filter, only `Ctrl+b` works). You can also click the thin strip at the left edge or the breadcrumb row, or press `Left`. Tab and Shift+Tab still change page. `--sidebar` and `--no-sidebar` force it either way. On a terminal narrower than 90 columns it starts collapsed so the page gets the room. BxRig does not remember the state: the next `bxrig tui` starts open again.

You can open any page without a terminal open first:

* **Menu:** `bxrig menu` has a Control Center section at the end. The first entry opens everything, then one entry per page. Each opens in your default terminal.
* **Application menu (optional):** `bxrig launchers on --yes` adds a "BxRig" submenu to your application menu: the Setup Wizard, the Runner Menu and the Control Center at the top, then Apps and Dashboard, then folders with their own icon (Develop, System, Look) holding one entry per page (menus without folders, like rofi, list them flat). `bxrig launchers status` shows them and `bxrig launchers off --yes` (or `bxrig remove launchers --yes`) takes them away. Entries you edited are kept. Nothing is added unless you ask.
* **Shortcuts:** every page has an unbound shortcut (`tui-databases`, ...). Give it keys with `bxrig keys set tui-databases Super+Alt+B --yes`, then `bxrig keys apply --yes`.

## Keys

|             Key              |                                                   What it does                                                    |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Tab, Shift+Tab (or `]`, `[`) | next and previous page                                                                                            |
| Left                         | move to the page list (Up and Down pick a page), Right or Enter goes back; with the list collapsed, Left opens it |
| `\`, Ctrl+b                  | collapse or open the page list                                                                                    |
| q, Escape, Ctrl+c            | leave                                                                                                             |
| mouse                        | click a page or a row, scroll the wheel                                                                           |

The key bar at the bottom shows the keys of the page you are on.

## Look and Themes

`bxrig tui look` shows the bar you have in a Preview box (the same text-chip pictures the wizard draws) and the settings below it in three groups: **Bar** (top bar layout, battery percentage, clock format, the bar toggle key), **Colors** (a link to the Themes page) and **Apps** (app grid style, dock). The values come from the read-only status commands (`bxrig appearance bar layout status`, `appearance appgrid status`, `appearance battery-percent status`, `time format`). A change is an ordinary command: the plan box shows it with `--dry-run`, and `y` runs it.

`bxrig tui themes` is the bigger selector: every theme, with `Enter` to apply it. The sidebar lists Look and Themes as two pages; the Look page has no theme list of its own.

The whole Control Center is drawn in the colors of the theme you applied last (`~/.config/bxrig/theme.json`), at start and again within a second of applying another one from the Themes page. `--demo` keeps the BxRig colors.

## Back into the wizard

The setup wizard is one entry away from anywhere: "Setup wizard (re-run, prefilled)" in the runner menu (second row, after Apps), "BxRig Setup Wizard" in the application menu, `w` on the Control Center Dashboard, or `bxrig init`. It starts from your saved answers merged with what this machine already has, shows the review, and changes nothing until you confirm.

## Advanced

How a page works: every key that changes something shows a plan first, and `y` runs it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Menu, application menu or shortcut"] --> B["bxrig tui PAGE"]
  B --> C["Page"]
  C --> D["Plan box"]
  D --> E["y runs the command"]
```

### Every page

|      Page      |                                                                                                                                                                          What it does                                                                                                                                                                           |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Dashboard      | what needs attention, meters, what runs, backups                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Apps           | install, remove and update software: Installed, Discover and Updates tabs, a search box that is always there, icons and screenshots (see [Apps](/data/apps/index.html#the-apps-manager))                                                                                                                                                                        |
| AI             | your local models on llama.cpp: Enter makes one active or downloads a pick, `p` asks a question, `t` tests, `u` tunes, `b` runs the bench, `h` opens it on Hugging Face, `x` removes it, `s` sets everything up (see [Local AI](/ai/local-ai/index.html))                                                                                                       |
| Discover       | models for this machine: BxRig's staff picks, then GGUF models on Hugging Face (`/` searches). Enter queues a download, `c` cancels one, `x` clears finished ones, `h` opens Hugging Face                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Agents         | your coding agents: the default one, which use the local model, their tmux sessions. Enter starts a session, `d` makes one the default, `l` points it at the local model or back, `s` lists the sessions                                                                                                                                                        |
| BoxLang agents | your bx-agents agents: Enter opens the chat in a terminal, `o` the web page, `s` starts or stops it, `d` the default one, `l` its log, `i` installs or updates bx-agents (see [BoxLang agents](/ai/boxlang-agents/index.html))                                                                                                                                  |
| BoxLang        | BoxLang versions through `bvm`: use, install, remove                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Modules        | BoxLang modules from ForgeBox: installed and latest versions, `i` install, `u` update, `x` remove                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Servers        | your BoxLang and CFML web apps: `s` start or stop, `r` restart, `o` open, `f` the folder, `l` the log, `a` add one, `x` forget it                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Tasks          | the scheduler: every timed job, when it runs next and how its recent runs went. Enter shows one, `r` runs it now, `p` pauses it, `g` its group, `a` adds one, `x` removes it                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Java           | your Java versions (jenv): global, remove, and `a` to browse every JDK SDKMAN offers and install one (see `bxrig java`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Maven          | every Maven version SDKMAN offers, installed ones marked: install, default, remove (see `bxrig sdk`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Gradle         | the same for Gradle                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Versions       | BoxLang, MatchBox, Java and Node in one table; Enter opens the deep page                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Ports          | what listens on which port and who owns it; stop or kill it, with a plan first. A port with two owners is red                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Network        | the Wi-Fi you are on, your VPNs, the DNS providers (the one in use is marked, with their last benchmark times and the fastest) and the last internet speed. `t` speed test, `b` DNS benchmark, `u` use the DNS on the row, `c` VPN on or off, `q` the Wi-Fi QR code, `w` bring Wi-Fi back                                                                       |
| Packages       | search the repos and the AUR with `/`, then install or remove                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Shortcuts      | every shortcut; rebind (it asks for the keys), reset, conflicts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Machines       | your VMs (Windows and Linux desktops in containers): start, stop, info, new                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Databases      | the databases BxRig runs: start, stop, info, new                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Mail           | the mail your apps send to the catcher (`bxrig mail`): headers and text of the highlighted message, delete, clear, open it in the browser, send a test; it refreshes by itself every 3 seconds                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Storage        | this computer's disk first (space used and the last disk speed; `t` tests it), then NAS shares and cloud remotes: mount, unmount, test                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Secrets        | names only; `v` shows one value for one look                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Boxy           | Boxy's look and voice: its sprite, the speech setting (`v`) and the outfits (Enter puts one on, `e` writes the pictures); see [Boxy's look and voice](/customize/boxy-look/index.html)                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Android        | Android apps with Waydroid (off until you turn it on): the state, then your apps; Enter opens one, `s` starts or stops it, `r` registers it for Google Play, `S` shows the plan to set it up (see [Android apps](/build/android/index.html))                                                                                                                    |
| Privacy        | what leaves this machine: where each agent's model runs, keys by name, MCP servers, telemetry, chat folders; `l`/`L` local model on or off, `t`/`T` telemetry off or on (see [MCP and privacy](/ai/mcp-and-privacy/index.html))                                                                                                                                 |
| Look           | the top bar layout (Minimal, Standard, Dense) with a picture of the bar and the dock, battery percentage, clock format, the key that hides the bar, the app grid style (Launchpad or Terminal-style) and the dock. `-` and `+` (or Right, Space, Enter) pick the previous or next value, and the plan comes first. The color theme is a link to the Themes page |
| Themes         | the 24 themes with a palette and wallpaper preview; Enter shows the plan, y applies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Accessibility  | zoom, reduce motion and the three contrast themes, one row each; Enter (or Space) switches the row, with the plan first                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Logs           | the journal of this boot; `p` changes the lowest priority shown                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

In a table, `/` filters the rows (or searches, on Packages), Enter keeps it and Escape clears it. Every key that changes something shows a plan first.

### Icons

The page list and page headers carry Nerd Font icons when your terminal has the font (the BxRig wizard installs one for Starship). They are on when a Nerd Font is found, and you can force them: `bxrig tui --icons=on` or `--icons=off`, or set `BXRIG_ICONS`. Without the font they would show as boxes, so BxRig leaves them off. Emoji are not used, because terminals draw them two cells wide and the tables would not line up.

### How the pages fit together

Every screen shares one kit for lists, tabs, plan boxes and meters, so they look and behave the same. A page is a small class, which is also how new pages are added. A page can send you to a full screen such as BxTimeMachine and bring you back.

`bxrig tui --demo` shows made-up data and runs nothing; `bxrig tui dashboard --json` prints the page's data, no terminal needed.

Next: [The menu](/desktop/menu/index.html), [Themes](/customize/themes/index.html), [Apps](/data/apps/index.html).

# Databases and virtual machines

Use this page to start a database for your app in one command, or to run a Windows or Linux desktop next to your own. Both run in containers: Podman by default, or Docker if you chose it with `bxrig db engine docker`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["bxrig db"] --> C["Container engine"]
  B["bxrig vm"] --> C
  C --> D["Podman (default)"]
  C --> E["Docker"]
  A --> F["127.0.0.1 only"]
  B --> F
```

The diagram shows that databases and virtual machines share one container engine and listen on this machine only.

## Databases

### Try it

```bash
bxrig db engines                 # what you can run
bxrig db start postgres --yes    # plan first without --yes
bxrig db info postgres           # host, port and how to connect (password hidden)
```

`start` creates a container with a pinned image, publishes its port on `127.0.0.1` only, and keeps the data in a named volume. A container that already exists is never replaced: a stopped one is started again. A password is generated for the engines that need one and kept in `~/.local/share/bxrig/databases/<container>/password` (mode 600), never on a command line.

### Run, look at, stop

```bash
bxrig db list                    # your database containers, running or not
bxrig db status postgres
bxrig db logs postgres           # the last 200 lines
bxrig db stop postgres
bxrig db remove postgres --yes   # the container AND its data
bxrig db remove postgres --keep-data --yes
bxrig db info postgres --show-password
```

`remove` deletes the container, its data volume and the password file. With `--keep-data` they stay, and starting the same name again reuses them.

Need two of the same engine? Give each a name:

```bash
bxrig db start postgres --name=shop --port=5433 --yes
```

Without `--name` the instance is called `default`. A name may contain letters, digits and hyphens (up to 40 characters), and a port is a whole number from 1024 to 65535. Choose your own password with `--ask-password` or `--password-file FILE`. `bxrig db menu` is a pick-from-a-list version of the same actions.

### Engines

|   Kind   |                                              Engines                                               |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SQL      | PostgreSQL 17 (`postgres`), MySQL 8.4 (`mysql`), MariaDB 11.8 (`mariadb`)                          |
| Cache    | Redis 7.4 (`redis`)                                                                                |
| Document | MongoDB 8.0 (`mongodb`), Couchbase community 8.0.2 (`couchbase`)                                   |
| Vector   | PostgreSQL with pgvector (`pgvector`), Chroma (`chroma`), Qdrant (`qdrant`), Weaviate (`weaviate`) |
| Search   | Meilisearch (`meilisearch`), OpenSearch (`opensearch`), Elasticsearch (`elasticsearch`)            |

`bxrig db engines` shows the exact image and default port of each. Milvus is listed but not supported yet: it needs several services, so one container would not work.

### Advanced

* Images are pinned to a major or minor version, never `latest`.
* `bxrig db engine docker` switches the container engine; `bxrig db engine` shows which one is in use.
* Couchbase publishes fixed extra ports, so `--port` is not accepted for it and only one instance can run. Finish its setup in the web console at `http://127.0.0.1:8091`, where you set the administrator name and password yourself.
* OpenSearch and Elasticsearch need the host setting `vm.max_map_count` of at least 262144; `start` stops with exit 4 when it is too low. Both use HTTPS with a self-signed certificate (use `curl -k`) and can take a minute to start. Elasticsearch uses about 1 GB of memory.
* pgvector: run `CREATE EXTENSION vector;` in the database to turn it on.
* Redis, Chroma and Qdrant have no password and Weaviate allows anonymous access: they are safe only because they listen on `127.0.0.1`. Never publish those ports.
* A kept data volume still has the password it was created with, so `start` refuses a different password for it. Remove it with `bxrig db remove ENGINE --yes` to start fresh.
* Exit codes: 0 done, 2 usage or plan printed without `--yes`, 4 a precondition failed (no container engine, unknown or unsupported engine, bad name or port), 6 the container command failed.

## Virtual machines

`bxrig vm` runs full desktops in containers: Windows (the dockur/windows image) and Linux desktops (LinuxServer's webtop, a desktop in your browser).

### Try it

```bash
bxrig vm doctor                          # is this machine ready? (KVM, groups, GPU, disk)
bxrig vm create linux dev                # a Ubuntu XFCE desktop called dev
bxrig vm list                            # all of them: state, ports, disk used
bxrig vm open dev                        # starts it if needed and opens it
```

`create` shows a plan first; add `--yes` to do it. `--dry-run` never changes anything.

### Linux desktops

```bash
bxrig vm versions linux                  # the tags
bxrig vm create linux arch --tag=arch-kde --gpu=auto
```

`versions linux` lists Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Arch with XFCE, KDE Plasma, MATE or i3 (plus LXQt on Ubuntu), and a small Alpine. The default is `ubuntu-xfce`. Make as many as you want; each gets its own port, data folder and password.

`vm open NAME` opens `https://127.0.0.1:PORT/` in your browser. The certificate is self-signed, so accept it once. The user is `bxrig`; show the password with `bxrig vm info NAME --show-password`.

**GPU** (optional): `--gpu=intel` or `--gpu=amd` passes `/dev/dri` in. `--gpu=nvidia` is supported too; it needs the NVIDIA driver 580 or newer and the NVIDIA container toolkit, and it is not available on the Alpine tags. `--gpu=auto` uses `/dev/dri` when the machine has it. `vm doctor` shows what your machine has.

### Windows

```bash
bxrig vm create windows                  # asks which Windows
bxrig vm open NAME --web                 # watch it install
bxrig vm open NAME                       # when ready: opens with FreeRDP
```

Windows installs itself the first time it starts: it downloads the ISO inside the container (3 to 8 GB) and takes a while. When it is ready, `vm open` opens it with FreeRDP, with the clipboard shared and the window resizable.
> **Warning:** You need your own Windows license. The install uses generic trial keys that do not activate Windows.

Windows needs `/dev/kvm`: turn on virtualization in the firmware and put yourself in the `kvm` group. `vm doctor` tells you what is missing. Defaults: half your RAM (4 to 8 GB), half your cores, a 64 GB disk. Change them with `--ram`, `--cpus` and `--disk`.

### Stop and remove

```bash
bxrig vm stop dev
bxrig vm remove dev            # the container, its data, password and menu entry (it asks first)
bxrig vm remove dev --keep-data
bxrig vm size                  # how much disk each VM uses
```

Your shared folder is never deleted. Everything listens on `127.0.0.1` only.

### Advanced

Windows versions (pass `--version=VALUE` in a script):

|            Choice             |    Size     |                         Note                          |
|-------------------------------|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `11` Windows 11 Pro           | 7.9 GB      | the usual choice                                      |
| `11l` Windows 11 LTSC         | 4.7 GB      | long-term servicing edition, fewer bundled apps       |
| `11e` Windows 11 Enterprise   | 6.6 GB      | business edition                                      |
| `10` Windows 10 Pro           | 5.7 GB      | older, for legacy needs                               |
| `10l` Windows 10 LTSC         | 4.6 GB      | long-term servicing edition                           |
| `tiny11` Tiny11               | 5.3 GB      | **unofficial** stripped-down build from the community |
| `core11` Tiny11 Core          | 3.0 GB      | **unofficial**, the most stripped-down                |
| `tiny10` Tiny10               | 3.6 GB      | **unofficial** stripped-down Windows 10               |
| `2025`, `2022` Windows Server | 7.6, 6.0 GB | server editions                                       |

`bxrig vm versions windows` shows all 25 (down to Windows 95 and ReactOS).

Where everything is:

|           What            |                                                    Where                                                     |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Disk and files of each VM | `~/.local/share/bxrig/vms/NAME` (`storage` for Windows, `config` for Linux)                                  |
| The VM's record           | `~/.config/bxrig/vms/NAME.json`                                                                              |
| Its password              | your keyring, as `BXRIG_VM_NAME_PASSWORD` (see `bxrig secrets`)                                              |
| Shared folder             | `~/Windows` (drive Z: in Windows) or `~/Shared` (inside the Linux desktop); `--share=PATH` or `--share=none` |
| App menu entry            | `~/.local/share/applications/bxrig-vm-NAME.desktop`                                                          |
| The container images      | in Podman or Docker (`podman image ls`)                                                                      |

Next: [Mail catcher](/build/mail/index.html) · [Developer tools](/build/developer-tools/index.html) · [Backups](/data/backups/index.html)

markdown:
# Pictures in the terminal

The TUIs can show app icons and screenshots. A picture is never required: when one is missing, slow or broken, BxRig draws a letter tile and carries on.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig tui apps                 # icons and screenshots in the Apps manager
BXRIG_IMAGES=off bxrig tui apps  # letter tiles only
```

![The Apps page with icons](/assets/screenshots/control-center-apps.webp)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["App name"] --> B["Icon theme"]
  B --> C["AppStream icons"]
  C --> D["Dashboard Icons"]
  D --> E["Letter tile"]
```

The diagram shows where an app icon comes from, in order, and the fallback.

## Where pictures come from

|  Picture   |                                                                                                                                                                         Sources, in order                                                                                                                                                                         |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| App icon   | the installed icon theme (your GTK icon theme and what it inherits first, then hicolor) and `.desktop` file, an SVG-only icon turned into a cached 128 px PNG with `rsvg-convert` (librsvg) or ImageMagick when one is installed, the AppStream catalog icons, [Dashboard Icons](https://github.com/homarr-labs/dashboard-icons) (a letter tile when none has it) |
| Screenshot | the AppStream catalog (`archlinux-appstream-data`, optional), downloaded on first view                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Dashboard Icons is Apache-2.0 licensed. The logos in it belong to their owners and are shown only to identify the app. There is no web image search.

## Change how pictures are drawn

MatchBox draws PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP. Terminals that speak the Kitty graphics protocol (Kitty, Ghostty) show the real picture; every other terminal gets half block pixels. `tui.image_support()` reports which. Needs a MatchBox built with `--features bif-tui`.

|      Setting       |                   Effect                    |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `BXRIG_IMAGES=off` | never draw pictures, only letter tiles      |
| `BXRIG_IMAGES=on`  | draw even when the terminal is not detected |
| `BXRIG_SHARE_DIR`  | where `/usr/share` is looked up (tests)     |
| `BXRIG_CACHE_HOME` | replaces the cache folder                   |

## What keeps it safe

* **Never blocks.** Downloads and the screenshot index scan run in the background. The first call returns nothing and the picture shows on a later redraw.
* **Never throws.** Every call is wrapped; a failure becomes a letter tile.
* **Limits.** https only, 5 s to connect, a time cap and a size cap per download (5 MB by default), the file type is checked by its first bytes (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP), files are written to a temporary name and renamed when complete. MatchBox itself refuses files over 20 MB or 12 megapixels.
* **Failures are remembered.** A URL that failed is not tried again for 6 hours, so a bad link cannot be hammered.
* **Bounded disk.** The cache lives in `~/.cache/bxrig/images` and is trimmed to 200 MB, oldest first. Deleting it is always safe.

## Advanced

### For developers

`TuiKit.image( x, y, w, h, path )` draws and answers `true` or `false`. `imageOrTile( x, y, w, h, path, name )` falls back to a coloured tile with the name's first letter. `ImageCache.get( url, kind )` answers a local path or an empty string. `AppIcons.iconFor( name, theme )` and `AppIcons.screenshotsFor( appstreamId )` answer paths the same way.

Tests: `tests/image_cache_test.bxs`, `tests/app_icons_test.bxs` (both start a local server from `tests/image_server.py`) and `tests/tui_kit_test.bxs`.

Next: [Apps and web apps](/data/apps/index.html) · [Updates and channels](/maintain/updates/index.html)

title: The setup wizard
body: The setup wizard The wizard asks for your choices once, shows the commands it will run, and does nothing until you confirm. Re-run it any time with bxrig init . flowchart LR A["Answer the pages"] --> B["Review: the exact commands"] B --> C{"Confirm?"} C -->|"yes"| D["Install screen"] C -->|"no"| E["Nothing changed"] D --> F["Summary and saved answers"] bxrig init opens a full-screen form with these pages: Desktop , Look , Top bar layout , App grid style , Theme , Input , Developer , Toolchains , Containers , NAS , Backups (with the copy somewhere else), Apps , AI , Extras and Import , then a review screen that lists exactly the commands it will run. With the Customize choice on the Apps page there is one more page per catalog group. Nothing runs until you confirm. Welcome Look: dark or light, dock, bar position Look: the world clock and its time zones Input: layouts, scrolling, shortcut style The look pages After Look (dark, light or auto, the dock, where the bar sits, the world clock) come three pages that show what you are choosing: Top bar layout (Hyprland and Both): Minimal, Standard (the default and the recommendation) or Dense. Each option draws its bar as a strip of text chips with the dock line below the list. Standard has the capture icon, Minimal does not, Dense adds brightness and weather. The arrow keys select as they move, so the strips and the description follow your cursor and Enter keeps what is highlighted. Later: bxrig appearance bar layout minimal|standard|dense or the Look page of the Control Center. App grid style (Hyprland and Both): Launchpad (the default, big colored tiles on a rounded card) or Terminal-style (flat glyphs, key hints, square corners). Both grids are drawn side by side and the arrow keys switch. Later: bxrig appearance appgrid launchpad|terminal . Theme (every desktop): every theme in themes/ on a row with a swatch, BxRig the default. A pane next to the list shows the palette of the highlighted theme, read from its colors.toml , and a sample terminal in those colors. The wizard itself is drawn in the highlighted theme, so what you see is what the desktop will get. The icon set is not asked: BxRig's own icons are used. Later: bxrig theme set NAME or the Themes page of the Control Center. On a terminal narrower than 92 columns (no step list) the Theme page keeps the list and the pane side by side; between 92 and 96 columns the pane is dropped and the rows keep their swatches.
