markdown:
# Calendar and reminders

Use this page to see what is coming up without opening a browser, and to set reminders. BxRig keeps a copy of your calendars on this machine with [vdirsyncer](https://github.com/pimutils/vdirsyncer), shows what is coming up in the terminal and in the Clock panel, and pops up reminders you set.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig pkg install vdirsyncer
bxrig calendar add ical holidays webcal://example.org/holidays.ics
bxrig calendar sync
bxrig calendar agenda --days=3
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Google or iCal calendar"] --> B["vdirsyncer sync"]
  B --> C["Local .ics files"]
  C --> D["bxrig calendar agenda"]
  C --> E["Clock panel"]
  S["Scheduler: calendar-sync"] --> B
```

The diagram shows how calendars are copied to your machine and where you read them.

## Add a calendar

|      Kind       |                                Add it with                                |                                                 Notes                                                  |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| An iCal address | `bxrig calendar add ical NAME URL`                                        | Any published `.ics` or `webcal://` address. Read only.                                                |
| Google Calendar | `bxrig calendar add google NAME --client-id=ID --client-secret-file=FILE` | Every calendar of the account. The first `bxrig calendar sync`, in a terminal, opens Google's sign-in. |

For Google, create a project in the Google Cloud console, turn on the **CalDAV API** , and create an **OAuth client** of type **Desktop app** . Pass its client ID, and save its client secret in a file for `--client-secret-file`.

`bxrig calendar` lists the calendars and how many events each has. `bxrig calendar remove NAME --yes` forgets one and deletes its local copy; the calendar itself stays where it is.

## Set reminders

```bash
bxrig remind "Call Ana" --in=30m
bxrig remind "Stand up" --at=09:25              # today, or tomorrow when 09:25 has passed
bxrig remind "Renew the domain" --at="2026-12-01 10:00"
bxrig remind list
bxrig remind done 3
```

`--in` takes minutes, hours and days: `45`, `30m`, `2h`, `1d`, `1h30m`.

![bxrig remind list](/assets/screenshots/remind-list.webp)

## See it in the Clock panel

Under the world clocks, the Clock panel shows today's and tomorrow's events and the reminders still to come. A reminder whose time has come is highlighted; its check button marks it done.

## Keep it up to date

With the [scheduler](/data/scheduler/index.html) installed, adding a calendar adds the task **calendar-sync** (every 15 minutes) and adding a reminder adds the task **reminders** (every minute), which pops up each reminder once, as a notice that stays until you close it. Installing the scheduler later adds both when you already have calendars or reminders.

## Advanced

BxRig writes its own vdirsyncer configuration (`~/.config/bxrig/vdirsyncer/config`, readable only by you), so a vdirsyncer setup of your own is not touched. The events are kept as `.ics` files in `~/.local/share/bxrig/calendars`.

Next: [Scheduler](/data/scheduler/index.html) · [AI agents](/ai/boxlang-agents/index.html)

Without --answers , the wizard's default answers are applied. More options: --channel stable|beta , --no-wizard , --dry-run , --source , --snapshot and --matchbox-branch (below). You choose which one: You pass MatchBox How nothing the stable release mvm install latest , mvm use latest --snapshot (or BXRIG_MATCHBOX_CHANNEL=snapshot ) the snapshot build mvm install snapshot , mvm use snapshot (mvm skips a build that has not changed) --matchbox-branch REF [ --matchbox-repo OWNER/NAME ] (or BXRIG_MATCHBOX_BRANCH , BXRIG_MATCHBOX_REPO ) a branch of a MatchBox repository, default ortus-boxlang/matchbox shallow clone, cargo build --release --features bif-tui , installed under ~/.local/share/bxrig/matchbox/bin curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash -s -- --snapshot curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash -s -- --matchbox-branch bxrig curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash -s -- --matchbox-branch feature/x --matchbox-repo someone/matchbox The normal install needs no particular MatchBox. The stable and snapshot builds do not have it yet (the bxrig branch is ahead of develop ), so a stage that compiles BxRig ( install.sh from a checkout, --source github:... ) first runs a small probe, and stops with This MatchBox (0.13.2) cannot compile BxRig ... Use the branch build: install.sh toolchains --yes --matchbox-branch bxrig if the MatchBox lacks it. It never switches MatchBox on its own. --source github:... therefore builds the bxrig branch by default; give --matchbox-branch to use another one, and --snapshot makes it stop at the probe. bxrig doctor reports such a MatchBox as miss matchbox ... (cannot compile BxRig; install: install.sh toolchains --yes --matchbox-branch bxrig) and exits 4. A branch build comes first. It is installed under ~/.local/share/bxrig/matchbox/bin and the installer calls it by that path, so the matchbox that mvm manages is not replaced. Add that directory to your PATH if you want matchbox to be the branch build. Running the installer again with --snapshot removes the branch build so that mvm's MatchBox is the one in use; running it with no option leaves what is installed alone, and rebuilds a branch only when its head moved. REF and OWNER/NAME may contain only letters, digits and . _ / @ + - ( . _ - for the owner and repository), may not start with a dash and are passed to git as arguments, never through a shell. --matchbox-from-source is the older spelling of --matchbox-branch bxrig . install.sh toolchains --yes [--snapshot | --matchbox-branch REF [--matchbox-repo OWNER/NAME]] re-runs just this stage. BXRIG_MATCHBOX_FILE=PATH installs a MatchBox you built yourself instead. Testing a branch curl -fsSL https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/bxrig/install.sh | bash -s -- --source github:ortus-boxlang/BxRig@development --yes --source SPEC (or BXRIG_SOURCE ) says where BxRig comes from: SPEC Meaning stable The default: the signed release beta The same as --channel beta github:OWNER/REPO@REF A branch, tag or commit of a GitHub repository. github:@REF and github:REF mean ortus-boxlang/BxRig A GitHub source is unsigned : no release signature and no checksum from the BxRig downloads. The installer prints a warning, and continues only with --yes or after you type the word unsigned (without either it stops with exit 2 and changes nothing). It downloads https://codeload.github.com/OWNER/REPO/tar.gz/REF (public repositories; for a private one set GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN , which is sent to GitHub only as a request header and never printed or logged), unpacks it, and runs that tree's own bootstrap/install.sh stages: packages, toolchains, the program built from the tree's src/Main.bx with a MatchBox that has the terminal UI (the bxrig branch unless you chose another, see above), the core apps, then the wizard from the freshly built program. --dry-run downloads and unpacks the tree, prints the commit and the tree's plan (including the MatchBox build), and installs nothing. The source ( github:OWNER/REPO@REF ) and the resolved commit are written to ~/.cache/bxrig/install.log and to ~/.local/share/bxrig/install-source . bxrig update does not read them: it compares the program with the channel's release, so after a GitHub install bxrig update check reports an update, and bxrig update apply --yes replaces your build with the stable (or beta) one. Skip update apply while you test the branch.

# Install options

The [normal install](/start/install/index.html) is one command. This page is for when you need more: no one at the keyboard, the beta channel, a specific MatchBox, or a branch you want to test.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Which install do you need?"] --> B["Normal"]
    A --> C["Unattended"]
    A --> D["Beta channel"]
    A --> E["Test a branch"]
    B --> B1["curl ... | bash"]
    C --> C1["--yes --answers answers.json"]
    D --> D1["--channel beta"]
    E --> E1["--source github:OWNER/REPO@REF"]
```

## Unattended

```bash
curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash -s -- --yes --answers answers.json
```

`--yes` never asks (it needs passwordless sudo). Without `--answers`, the wizard's default answers are applied. More options: `--channel stable|beta`, `--no-wizard`, `--dry-run`, `--source`, `--snapshot` and `--matchbox-branch` (below).

### Which MatchBox

The installer installs [MatchBox](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/matchbox) with `mvm`, which it installs first. You choose which one:

|                                                   You pass                                                   |                                MatchBox                                 |                                                      How                                                       |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| nothing                                                                                                      | the **stable** release                                                  | `mvm install latest`, `mvm use latest`                                                                         |
| `--snapshot` (or `BXRIG_MATCHBOX_CHANNEL=snapshot`)                                                          | the **snapshot** build                                                  | `mvm install snapshot`, `mvm use snapshot` (mvm skips a build that has not changed)                            |
| `--matchbox-branch REF` \[`--matchbox-repo OWNER/NAME`\] (or `BXRIG_MATCHBOX_BRANCH`, `BXRIG_MATCHBOX_REPO`) | a **branch** of a MatchBox repository, default `ortus-boxlang/matchbox` | shallow clone, `cargo build --release --features bif-tui`, installed under `~/.local/share/bxrig/matchbox/bin` |

```bash
curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash -s -- --snapshot
curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash -s -- --matchbox-branch bxrig
curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash -s -- --matchbox-branch feature/x --matchbox-repo someone/matchbox
```

* **The normal install needs no particular MatchBox.** It installs the prebuilt `bxrig` of your channel, so MatchBox is only part of the toolchain and any version is fine.
* **Compiling BxRig needs a MatchBox with the terminal UI.** The stable and snapshot builds do not have it yet (the `bxrig` branch is ahead of `develop`), so a stage that compiles BxRig (`install.sh` from a checkout, `--source github:...`) first runs a small probe, and stops with `This MatchBox (0.13.2) cannot compile BxRig ... Use the branch build: install.sh toolchains --yes --matchbox-branch bxrig` if the MatchBox lacks it. It never switches MatchBox on its own. `--source github:...` therefore builds the `bxrig` branch by default; give `--matchbox-branch` to use another one, and `--snapshot` makes it stop at the probe. `bxrig doctor` reports such a MatchBox as `miss matchbox ... (cannot compile BxRig; install: install.sh toolchains --yes --matchbox-branch bxrig)` and exits 4.
* **A branch build comes first.** It is installed under `~/.local/share/bxrig/matchbox/bin` and the installer calls it by that path, so the `matchbox` that `mvm` manages is not replaced. Add that directory to your `PATH` if you want `matchbox` to be the branch build. Running the installer again with `--snapshot` removes the branch build so that mvm's MatchBox is the one in use; running it with no option leaves what is installed alone, and rebuilds a branch only when its head moved.
* `REF` and `OWNER/NAME` may contain only letters, digits and `. _ / @ + -` (`. _ -` for the owner and repository), may not start with a dash and are passed to git as arguments, never through a shell. `--matchbox-from-source` is the older spelling of `--matchbox-branch bxrig`.
* `install.sh toolchains --yes [--snapshot | --matchbox-branch REF [--matchbox-repo OWNER/NAME]]` re-runs just this stage. `BXRIG_MATCHBOX_FILE=PATH` installs a MatchBox you built yourself instead.

### Testing a branch

```bash
curl -fsSL https://downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/bxrig/install.sh | bash -s -- --source github:ortus-boxlang/BxRig@development --yes
```

`--source SPEC` (or `BXRIG_SOURCE`) says where BxRig comes from:

|          SPEC           |                                                  Meaning                                                  |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `stable`                | The default: the signed release                                                                           |
| `beta`                  | The same as `--channel beta`                                                                              |
| `github:OWNER/REPO@REF` | A branch, tag or commit of a GitHub repository. `github:@REF` and `github:REF` mean `ortus-boxlang/BxRig` |

A GitHub source is **unsigned** : no release signature and no checksum from the BxRig downloads. The installer prints a warning, and continues only with `--yes` or after you type the word `unsigned` (without either it stops with exit 2 and changes nothing). It downloads `https://codeload.github.com/OWNER/REPO/tar.gz/REF` (public repositories; for a private one set `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN`, which is sent to GitHub only as a request header and never printed or logged), unpacks it, and runs that tree's own `bootstrap/install.sh` stages: packages, toolchains, the program built from the tree's `src/Main.bx` with a MatchBox that has the terminal UI (the `bxrig` branch unless you chose another, see above), the core apps, then the wizard from the freshly built program. `--dry-run` downloads and unpacks the tree, prints the commit and the tree's plan (including the MatchBox build), and installs nothing.

The source (`github:OWNER/REPO@REF`) and the resolved commit are written to `~/.cache/bxrig/install.log` and to `~/.local/share/bxrig/install-source`. `bxrig update` does not read them: it compares the program with the channel's release, so after a GitHub install `bxrig update check` reports an update, and `bxrig update apply --yes` replaces your build with the stable (or beta) one. Skip `update apply` while you test the branch.

markdown:
# Launcher

On other desktops, or if you prefer it, search apps, files, your clipboard and BxRig's own actions from one keyboard-first box. [Vicinae](https://github.com/vicinaehq/vicinae) is the launcher and menu BxRig recommends and the wizard's default (Noctalia's own launcher, Walker, Rofi, Fuzzel and Wofi are still choices), drawn in your BxRig theme.

## The BxRig launcher (Noctalia panel)

On the Noctalia desktop, `Super+Space` opens the BxRig launcher: one flat search box, drawn in your theme. Type and it ranks, best first:

* a **calculator answer** (`2*(3+4)` gives `14`; Enter copies it);
* an **Ask Boxy** row, and **Tab** switches the whole panel to a chat with Boxy (see below);
* **menu actions** with their path, such as `Trigger › Capture`, so every action of `bxrig menu` is one search away;
* **applications** with their icons, and **themes** (Enter applies the theme);
* a **Clipboard history** row, which opens the clipboard panel: the history on the left, the full text of the highlighted entry on the right, Enter copies it back (`Super+Ctrl+V` opens it directly);
* **web searches** (DuckDuckGo, Google, GitHub, BoxLang docs) at the end.

![The launcher with a calculator answer](/assets/screenshots/launcher-answer.webp)

![Menu actions on themed icon tiles, with their path](/assets/screenshots/launcher-search.webp)

![A theme row, and the Ask Boxy row](/assets/screenshots/launcher-ask-boxy.webp)

![The clipboard history with the entry on the right](/assets/screenshots/launcher-clipboard.webp)

Every row sits on a rounded **icon tile** tinted with the theme's colours: menu actions get a glyph for what they do (a camera for screenshots, a palette for themes), sections keep their colour (Remove and System are red), web searches and Boxy are the tertiary colour, and an application shows its own icon. The tiles follow the Noctalia theme, so a theme change recolours them.

### Boxy mode

Press **Tab** (or Enter on the *Ask Boxy* row) and the launcher becomes a chat with your default agent, Boxy. Type, press Enter, and the answer appears; a tool Boxy wants to run shows **Approve** and **Reject** . **New chat** starts a thread over, **Open full chat** opens the chat window, and Tab goes back to the launcher. If Boxy is not set up or not running, the panel says so and offers **Make Boxy** or **Start** . It uses `bxrig ai agents ask TEXT --thread=ID --json` (not `bxrig ai ask`, which asks the local model directly).

![Boxy mode: an example conversation with a tool waiting for approval](/assets/screenshots/launcher-boxy.webp)

### The menu

`Super+Alt+Space` opens the BxRig menu as a panel in the same style, like the Omarchy menu: the sections as icon tiles, a header with where you are (`Trigger › Capture`), Enter or Right to go in, Left to go back, type to filter the level. It lists the same entries as `bxrig menu` (`bxrig menu level "Trigger > Capture" --json` is the data), and a leaf runs through `bxrig launcher run`.

![The menu panel, top level](/assets/screenshots/menu-panel-root.webp)

![A level of the menu panel](/assets/screenshots/menu-panel-capture.webp)

Things you run often rise to the top (kept in `~/.local/state/bxrig/launcher.json`). F2 opens the Actions list for the highlighted row. The menu panel is on `Super+Alt+Space`, for browsing by section.

The panels are the `bxrig/launcher` plugin. They call the same commands you can run yourself:

```bash
bxrig launcher search capture --json     # the ranked rows
bxrig launcher run theme:nord            # what Enter does for a row
bxrig launcher run web:ddg bash docs     # answer and web rows take the words typed
bxrig clipboard list token --json        # the clipboard history, filtered
bxrig clipboard copy 42                  # put one entry back
```

The clipboard needs `cliphist` and `wl-clipboard` (`bxrig install cliphist wl-clipboard`). The ranking idea follows [oma-cast](https://github.com/typecraft-dev/oma-cast) (MIT).

## Vicinae

### Try it

```bash
bxrig pkg install vicinae
bxrig launcher setup --yes
bxrig launcher                  # what is set up
```

`bxrig launcher setup` shows its plan first. With `--yes` it:

* makes Vicinae BxRig's launcher and menu (the same as `bxrig runner set vicinae` and `bxrig runner menu-set vicinae`), so `bxrig menu` opens in Vicinae;
* writes the **BxRig theme** for Vicinae and selects it;
* adds BxRig's actions to Vicinae's search as **script commands**;
* starts the Vicinae server when it is not running.

Vicinae's own `settings.json` is never edited.

## It follows your theme

Every `bxrig theme set` rewrites `~/.local/share/vicinae/themes/bxrig.toml` from the theme's colours: the background, the text, the accent for selection and focus, and the theme's red, green, yellow, blue, magenta and cyan. Vicinae watches that folder, so the change shows at once. When Vicinae is your launcher, BxRig also selects the theme.

![The Vicinae theme BxRig writes](/assets/screenshots/launcher-theme.webp)

## Run BxRig from the search

|       Command        |                     What it does                      |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| BxRig Control Center | Every BxRig command as one menu                       |
| Agenda               | Your calendars for the next 7 days                    |
| Next event           | Your next event today, shown under the command's name |
| Remind me            | A reminder: what, then `30m`, `2h` or `09:25`         |
| Reminders            | The reminders still to come                           |
| World clock          | The time in your world clock zones                    |
| Next theme           | Switch to the next BxRig theme                        |
| Check for updates    | Whether a BxRig update is waiting                     |
| Scheduled tasks      | The scheduler's tasks and how they ran                |
| BoxLang servers      | Your BoxLang apps and their ports                     |
| Lock screen          | Lock the screen                                       |

They live in `~/.local/share/vicinae/scripts/bxrig`. Vicinae reads its script folders when it starts, every 15 minutes, and when you run **Reload Script Directories** . `bxrig launcher scripts --yes` writes them again, and `bxrig launcher scripts remove --yes` deletes them. Script commands of your own in other folders are not touched.

## Search your files

Vicinae indexes your home folder in the background and keeps the index up to date.

```bash
bxrig launcher files            # Vicinae's file search
bxrig launcher files invoice    # with "invoice" already typed
```

Next: [The menu](/desktop/menu/index.html), [Themes](/customize/themes/index.html).

# Your own config

BxRig writes starter config files once and generated files again and again. It never overwrites a file you edited, and every change it does make can be undone.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig config list                  # every managed file and its state
bxrig config diff hypr/bxrig.lua   # how it differs from what BxRig would write
bxrig config history               # every change BxRig made, with an id
```

`config list` prints one line per file, such as `hypr/bxrig.lua: clean (/home/you/.config/hypr/bxrig.lua)`.

## What is yours and what is BxRig's

|                Kind                |                                                         Example                                                         |                                            Rule                                            |
|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Starter**, written once          | `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`, `~/.config/noctalia/config.toml`, terminal and Starship configs                          | Yours from the moment it is written. Edit freely.                                          |
| **Generated**, rewritten on change | `~/.config/hypr/bxrig.lua`, `~/.config/bxrig/theme/look.lua`, `hypr.lua`, `monitors.lua`, `~/.config/xremap/config.yml` | BxRig's. Never edit; change the setting instead.                                           |
| **Settings** BxRig reads           | `~/.config/bxrig/shortcuts.json`, `appearance.json`, `menu.json`                                                        | Yours, through the commands (`bxrig keys set`, `bxrig appearance`) or by hand where noted. |

Every path is listed in [Files and folders](/reference/config-files/index.html).
> **Note:** Moving `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` moves all of these. `BXRIG_CONFIG_HOME` wins over it.

## Edit a starter file

Open it and change it. BxRig will not touch it again. If you want BxRig's current starter back, `bxrig refresh hyprland --starter --yes` (or `noctalia`) rewrites it after a backup.

## Use BxRig's generated files from your own config

The starter Hyprland file already loads the generated shortcuts with `require("bxrig")` at the bottom. For anything else, add one include line to your own file:

Replace `/home/you` with your home folder.

|   Tool    |                                  Line to add                                  |
|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Ghostty   | `config-file = ?/home/you/.config/bxrig/theme/ghostty`                        |
| kitty     | `include /home/you/.config/bxrig/theme/kitty.conf`                            |
| alacritty | `import = ["/home/you/.config/bxrig/theme/alacritty.toml"]` under `[general]` |
| foot      | `include=/home/you/.config/bxrig/theme/foot.ini`                              |
| tmux      | `source-file /home/you/.config/bxrig/theme/tmux.conf`                         |
| rofi      | `@theme "/home/you/.config/bxrig/theme/rofi.rasi"`                            |

`bxrig theme set` prints the exact line, with your real path, for each config of yours that does not follow the theme yet.

## How a change is applied

Every file BxRig writes goes through one safe writer.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Plan"] --> B["Backup"]
  B --> C["Atomic write"]
  C --> D["Verify"]
  D --> E["Journal"]
```

* **Plan:** without `--yes` you see what would happen and nothing changes (exit 2).
* **Backup:** the old file is copied to `~/.local/state/bxrig/backups/NAME/` (mode 600).
* **Atomic write:** the new text goes to a temporary file, then replaces the target in one step.
* **Journal:** one record per change in `~/.local/state/bxrig/journal/`, with the file's hash before and after and the backup path. BxRig keeps the last 20 per file.

A single lock file (`~/.local/state/bxrig/lock`) stops two BxRig runs from writing at once. A symlink or special file at the target is refused.

## Drift: when you edited a file

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["bxrig config apply NAME"] --> B{"State of the file"}
  B -->|"clean"| C["Nothing to do"]
  B -->|"missing or outdated"| D["Written, backup kept"]
  B -->|"drifted"| E["Kept and reported"]
  E --> F["config diff, then --force"]
```

|   State    |                                   Meaning                                    |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `clean`    | the file is exactly what BxRig would write                                   |
| `missing`  | the file does not exist yet                                                  |
| `outdated` | the file is what BxRig last wrote, but BxRig would now write something newer |
| `drifted`  | you changed it. BxRig keeps it and says so                                   |
| `blocked`  | the target is not a regular file (for example a symlink)                     |

To see what differs run `bxrig config diff NAME`. To replace your version anyway, `bxrig config apply NAME --force --yes`; your version is kept in the backup.

## Undo

```bash
bxrig config history hypr/bxrig.lua            # find the journal id
bxrig config restore hypr/bxrig.lua ID --yes   # put that backup back
```

A restore puts the backup back byte for byte and records itself in the journal. It refuses when there is no backup (the file did not exist before, or the backup was pruned) or when the backup no longer matches its recorded hash.

## Advanced

* `bxrig config list|diff|apply|restore|history` take `--dry-run`, `--force` and `--json`.
* `bxrig refresh hyprland|noctalia|terminals|shell|nvim|theme|all` puts a whole component's files back to what BxRig ships, with a backup first and without installing anything. `--force` overwrites a file you edited, `bxrig refresh list` shows what each component owns.
* `bxrig config apply NAME` takes the name shown by `config list`.
* Config snapshots of your whole BxRig setup are a different tool: see [Backups](/data/backups/index.html).

Next: [Files and folders](/reference/config-files/index.html), [Themes](/customize/themes/index.html), [Shortcuts](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html).

markdown:
# Add a shortcut

You will bind a key to a BxRig command by adding one row to one table. Hyprland, Plasma and xremap all read that table, so there is nothing else to wire up.

## Files you touch

|               File                |                          What for                          |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `src/bxrig/Shortcuts.bx`          | The table: add one line in `rawRows()`.                    |
| `src/bxrig/MenuTree.bx`           | Optional: a runner (BxRig menu) entry for the same action. |
| `tests/shortcuts_test.bxs`        | Add a check for your key.                                  |
| `tests/shortcuts_runner_test.bxs` | Run it when you touch the menu.                            |

## How one table feeds three targets

This diagram shows which rows go to which output.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T["Shortcuts.bx table: one row per action"] --> S["Style: Traditional or Mac"]
  S --> X["xremap: remap rows"]
  S --> H["Hyprland Lua: bind and hypr-bind rows"]
  S --> P["Plasma kglobalshortcutsrc: bind rows"]
  T --> R["keys run ID, keys sheet, keys search"]
```

## Steps

1. Pick a free key. Look at what is taken, in your style:

   ```bash
   bxrig keys show
   bxrig keys search notify
   ```

2. Add a row with `bx()` in `rawRows()` of `src/bxrig/Shortcuts.bx`, inside the group it belongs to. This one runs `bxrig notify uptime` (assume that command exists, see [Add a command](/developer/add-a-command/index.html)).

   ```boxlang
   bx( "notify-uptime", G.note, "Show the uptime", "Super+Ctrl+Alt+U", "Super+Ctrl+Alt+U", "notify uptime" ),
   ```

   The arguments are, in order: a unique `id`, the group, the text people read, the **Traditional** keys, the **Mac** keys, and the words after `bxrig`.
3. Keys are written `Super+Ctrl+Alt+U`: modifiers `Super`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `Ctrl`, then a letter, a digit, or a named key (`Space`, `Return`, `Comma`, `Print`, `F5`...). An empty string `""` means no key in that style.

4. Check for double use before you commit:

   ```bash
   bxrig keys conflicts
   ```

5. Optional: if people should also find it in the BxRig menu, add an entry in `src/bxrig/MenuTree.bx`, in the section it fits. `spawn` opens the command, `run` shows its output.

   ```boxlang
   spawn( "Show the uptime", [ "notify", "uptime" ] ),
   ```

6. Add a check to `tests/shortcuts_test.bxs`, next to the others:

   ```boxlang
   testkit.check( "Super+Ctrl+Alt+U shows the uptime", keyOf( trad, "notify-uptime" ) == "Super+Ctrl+Alt+U" && keyOf( mac, "notify-uptime" ) == "Super+Ctrl+Alt+U" );
   ```

## See it working

```bash
scripts/dev-build.sh
dist/bxrig keys show | grep uptime
dist/bxrig keys render hyprland | grep uptime
dist/bxrig keys run notify-uptime        # runs the command the key stands for
dist/bxrig keys apply --dry-run          # what would be written
dist/bxrig keys apply --yes              # write it, then press the key
```

## Test it

```bash
cd src && matchbox ../tests/shortcuts_test.bxs
cd src && matchbox ../tests/shortcuts_runner_test.bxs
tests/keys-test.sh dist/bxrig
```

The runner test also checks that every `menu open ROUTE` key points at exactly one menu route.

## Common mistakes

* Two rows on one combo: `keys conflicts` lists them under `within`. A binding on a key that a remap rewrites first (Cmd-style keys in the Mac style) can never fire, and is listed under `remapShadows`.
* A row id used twice: ids must be unique, the test checks it.
* Forgetting that both styles need a value: use `""` on purpose, not by accident.
* Words that are not a real `bxrig` command: `keys run ID` exits 4 or 6.

## Advanced

* Row kinds: `remap` (xremap rewrites the key, with `to` and `termTo` for terminals), `bind` (Hyprland and Plasma), `hypr-bind` (Hyprland only). `bx()` makes a `hypr-bind` that runs a `bxrig` command. Use `row()` directly for a Lua dispatch such as `hl.dsp.exec_cmd(terminal)`, with an options table like `{ release = true }` for key-up binds.
* Users rebind with `bxrig keys set ID KEYS --yes`; overrides live in `~/.config/bxrig/shortcuts.json`. Only bindings can be changed, not remaps.
* `bxrig keys style traditional|mac` picks the style. See [Shortcuts](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html) for the user view.
* Next: [Tests](/developer/tests/index.html), [Code rules](/developer/code-rules/index.html).

Try it bxrig input status # devices, drivers, helpers, what is missing bxrig input offer # the plan: what to install for the devices found bxrig input offer --yes # install it bxrig input undo --yes # remove only what offer installed The flow from finding a device to installing and removing its helpers. flowchart LR A["input status"] --> B["Devices found"] B --> C["input offer: the plan"] C --> D["--yes installs helpers"] D --> E["input undo removes them"] Magic Mouse and Magic Trackpad work through the Linux kernel; Logitech's Logi Options+ has a Linux equivalent in Solaar. The offer input offer is a plan until you add --yes ( --dry-run shows it and changes nothing). Found Installs Why a Logitech device solaar Buttons, DPI, scroll and battery: what Logi Options+ does on a Mac. Its package installs a udev rule, so no root daemon is needed. a Logitech gaming mouse libratbag and piper Report rate, DPI and profiles of gaming mice. "Gaming mouse" is a guess from the name (G-series, G Pro, Superlight, Lightspeed, "Gaming"); the plan says so. a Magic Trackpad on Hyprland libinput-gestures (AUR) Three-finger swipes. A Magic Mouse has no touchpad gestures here. On Plasma use System Settings, Touchpad. any of them upower Battery levels. Choose by hand with --for=apple , --for=logitech or --for=both ( --for=detect is the default). Use one tool per Logitech device: Solaar, libratbag and Piper can all talk to the same mouse and are not meant to run together. logiops is not offered. input undo removes the packages offer installed and nothing else; your own settings in ~/.config stay. In the wizard The Input page asks "Input devices" (Detect and offer helpers, None, Apple, Logitech, Apple and Logitech). It appears when a device is detected or the Mac-style keys are on; the default is Detect. The choice becomes one optional step, bxrig input offer --for=CHOICE --yes , that does nothing when nothing is found. Apple Magic bxrig input apple checks the driver ( hid_magicmouse ), the Bluetooth service, the battery and the driver's module options: scroll_speed , scroll_acceleration , emulate_scroll_wheel and emulate_3button . It exits 4 when the kernel has no hid_magicmouse . Scroll speed is a kernel module option, from 0 to 63 (default 32): bxrig input apple --scroll-speed=48 # the plan bxrig input apple --scroll-speed=48 --yes # writes /etc/modprobe.d/bxrig-magicmouse.conf with sudo It applies the next time the module loads: reconnect the mouse or reboot. If the driver is built into your kernel, modprobe options are not read; the command says so and you add hid_magicmouse.scroll_speed=48 to the kernel command line instead. bxrig input undo removes the file. Gestures stay with libinput-gestures ( bxrig input gestures --yes , Hyprland): BxRig does not write Hyprland's own gesture configuration, because its syntax changed between versions and is not verified here. To pair a device use bluetoothctl (or the Bluetooth panel): scan on , pair , trust , connect . Logitech bxrig input logitech shows the receivers (Unifying, Bolt, Lightspeed) and devices with their battery, the hid_logitech_dj and hid_logitech_hidpp drivers, whether Solaar's udev rule ( 42-logitech-unify-permissions.rules ) is installed, and, when Solaar is installed, what solaar show lists. Firmware updates are not part of Solaar: use fwupdmgr . Advanced Detection needs no root and no extra tool: it reads the kernel's /sys/bus/hid/devices (vendor 05AC is Apple, 046D is Logitech; bus 0005 is Bluetooth, 0003 USB), bluetoothctl devices for paired devices that are not connected now, and upower for a battery the kernel did not report. What is found input status lists each device with its kind ( apple-mouse , apple-trackpad , apple-keyboard , logitech-mouse , logitech-keyboard , logitech-receiver , other ), how it is connected, and its battery. An Apple device counts when its name has "Magic" in it; no product ids are hard-coded. The kind is read from the name, so an unusual name can land in other . It also shows whether the drivers are loaded or built in (a built-in driver never shows in lsmod , which is why the old doctor could say "not loaded" for a working mouse). Not verified on real hardware Magic Trackpad 2, Magic Mouse 2 and an MX Master have not been tested here; the commands are tested against a fake sysfs and fake tools. Whether upower reports these batteries is unconfirmed (the kernel's own battery is read first), and whether hid_magicmouse is built in on CachyOS kernels is not known. Next: Displays, power and time , Shortcuts .
markdown:
# Mice, trackpads and keyboards

Get Apple Magic Mouse, Magic Trackpad and Logitech devices working well on Linux. BxRig finds them and offers the helpers around them.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig input status          # devices, drivers, helpers, what is missing
bxrig input offer           # the plan: what to install for the devices found
bxrig input offer --yes     # install it
bxrig input undo --yes      # remove only what offer installed
```

The flow from finding a device to installing and removing its helpers.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["input status"] --> B["Devices found"]
  B --> C["input offer: the plan"]
  C --> D["--yes installs helpers"]
  D --> E["input undo removes them"]
```

Magic Mouse and Magic Trackpad work through the Linux kernel; Logitech's Logi Options+ has a Linux equivalent in Solaar.

## The offer

`input offer` is a plan until you add `--yes` (`--dry-run` shows it and changes nothing).

|            Found             |         Installs          |                                                                               Why                                                                                |
|------------------------------|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| a Logitech device            | `solaar`                  | Buttons, DPI, scroll and battery: what Logi Options+ does on a Mac. Its package installs a udev rule, so no root daemon is needed.                               |
| a Logitech gaming mouse      | `libratbag` and `piper`   | Report rate, DPI and profiles of gaming mice. "Gaming mouse" is a **guess from the name** (G-series, G Pro, Superlight, Lightspeed, "Gaming"); the plan says so. |
| a Magic Trackpad on Hyprland | `libinput-gestures` (AUR) | Three-finger swipes. A Magic Mouse has no touchpad gestures here. On Plasma use System Settings, Touchpad.                                                       |
| any of them                  | `upower`                  | Battery levels.                                                                                                                                                  |

Choose by hand with `--for=apple`, `--for=logitech` or `--for=both` (`--for=detect` is the default). Use one tool per Logitech device: Solaar, libratbag and Piper can all talk to the same mouse and are not meant to run together. logiops is not offered.

`input undo` removes the packages `offer` installed and nothing else; your own settings in `~/.config` stay.

## In the wizard

The **Input** page asks "Input devices" (Detect and offer helpers, None, Apple, Logitech, Apple and Logitech). It appears when a device is detected or the Mac-style keys are on; the default is Detect. The choice becomes one optional step, `bxrig input offer --for=CHOICE --yes`, that does nothing when nothing is found.

## Apple Magic

`bxrig input apple` checks the driver (`hid_magicmouse`), the Bluetooth service, the battery and the driver's module options: `scroll_speed`, `scroll_acceleration`, `emulate_scroll_wheel` and `emulate_3button`. It exits 4 when the kernel has no `hid_magicmouse`.

Scroll speed is a kernel module option, from 0 to 63 (default 32):

```bash
bxrig input apple --scroll-speed=48          # the plan
bxrig input apple --scroll-speed=48 --yes    # writes /etc/modprobe.d/bxrig-magicmouse.conf with sudo
```

It applies the next time the module loads: reconnect the mouse or reboot. If the driver is **built into** your kernel, modprobe options are not read; the command says so and you add `hid_magicmouse.scroll_speed=48` to the kernel command line instead. `bxrig input undo` removes the file.

**Gestures** stay with `libinput-gestures` (`bxrig input gestures --yes`, Hyprland): BxRig does not write Hyprland's own gesture configuration, because its syntax changed between versions and is not verified here. To pair a device use `bluetoothctl` (or the Bluetooth panel): `scan on`, `pair`, `trust`, `connect`.

## Logitech

`bxrig input logitech` shows the receivers (Unifying, Bolt, Lightspeed) and devices with their battery, the `hid_logitech_dj` and `hid_logitech_hidpp` drivers, whether Solaar's udev rule (`42-logitech-unify-permissions.rules`) is installed, and, when Solaar is installed, what `solaar show` lists. Firmware updates are not part of Solaar: use `fwupdmgr`.

## Advanced

Detection needs no root and no extra tool: it reads the kernel's `/sys/bus/hid/devices` (vendor `05AC` is Apple, `046D` is Logitech; bus `0005` is Bluetooth, `0003` USB), `bluetoothctl devices` for paired devices that are not connected now, and `upower` for a battery the kernel did not report.

### What is found

`input status` lists each device with its kind (`apple-mouse`, `apple-trackpad`, `apple-keyboard`, `logitech-mouse`, `logitech-keyboard`, `logitech-receiver`, `other`), how it is connected, and its battery. An Apple device counts when its name has "Magic" in it; no product ids are hard-coded. The kind is read from the name, so an unusual name can land in `other`. It also shows whether the drivers are **loaded** or **built in** (a built-in driver never shows in `lsmod`, which is why the old doctor could say "not loaded" for a working mouse).

### Not verified on real hardware

Magic Trackpad 2, Magic Mouse 2 and an MX Master have not been tested here; the commands are tested against a fake sysfs and fake tools. Whether `upower` reports these batteries is unconfirmed (the kernel's own battery is read first), and whether `hid_magicmouse` is built in on CachyOS kernels is not known.

Next: [Displays, power and time](/desktop/system/index.html), [Shortcuts](/desktop/shortcuts/index.html).

markdown:
# Move to another machine

Use this page to carry your BxRig settings, wizard answers and keys to a new machine.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig settings export my-settings.tar.gz
bxrig settings import my-settings.tar.gz --yes
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Old machine"] --> B["settings export"]
  A --> C["secrets export (encrypted)"]
  B --> D["New machine"]
  C --> D
  D --> E["settings import"]
  D --> F["secrets import"]
```

The diagram shows that settings and keys travel as two separate files.

## Move your settings

Export bundles `~/.config/bxrig` (answers, shortcuts, runner and update settings) **without secrets, backups or state** . Import backs up each existing file as `NAME.bak-STAMP` first and refuses archives with paths outside `bxrig/`.

## Move your keys

Keys travel separately and encrypted:

```bash
bxrig secrets export
bxrig secrets import
```

## Set up a new machine from answers only

To set up a new machine without touching the old one, export only the wizard answers, then use them there:

```bash
bxrig init --export answers.json
bxrig init --from answers.json                  # on the new machine
bxrig init --answers answers.json --yes         # or unattended
```

## Advanced

Your files are not part of an export. To move those, use [Backups](/data/backups/index.html): `bxrig backup export config ID --to=FILE` writes a config snapshot as one file, and `bxrig backup data restore ID --to=DIR` restores your files from a place.

Next: [Backups](/data/backups/index.html) · [AI agents and skills](/ai/agents/index.html)

# Troubleshooting

Start with `bxrig status` and the doctors; each prints a fix next to every failed check.

|             Problem              |                                                                       Run                                                                       |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Something is missing after setup | `bxrig status`, then `bxrig init`                                                                                                               |
| Installer failed                 | read `~/.cache/bxrig/install.log`; a wizard install also has its own log, `~/.local/state/bxrig/logs/init-*.log` (send it when asking for help) |
| GPU or drivers                   | `bxrig gpu doctor`                                                                                                                              |
| Magic Mouse, Trackpad, Bluetooth | `bxrig input doctor`, `bxrig input apple`                                                                                                       |
| Logitech mouse or keyboard       | `bxrig input logitech`, `bxrig input offer`                                                                                                     |
| Dolphin "Open with" is empty     | `bxrig dolphin doctor --fix`                                                                                                                    |
| App launcher or menu             | `bxrig runner doctor`                                                                                                                           |
| Containers                       | `bxrig containers doctor`                                                                                                                       |
| Shortcuts clash                  | `bxrig keys conflicts`                                                                                                                          |
| Plasma panels look wrong         | `bxrig plasma panels undo --yes`                                                                                                                |

## Exit codes

|  Code   |                         Meaning                         |
|---------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| 0       | done                                                    |
| 2       | a plan was printed (add `--yes`) or the usage was wrong |
| 4       | a precondition failed (a tool is missing, bad input)    |
| 5, 6, 7 | a step failed (7: some steps done, some failed)         |
| 9       | an internal error                                       |
| 10      | `update check`: an update is available                  |

Add `--json` to any command for machine-readable output.

markdown:
# Displays, power and time

Set up your monitors, laptop power, time zone and network basics, and fix a stuck desktop piece, each with one command.

## Try it

```bash
bxrig display list              # your screens and their names
bxrig power status              # laptop charge, profile, lid actions
bxrig time status               # the zone and clock
```

What each command family changes on your machine.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["bxrig display"] --> B["monitors.lua on Hyprland"]
  A --> C["kscreen-doctor on Plasma"]
  D["bxrig power"] --> E["profiles, lid, charge limit"]
  F["bxrig time"] --> G["zone, NTP, auto zone"]
```

## Displays

```bash
bxrig display list
bxrig display scale DP-2 1.5          # auto or 0.5 to 4
bxrig display rotate DP-2 90
bxrig display mode DP-2 2560x1440@144
bxrig display position DP-2 2880x0
bxrig display mirror on               # the laptop panel on every external monitor
bxrig display laptop off              # refused when no other monitor would be on
bxrig display brightness up           # down, or set 40
bxrig display apply                   # push what is saved again
```

The starter `hyprland.lua` that `bxrig setup hyprland` writes gives each connected screen a first scale from its resolution, so a high-density laptop panel does not start too big: it aims at the room of a 1200 pixel high screen (2880x1800 gets 1.5, 3840x2160 gets 2, 1920x1080 stays at 1) and only uses a scale that divides the resolution evenly; otherwise it leaves Hyprland's own `auto`. The file is yours after that. On a machine that already has a `hyprland.lua`, set it yourself: `bxrig display scale eDP-1 1.5 --yes` (`bxrig display list` shows the names).

On Hyprland the settings are one generated file, `~/.config/bxrig/theme/monitors.lua`, loaded after your own `hyprland.lua`, and Hyprland reloads. On Plasma they go through `kscreen-doctor`.

## Laptop power

CachyOS does not ship laptop power tools, so BxRig adds them.

```bash
bxrig power status                    # charge, state, time left, watts, health, cycles, profile, lid actions
bxrig power setup --yes               # power-profiles-daemon and upower; nothing happens on a desktop
bxrig power profile saver             # performance, balanced, saver
bxrig power lid lock --yes            # suspend, hibernate, lock or ignore when the lid closes (battery and AC)
bxrig power lid battery hibernate --yes   # only on battery
bxrig power lid ac lock --yes             # only on AC power
bxrig power hibernate --yes           # save to disk and power off (exit 4 until swap and resume are ready)
bxrig power charge-limit 80 --yes     # stop charging at 80 percent (laptops whose battery supports it)
bxrig power charge-limit off --yes    # back to a full charge
bxrig power doctor                    # daemons, the lid, zram, swap, resume and the kernel for hibernation, the charge limit
```

The lid setting is a logind drop-in and applies from the next login. Hibernation is not configured for you: `power hibernate` and `doctor` tell you what is missing (disk swap at least the size of RAM, zram does not count; `resume=` on the kernel command line, with `resume_offset=` for a swap file; a kernel without secure boot lockdown). The charge limit uses the kernel attribute `charge_control_end_threshold`, kept across reboots and suspends by a small systemd unit; many laptops (ThinkPad, ASUS, Framework and others) have it, some do not, and then the command exits 4. The charge limit and hibernation are not verified on real hardware yet.

The bar's battery widget opens a Power panel with these settings (see Quick settings and Power in the appearance guide).

## Time zone and travel

```bash
bxrig time status
bxrig time zone Europe/Madrid --yes   # set it (bxrig time zone --list shows them all)
bxrig time sync --yes                 # after you land: set the zone from your IP address
bxrig time auto on --yes              # or follow your location by itself
bxrig time ntp on --yes
```

`time auto on` installs GeoClue and `automatic-timezoned`, writes the service and the GeoClue settings it needs, and enables it. **GeoClue looks your location up online (the Wi-Fi networks around you or your IP address)** , so the plan says so before you agree. `time auto off` removes everything it wrote. If the zone does not follow you, read `journalctl -u automatic-timezoned`.

## DNS, kernels and stay awake

```bash
bxrig dns                              # the servers in use
bxrig dns cloudflare --yes             # google, quad9, custom 9.9.9.10, dhcp
bxrig dns bench                        # time each provider and see the fastest
bxrig kernel list
bxrig kernel install linux-cachyos-lts --yes
bxrig toggle stay-awake                # keep the screen from idling (Noctalia)
```

`dns` changes the active NetworkManager connections. `dns bench` asks Cloudflare, Quad9, Google, your router and your own servers (when you use some) the same five names twice with `dig` and shows the median of the second round, the one in use marked; it needs `dig` (`bind` on Arch, `bind9-dnsutils` on Debian and Ubuntu, `bind-utils` on openSUSE). `kernel` installs or removes kernel packages with their headers; it never edits the bootloader, never removes the running or the last kernel, and you pick the kernel in the boot menu. Stay awake needs Noctalia (Hyprland); on Plasma use System Settings.

## When something is stuck

```bash
bxrig system restart shell        # Noctalia (or Plasma's shell)
bxrig system restart audio        # PipeWire and WirePlumber
bxrig system restart wifi         # unblock the radio, Wi-Fi on, rescan
bxrig system restart bluetooth    # unblock the radio, adapter on
```

Each shows a plan first; add `--yes` (the menu's Update \> Restart does).

## Advanced

### Password, firmware and speed

```bash
bxrig system password             # passwd, on this terminal
bxrig system firmware             # firmware updates your vendors offer (fwupd, from LVFS)
bxrig system firmware update --yes
bxrig system speedtest network    # speedtest-cli: ping, download, upload
bxrig system speedtest disk       # write and read 1 GiB in ~/.cache
bxrig system speedtest dns        # the same as dns bench
bxrig system speedtest last       # the last result of each
```

Only the last result of each test is kept (`~/.local/state/bxrig/speedtest-last.json`), so the panels can show it when they open. On the bar, the System panel's Network tab has the Wi-Fi (with Share Wi-Fi, a QR code a phone scans), the speed and disk tests and a DNS list to pick from; the Quick panel has Share Wi-Fi and Control Center buttons at the top. The Control Center has the same on its Network page.

Firmware updates cover BIOS/UEFI, SSDs, docks and some keyboards and mice, from vendors that publish to LVFS (Dell, Lenovo, HP, Framework, Logitech and others). Many consumer laptops are not covered.

### Hardware switches

```bash
bxrig input touchpad off          # and on, toggle, status (Hyprland); also touchscreen
bxrig gpu mode                    # a laptop with two GPUs: the current mode
bxrig gpu mode integrated --yes   # the dedicated GPU off (battery); hybrid turns it back on
bxrig wifi qr                     # a QR code a phone scans to join your network
bxrig share file report.pdf       # LocalSend: a file, a folder or the clipboard to a device nearby
bxrig default editor neovim --yes # the app for text files, and EDITOR / VISUAL
```

`gpu mode` uses supergfxctl (supergfxd); log out or reboot after a switch. `share` needs LocalSend's command line, `localsend-cli` (LocalSend 1.18 and later); `bxrig share receive` opens the LocalSend app.

Next: [Appearance](/customize/appearance/index.html), [Updates](/maintain/updates/index.html).

title: Wizard pages
body: Wizard pages You will add one yes/no question to the setup wizard and make it run a command. The wizard only asks and saves answers. bxrig init turns the answers into ordinary commands. Files you touch File What for assets/wizard/pages-demo.json The built-in pages and questions (JSON). src/bxrig/InitPlan.bx Turns an answer into a step: the command to run. tests/init_plan_test.bxs Checks the step for your answer. tests/wizard_app_test.bxs , tests/wizard_view_test.bxs Wizard logic and screens, run when you change page behaviour. How an answer travels This diagram shows the path from a question to a command, and how the saved answers come back. flowchart LR A["pages-demo.json + catalog pages"] --> B["bxrig init: wizard"] B --> C["answers.json, saved"] C --> D["InitPlan: answers to steps"] D --> E["ordinary bxrig commands"] C -. "next run, or --from, --answers" .-> B The wizard itself ( bxrig wizard ) changes nothing on the machine. Saved answers live in ~/.config/bxrig/answers.json (mode 600, no secrets). Steps Add the question to the page it belongs to in assets/wizard/pages-demo.json , in that page's questions list. A yes/no question: { "type": "confirm", "id": "stay_awake", "label": "Stay awake while plugged in", "default": false, "help": "The screen and the machine stay on while on mains power. Change it later from the BxRig menu." } The id is the answer key: it must be unique across all pages. Question types: Type Answer is Extra keys choice a string options ( value , label , description , optional group ) multi an array of strings options text a string placeholder number a number min , max confirm true or false none info no answer, just text label , help Turn the answer into a step in src/bxrig/InitPlan.bx , next to the similar ones. Nothing runs that the user did not choose, so an unanswered question must add no step. Look at night_shift there for the pattern: if ( pick( a, "stay_awake", false ) ) out.steps.append( { id: "stay-awake", title: "stay awake while plugged in", argv: [ "bxrig", "toggle", "stay-awake" ], optional: true } ); argv[1] of "bxrig" means this program. optional: true means a failure is skipped instead of stopping the run. Add a test in tests/init_plan_test.bxs (it follows the power_setup check): testkit.check( "stay_awake adds its step", cmd( ip.plan( { stay_awake: true } ), "stay-awake" ) == "bxrig toggle stay-awake" ); testkit.check( "no answer, no step", ip.plan( {} ).steps.len() == 0 ); See it working scripts/dev-build.sh dist/bxrig wizard --demo --out /tmp/answers.json # your question is on its page dist/bxrig init --print-answers # includes stay_awake echo '{"stay_awake": true}' > /tmp/a.json dist/bxrig init --answers=/tmp/a.json --dry-run # the plan has your step Replay answers Command Does bxrig init --from=FILE Opens the wizard filled with the answers in FILE. bxrig init --answers=FILE --yes Runs the answers without asking ( --dry-run prints the plan). bxrig init --export=FILE Copies your saved answers to take to another machine. bxrig init --print-answers Prints the saved answers ( --from-system adds what the machine has). bxrig wizard --pages=P.json --answers=A.json --out=O.json The bare wizard with your own pages. An answer for a question this version does not ask is ignored. Test it (cd src && matchbox ../tests/init_plan_test.bxs) (cd src && matchbox ../tests/wizard_app_test.bxs) (cd src && matchbox ../tests/wizard_view_test.bxs) bash tests/wizard-test.sh dist/bxrig # end to end in a pseudo-terminal bash tests/init-test.sh dist/bxrig Common mistakes A duplicate question id : the second hides the first in the answers. A step that runs when nothing was answered. Use pick( a, "id", false ) so a missing answer does nothing. An answer that is saved but no command uses: add it to pendingKeys() in InitPlan so the user is told. Putting app choices in the JSON by hand: the Customize pages per catalog group are generated from the catalog ( AppPages ). See Add an app . Advanced Conditions Any question may carry "when": { "id": "other_question", "in": ["a", "b"] } or "equals": "a" . It is shown only while that answer matches, and a hidden question is left out of the review and the answers file. "when": { "any": [ {...}, {...} ] } lists conditions where one is enough. A question with "hidden": true is never shown, it only carries a value (what the system detected) that other when s read, like input_detected on the Input page. A whole page may carry when too: it is skipped by Next and Back and left out of the sidebar, step count, review and result. The wizard program The wizard is a full-screen terminal form written in BoxLang on MatchBox's terminal canvas. It needs a 76x24 terminal. Exit codes: 0 answers written, 130 cancelled (nothing written), 2 usage, 4 unreadable pages or answers file. Class Does WizardApp State and key handling, no drawing (unit tested). WizardView Draws a frame and records click regions. Wizard The run loop: events in, frames out. WizardCmd The bxrig wizard command. WizardData The built-in pages (a resource). Keys: Up/Down (or j/k) move, Space selects, Enter finishes the question, Left/Right change a number, Tab or PageDown next page, Esc or Shift-Tab previous, Ctrl-C cancels. Clicks select options and jump to visited steps. Record the wizard for the docs with python3 tools/record-wizard.py --bin dist/bxrig --out /tmp/rec (needs Pillow, pyte and ffmpeg). Next: Add a command , Tests .

| `tests/init_plan_test.bxs`                                | Checks the step for your answer.                              |
| `tests/wizard_app_test.bxs`, `tests/wizard_view_test.bxs` | Wizard logic and screens, run when you change page behaviour. |

## How an answer travels

This diagram shows the path from a question to a command, and how the saved answers come back.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["pages-demo.json + catalog pages"] --> B["bxrig init: wizard"]
  B --> C["answers.json, saved"]
  C --> D["InitPlan: answers to steps"]
  D --> E["ordinary bxrig commands"]
  C -. "next run, or --from, --answers" .-> B
```

The wizard itself (`bxrig wizard`) changes nothing on the machine. Saved answers live in `~/.config/bxrig/answers.json` (mode 600, no secrets).

## Steps

1. Add the question to the page it belongs to in `assets/wizard/pages-demo.json`, in that page's `questions` list. A yes/no question:

   ```json
   {
     "type": "confirm",
     "id": "stay_awake",
     "label": "Stay awake while plugged in",
     "default": false,
     "help": "The screen and the machine stay on while on mains power. Change it later from the BxRig menu."
   }
   ```

   The `id` is the answer key: it must be unique across all pages. Question types:

   |   Type    |      Answer is       |                          Extra keys                           |
   |-----------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
   | `choice`  | a string             | `options` (`value`, `label`, `description`, optional `group`) |
   | `multi`   | an array of strings  | `options`                                                     |
   | `text`    | a string             | `placeholder`                                                 |
   | `number`  | a number             | `min`, `max`                                                  |
   | `confirm` | true or false        | none                                                          |
   | `info`    | no answer, just text | `label`, `help`                                               |

2. Turn the answer into a step in `src/bxrig/InitPlan.bx`, next to the similar ones. Nothing runs that the user did not choose, so an unanswered question must add no step. Look at `night_shift` there for the pattern:

   ```boxlang
   if ( pick( a, "stay_awake", false ) ) out.steps.append( { id: "stay-awake", title: "stay awake while plugged in", argv: [ "bxrig", "toggle", "stay-awake" ], optional: true } );
   ```

   `argv[1]` of `"bxrig"` means this program. `optional: true` means a failure is skipped instead of stopping the run.
3. Add a test in `tests/init_plan_test.bxs` (it follows the `power_setup` check):

   ```boxlang
   testkit.check( "stay_awake adds its step", cmd( ip.plan( { stay_awake: true } ), "stay-awake" ) == "bxrig toggle stay-awake" );
   testkit.check( "no answer, no step", ip.plan( {} ).steps.len() == 0 );
   ```

## See it working

```bash
scripts/dev-build.sh
dist/bxrig wizard --demo --out /tmp/answers.json     # your question is on its page
dist/bxrig init --print-answers                      # includes stay_awake
echo '{"stay_awake": true}' > /tmp/a.json
dist/bxrig init --answers=/tmp/a.json --dry-run      # the plan has your step
```

## Replay answers

|                           Command                           |                                 Does                                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `bxrig init --from=FILE`                                    | Opens the wizard filled with the answers in FILE.                     |
| `bxrig init --answers=FILE --yes`                           | Runs the answers without asking (`--dry-run` prints the plan).        |
| `bxrig init --export=FILE`                                  | Copies your saved answers to take to another machine.                 |
| `bxrig init --print-answers`                                | Prints the saved answers (`--from-system` adds what the machine has). |
| `bxrig wizard --pages=P.json --answers=A.json --out=O.json` | The bare wizard with your own pages.                                  |

An answer for a question this version does not ask is ignored.

## Test it

```bash
(cd src && matchbox ../tests/init_plan_test.bxs)
(cd src && matchbox ../tests/wizard_app_test.bxs)
(cd src && matchbox ../tests/wizard_view_test.bxs)
bash tests/wizard-test.sh dist/bxrig       # end to end in a pseudo-terminal
bash tests/init-test.sh dist/bxrig
```

## Common mistakes

* A duplicate question `id`: the second hides the first in the answers.
* A step that runs when nothing was answered. Use `pick( a, "id", false )` so a missing answer does nothing.
* An answer that is saved but no command uses: add it to `pendingKeys()` in `InitPlan` so the user is told.
* Putting app choices in the JSON by hand: the Customize pages per catalog group are generated from the catalog (`AppPages`). See [Add an app](/developer/add-an-app/index.html).

## Advanced

### Conditions

Any question may carry `"when": { "id": "other_question", "in": ["a", "b"] }` or `"equals": "a"`. It is shown only while that answer matches, and a hidden question is left out of the review and the answers file. `"when": { "any": [ {...}, {...} ] }` lists conditions where one is enough. A question with `"hidden": true` is never shown, it only carries a value (what the system detected) that other `when`s read, like `input_detected` on the Input page.

A whole page may carry `when` too: it is skipped by Next and Back and left out of the sidebar, step count, review and result.

### The wizard program

The wizard is a full-screen terminal form written in BoxLang on MatchBox's terminal canvas. It needs a 76x24 terminal. Exit codes: 0 answers written, 130 cancelled (nothing written), 2 usage, 4 unreadable pages or answers file.

|    Class     |                       Does                        |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `WizardApp`  | State and key handling, no drawing (unit tested). |
| `WizardView` | Draws a frame and records click regions.          |
| `Wizard`     | The run loop: events in, frames out.              |
| `WizardCmd`  | The `bxrig wizard` command.                       |
| `WizardData` | The built-in pages (a resource).                  |

Keys: Up/Down (or j/k) move, Space selects, Enter finishes the question, Left/Right change a number, Tab or PageDown next page, Esc or Shift-Tab previous, Ctrl-C cancels. Clicks select options and jump to visited steps.

Record the wizard for the docs with `python3 tools/record-wizard.py --bin dist/bxrig --out /tmp/rec` (needs Pillow, pyte and ffmpeg).

Next: [Add a command](/developer/add-a-command/index.html), [Tests](/developer/tests/index.html).

markdown:
# Noctalia plugins

You will build a small bar widget, `bxrig/acstate`, that shows whether the machine is on mains power or battery. It runs a `bxrig` command, reads its JSON, and draws one label.
> **Note:** Noctalia v5 plugins are written in Luau (`.luau` files) with a `plugin.toml`, not QML. Every BxRig plugin lives in `templates/noctalia-plugins/NAME/`.

## Files you touch

|                           File                            |                                  What for                                   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `templates/noctalia-plugins/acstate/plugin.toml`          | Id, settings, and which widgets and panels exist.                           |
| `templates/noctalia-plugins/acstate/bar.luau`             | The bar widget.                                                             |
| `templates/noctalia-plugins/acstate/bxrig.luau`           | The shared helper that runs `bxrig`. Copy it unchanged from another plugin. |
| `templates/noctalia-plugins/acstate/translations/en.json` | The labels of the settings.                                                 |
| `src/bxrig/NoctaliaConfig.bx`                             | The `enabled = [...]` list and the bar layout lines.                        |
| `tests/dev_plugin_test.bxs`                               | A model for a plugin test.                                                  |
| `templates/noctalia-plugins/README.md`                    | Add a row to the table.                                                     |

## How a plugin gets onto the desktop

This diagram shows how a folder in the repository ends up as a widget in the bar.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["templates/noctalia-plugins/NAME"] --> B["Packed into bxrig as resources"]
  B --> C["Starter writes files to ~/.local/share/noctalia/plugins/NAME"]
  D["config.toml: plugins enabled list"] --> E["Noctalia loads bxrig/NAME"]
  C --> E
  E --> F["Bar widget runs bxrig NAME --json"]
```

`TemplateData.pluginEntries()` lists every file under `templates/noctalia-plugins/`, so a new folder is picked up with no code. The enabled list and the bar layout are written by `NoctaliaConfig.bx`.

## Steps

1. Create the folder and copy the helper. The helper runs `bxrig`, unwraps the `{"ok":true,"data":{...}}` envelope and honors the `command` setting. It must be identical in every plugin.

   ```bash
   mkdir -p templates/noctalia-plugins/acstate/translations
   cp templates/noctalia-plugins/clock/bxrig.luau templates/noctalia-plugins/acstate/
   ```

2. Write `plugin.toml`. Keep `plugin_api = 43` like the others.

   ```toml
   id = "bxrig/acstate"
   name = "Power source (BxRig)"
   version = "1.0.0"
   plugin_api = 43
   author = "bxrig"
   license = "MIT"
   dependencies = ["bxrig"]
   tags = ["power", "bxrig"]
   icon = "plug"
   description = "Shows AC or battery in the bar."

   [[setting]]
   key = "command"
   type = "string"
   label_key = "settings.command.label"
   description_key = "settings.command.description"
   default = "bxrig"

   [[widget]]
   id = "bar"
   entry = "bar.luau"
   ```

3. Write `translations/en.json`. Every `label_key` and `description_key` above needs an entry.

   ```json
   {
     "settings": {
       "command": {
         "description": "The bxrig executable (name on PATH, absolute path, or ~/ path)",
         "label": "bxrig command"
       }
     },
     "title": "Power source"
   }
   ```

4. Write `bar.luau`. `update()` runs on the interval you set, `barWidget.render` draws a ui tree.

   ```lua
   --!nonstrict
   -- Power source bar widget: "AC" or "Battery", from `bxrig power status --json` every 30 s.
   local bxrig = require("./bxrig.luau")

   local function draw(text)
   	barWidget.render(ui.label({ text = text }))
   end

   local function fetch()
   	bxrig.json({ "power", "status", "--json" }, function(data, err)
   		if err ~= nil then
   			draw("?")
   			barWidget.setTooltip(err)
   			return
   		end
   		draw(data.on_ac == true and "AC" or "Battery")
   	end)
   end

   function update()
   	fetch()
   end

   noctalia.setUpdateInterval(30000)
   fetch()
   ```

   Draw with palette roles only (`primary`, `on_surface_variant`, `error`, `surface_container`...), never hard-coded colors, so the widget follows the active theme. Do not use the em dash or en dash in plugin files: the plugin tests check for it.
5. For a click, add `function onClick() noctalia.togglePanel("bxrig/acstate:panel") end` and a `[[panel]]` block with an `entry = "panel.luau"` in `plugin.toml`. The clock plugin (`templates/noctalia-plugins/clock/`) is the smallest complete example of a bar widget plus panel.

6. Enable it in BxRig. In `src/bxrig/NoctaliaConfig.bx` add `bxrig/acstate` to the `enabled = [...]` line, add a `[widget.bxrig-acstate]` block with `type = "bxrig/acstate:bar"`, and put `bxrig-acstate` in a bar section. Update the matching list in `tests/noctalia-config-test.sh`.

## See it working

Copy the plugin by hand and enable it, without rebuilding:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/noctalia/plugins
rm -rf ~/.local/share/noctalia/plugins/acstate
cp -r templates/noctalia-plugins/acstate ~/.local/share/noctalia/plugins/acstate
noctalia msg plugins enable bxrig/acstate
noctalia msg plugins list | grep bxrig
```

Noctalia hot-reloads edited `.luau` files. After replacing a whole folder, disable and enable the plugin again. Panels open from a key with `noctalia msg panel-toggle bxrig/NAME:panel`.

To see the real thing, rebuild and run the starter: `scripts/dev-build.sh`, then `dist/bxrig setup hyprland --dry-run`.

## Test it

Model a test on `tests/dev_plugin_test.bxs`: every file is there, `plugin.toml` has the right id and `plugin_api = 43`, the shared `bxrig.luau` equals the one in another plugin, the translations are valid JSON, every `require` names a file of the plugin, and the starter installs the files.

```bash
cd src && matchbox ../tests/dev_plugin_test.bxs
tests/noctalia-config-test.sh dist/bxrig
```

`noctalia config validate` warns about unknown `bxrig/...` widget types when no plugin is loaded. That is expected, it still reports the config as valid.

## Common mistakes

* A `label_key` with no entry in `translations/en.json`: the settings show raw keys.
* A copy of `bxrig.luau` that drifted from the others: the tests compare them.
* Plugin enabled in `config.toml` but not installed, or the reverse. Installed does not mean active.
* Hard-coded colors: the widget looks wrong in other themes.
* Running a bxrig command without `--json` in a data call: the helper expects the envelope.

## Advanced

* Plugin-level settings are read with `noctalia.getConfig("key")`, and set under `[plugin_settings."bxrig/NAME"]` in `config.toml`.
* Pin the executable with `command = "~/.local/bin/bxrig"` when Noctalia starts without `~/.local/bin` on its PATH.
* Panels declare `width`, `height`, `placement` and `position` in `plugin.toml`. Use `panel.render`, `onOpen` and `update` for live data, and keep polling to while the panel is open.
* Secrets never go on a command line: copy through `noctalia.copyToClipboard`.
* The JSON contract of each BxRig command a plugin reads is in `templates/noctalia-plugins/README.md`.
* Next: [Add a command](/developer/add-a-command/index.html), [Tests](/developer/tests/index.html).
